7a99e6357dc9817e: Landscape as a package. Landscape should be designed and budgeted from the start, not left as a provisional sum for the end.

1854ab203160151c: Indoor-outdoor detailing. Level thresholds, large sliding glass and covered terraces are beautiful and unforgiving if detailed poorly. Water and heat get in through the junctions.
e10fc1c311b6258d: Several of the houses in our UK portfolio were built into wooded and landscaped sites, with green roofs, timber decks and structures designed to disappear into their setting. f8a2fa791fea03bd: Arabian Ranches villas: renovations and upgrades
fa628852e681d02e: A large Emaar golf and family villa community from the mid-2000s, now in its renovation years. The house can change a great deal inside; the outside largely cannot.
d1c732c47c23c253: This page sets out what is particular to Arabian Ranches. It is one example of where we work, not a limit: we cover every community in Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
6472e17adfd69a66: Arabian Ranches is an Emaar community, managed by Emaar Community Management and laid out as a series of sub-communities around a golf course, among them Alvorada, Mirador, Palmera, Saheel and Savannah (Emaar Community Management). Its villas and townhouses were released in phases from the mid-2000s. Gulf News reported in 2006, for example, that Emaar first released the Alvorada villas in May 2005, in six types from 3,566 to 4,844 sq ft with three to five bedrooms (Gulf News, 2006).
585a3a88d88ef41f: Two features shape any project here. The houses were built to a set of standard types, so most owners are working within a known plan and a known structure, which makes early scoping easier than on a one-off house. And the community's look is protected: Emaar's rules are written to keep the street scene consistent, so the scope of work is defined as much by what the guidelines allow as by what the owner wants.
63e8445f76abf5d7: What owners here are usually doing
1e3fdeb25ca519c9: Kitchens, bathrooms and the ground floor. Opening up the original layout, new kitchens and wet rooms, new floors and joinery. This is the most common project, and the one most prone to creeping scope.
eb3e719838c1d564: Services and comfort. Replacing original air conditioning, upgrading electrics and lighting controls, and improving the glazing and roofs.
819d43f9a026b5b7: Gardens and outdoor living. Pools, pergolas, outdoor kitchens and landscaping. These are external works and need Emaar's approval before they start.
f44b200b087a668f: Full refurbishment before a sale or a long stay. Everything at once, which is when a properly sequenced programme and a fixed scope pay for themselves.
e8201c2eb5bf9a45: Typical villa stock, and what to investigate
4e878cf03483fcde: The stock is a set of standard villa and townhouse types repeated across the sub-communities. The Alvorada release is typical: six types of three to five bedrooms, from 3,566 to 4,844 sq ft. Many of the earliest houses are now around twenty years old, and owners have changed them to different degrees since. None of the points below is a diagnosis of any house; they are the things worth checking before a contractor's price is agreed.
1d378bff6b9653e4: What earlier owners changed. Covered terraces, garden rooms and converted garages may or may not have an Emaar NOC. If you are buying, ask the seller for the NOC and drawings for each change; if you own the villa, establish its status before design starts.
ba796768708c5c17: Air conditioning and controls. Original systems may be near the end of their working life, and a more open ground floor changes the cooling the house needs. Survey them before the budget assumes they can be kept.
0e315fa77fb05793: Roofs and wet areas. Waterproofing on flat roofs, terraces, balconies and showers, opened up and tested where the new design builds over or around them.
d3e24aff9adc0b62: Plumbing and electrics. Pipework, distribution boards and capacity for what you are adding: a pool, an outdoor kitchen, a car charger, more cooling.
7ab15c2662cb7db6: Garden structures. Pergolas, boundary walls and paving laid by earlier owners, and the drainage under them.
20b6371fd78bf50a: In most communities we would price a rebuild alongside a deep renovation. In Arabian Ranches the guidelines narrow that choice: Emaar's guidance is that external modifications that change the look of the villas are not permitted, so a new house of a different design is unlikely to be accepted, and rebuilding the same house rarely makes sense. Put any idea of demolition to Emaar before spending on it. The practical decision is how deep to go inside the existing shell, and that rests on a condition survey: if the services, waterproofing and wet areas all need replacing, plan the work as one properly sequenced project rather than a series of small ones. Our renovate-or-rebuild guide explains how to make that judgement on the numbers.
5d65e92e88b1d208: The approval route: Emaar's home modification NOC
5cb1f60f62822290: Emaar Community Management's guidance for Arabian Ranches is that any alteration to the villa has to be approved by Emaar, applied for as a home modification NOC through the community portal. External modifications that change the look of the villas are not permitted, while interior painting and regular maintenance do not need an NOC, although the contractor still needs an entry permit to the community (Emaar Community Management, Arabian Ranches FAQs). Read the current Home Modification Guidelines for your sub-community before design starts: they decide whether a pergola, a pool or a change to a terrace is possible, and on what terms.
5af1cc8dfdf27ca3: After Emaar's NOC, structural work and other significant changes need a building permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits. Your registered consultant or licensed contractor prepares and makes those applications. We review them with you, track them, and make sure the contractor's start date waits for approvals in hand.
0ac740c72c74ac69: How much does it cost, and how long does it take?
38f0a41583dcd0de: Property Finder's September 2025 guide to villa renovation in Dubai gives AED 600,000 to 850,000 and 90 to 120 days of works for the interior and landscaping of a four-bedroom independent villa, naming the Ranches as one of its examples. For a three-bedroom townhouse with interior, kitchen and bathroom work it gives AED 250,000 to 400,000 and 60 to 90 days (Property Finder, 2025). Those are contractor prices and works durations. Design, the Emaar NOC, any authority permit, contingency and the cost of living elsewhere come on top.
51b1ba15ab8ef16d: For your own figure, our villa build and renovation cost calculator gives indicative low, likely and high ranges with every source listed, and our villa renovation cost guide explains how to budget for an older villa. We do not publish a separate rate per square foot for Arabian Ranches, because no published source supports a premium or discount by community.
0ead91c59d48f947: Where Arabian Ranches renovations go wrong
afdfa11edf191c57: Scope creep. A kitchen becomes the ground floor, which becomes the whole house. Decide the scope and the budget together, before quotes, and record every later change with its cost and time.
a314ea1113ab4dc2: Quotes that are not comparable. One contractor includes the air conditioning, another assumes it can be reused, a third leaves it as a provisional sum. In our years as the builder, a low price built on assumptions was usually recovered later in variations. Our guide to choosing a villa contractor explains how to compare them like-for-like.
a13d2e135d343e1e: Outdoor works treated as an afterthought. Pools and pergolas need their own approval, their own drawings and their own place in the programme.
1e5b958a229b4624: Living in during the works. Staying in the house saves rent but costs time, and contractors price the disruption. Weigh both before you decide.
0b4344a8b4764cd8: Our article on villa renovation mistakes in Dubai covers these and others from the builder's side.

94ab4cee7b974a10: This page sets out what is particular to Dubai Hills Estate. It is one example of where we work, not a limit: we cover every community in Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
77fc286420e88d8d: What makes Dubai Hills Estate different
729eca46bc82cbe3: Dubai Hills Estate is a joint venture between Emaar Properties and Meraas, announced in June 2013 as the first phase of Mohammed Bin Rashid City: more than 11 million square metres around an 18-hole championship golf course (Khaleej Times, 2013). In 2016 Emaar described a total green area of over 2.2 million square metres, including the golf course and a central park, and said investors could buy land plots and design villas of their choice, setting the community alongside its earlier Emirates Hills (Emaar press release, March 2016).
a10174fdaa86140f: What sets it apart is that very different projects sit side by side in one community. The same 2016 release described the first golf villas in the Fairways and Parkways communities as shell-and-core, for owners to complete to their own design, alongside developer-built townhouses and villas such as Maple, and later Sidra, which Emaar released with three to five bedrooms from 3,102 to 4,283 sq ft (Invest-Gate, December 2016). So one owner here is designing a house from an empty plot, a second is finishing a shell, and a third is renovating a family villa that is barely ten years old. Each starts from a different point, with different paperwork and different risks.
cfc17496bd386e0f: The community is also young compared with the Palm or Jumeirah Islands. Most of its villas are still in their first decade, which changes the questions: less about twenty-year-old services, more about what the developer handed over, what a previous owner has already changed, and how far the house can now be taken.
554b5ee27c1e3869: Plot, shell or finished villa: new build versus renovation
2f644b7e3a49469e: Building on a plot. A full design and approval cycle, then a build of a year or more. Engel & Völkers says most villas take 12 to 24 months from approval to completion, and puts luxury construction at AED 900 to 1,400 per sq ft before land, design, approvals and interiors (Engel & Völkers, December 2025). The freedom is greatest and so is the owner's exposure, so the brief and budget need fixing before design goes far. Our guide to how to build a villa in Dubai sets out the stages.
7e5c13d1964c28f4: Completing a shell-and-core villa. The structure and envelope are in place; the owner commissions the fit-out. "Shell and core" means different things on different contracts, so the first job is to establish exactly what was delivered, what was tested and which warranties came with it. The joint between the developer's work and your fit-out contractor's is where responsibility for a defect can be hardest to pin down.
d17138789e774f03: Renovating a developer villa. The most common project here. Property Finder's September 2025 guide gives AED 250,000 to 400,000 and 60 to 90 days of works for a three-bedroom townhouse, naming Maple as an example, and AED 900,000 to 1,400,000 and 120 to 150 days for a five-bedroom villa, naming Sidra (Property Finder, 2025). Those are contractor prices and works durations; design, approvals, contingency and any rent while you are out of the house come on top.
9c8ed53fd5e1c376: On a villa this young, demolishing and rebuilding is rarely the question. The real decision is how far to change the house you have, and whether a larger or different house is better bought than built. Our renovate-or-rebuild tool and villa build and renovation cost calculator give a sourced first range for each route.
eef3c2f19fe0ff87: Dubai Hills Estate is an Emaar community developed with Meraas, and the master developer's consent comes before any authority permit. For alterations to existing homes in Emaar communities, owners apply for a home modification NOC through Emaar Community Management's online portal, and appointed contractors register and apply for community entry permits separately (Emaar Community Management). Guidelines differ between sub-communities, and a private plot build is reviewed against design guidelines for the plot rather than treated as a home modification, so ask Emaar which route and which guidelines apply to your property before design starts.
5b838063e1d4a6e9: With the developer's consent in hand, your registered consultant applies for the building permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits, through Dubai's unified permit window. Your appointed consultant or licensed contractor prepares and submits the applications. We review them with you, track them, and keep the contractor's start date tied to approvals in hand. Our guide to which Dubai authority covers your villa explains why the authority is set plot by plot.
5eee056729da7497: Most homes here are developer-built townhouses and villas in clusters of repeated types, with golf-front villas and private plots at the top of the range. Because neighbouring houses share a design, the developer's guidelines are written to keep the street consistent, and the scope of a project is often decided as much by what is allowed outside as by what the owner wants inside. None of the points below is a diagnosis of any house; they are the things worth checking before a price is agreed.
c9a7b93df2716c44: What has already been changed. If you are buying a villa that a previous owner has extended or remodelled, ask for the NOC and drawings for each change. Unapproved work becomes the new owner's problem.
b940ef0caaefed31: Cooling and electrical capacity. An enclosed terrace, a new room or a pool adds load. Check that the air conditioning and electrical supply can take it before the design assumes they can.
011354c7a10ff7b6: Roofs, terraces and wet rooms. Even on a young villa, test the waterproofing where you plan to build over it or open it up, and record the result.
acef8cc87a96a493: Handover records. As-built drawings, warranties and the defects history tell you what you are working with. If they are missing, ask the developer or seller for them early.
4640ab6ac93b710a: The garden. Pools, pergolas, outdoor kitchens and landscaping are external works and need the developer's consent. Optimal Engineering Consultants' 2026 guide puts a basic fibreglass pool at AED 80,000 to 120,000 and a standard concrete villa pool at AED 150,000 to 250,000 (Optimal, 2026). Give outdoor works their own drawings, approval and place in the programme.
363b674ae7004676: Where Dubai Hills projects go wrong
77d6e7d921c9d8b0: Scope creep. A kitchen becomes the ground floor, which becomes the whole house. Decide scope and budget together, and record every later change with its cost and time.
1b4dc447e8cbc26d: Quotes that are not comparable. One contractor allows for new air conditioning, another assumes the old system stays. On the contractor's side, we learned that a low price built on assumptions is usually recovered later in variations. Our guide to choosing a villa contractor shows how to compare quotes like-for-like.
6be4467ad41904c8: Designing before the guidelines are read. A garden room or roof terrace drawn in detail and then refused is wasted fees and months.
2fae4fb0053c50c3: Treating a plot like a renovation. A house on an empty plot needs a full design team, a ground investigation and a programme measured in years, not months.
e55c501bcb67d117: Our article on villa renovation mistakes in Dubai covers these from the builder's side.

5907ff59eeccebf8: New plot releases are selling quickly. The decisions that decide whether a plot is a good purchase are rarely the ones in the brochure.
2bb1ba9e960329b1: This page sets out what is particular to Dubai Islands. It is one example of where we work, not a limit: we cover every community in Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
44c462b6da1881e0: Dubai Islands, formerly Deira Islands, is a Nakheel master plan of five islands covering 17 square kilometres off Dubai's northern coastline, with more than 20 kilometres of beaches and about two square kilometres of parks and open space (Nakheel, August 2022). Here, villa plots are being created on new islands rather than released inside an established community.
046743240c4215e7: That makes it the opposite of the Palm or Jumeirah Islands. There is no twenty-year-old house to survey and no approval history to unpick. Instead, almost everything an owner relies on is still in the future: the roads and utilities that will reach the plot, the neighbours who will build on either side, and in some cases the final version of the rules the house must meet. There are also few completed private villas here yet to benchmark against, so evidence on actual build costs and timelines is thin. The questions that decide whether a plot is a good purchase are rarely the ones in the brochure.
37063abea7fae605: Not every buyer here is building their own house. Nakheel's first villa sales on Dubai Islands, reported by Gulf News in February 2024, were off-plan townhouses and waterfront villas, with 20% of the price due on handover (Gulf News, 2024). That launch, Bay Villas on Dubai Islands B, comprised waterfront villas, garden villas, semi-detached residences and townhouses (Nakheel, February 2024), and in August 2025 Nakheel awarded an AED 2.6 billion contract to build its 636 homes (Dubai Media Office, 2025). For owners of developer-built homes, the handover inspection and the first year in the house matter more than design guidelines, and any later alterations go through Nakheel's NOC process before an authority permit. Our villa snagging checklist shows what to check at handover.
76fa43c8a082fbe7: Private plots are the other half of the market. In October 2026 Nakheel launched Bay Estate, a gated waterfront community of about 360 three- and four-bedroom homes alongside a selection of beachfront and waterfront plots, in a master plan of 653,709 square metres with 2.4 kilometres of beachfront and 6.5 kilometres of waterfront (TradeArabia, October 2026). A plot buyer appoints their own designer, registered consultant and contractor, and carries every design, cost and programme decision that a developer would otherwise make.
c4a2312396bde80a: New build versus buying a developer home
784bc57ec3b88962: A finished developer villa gives you a known house and a handover date in your contract. A plot gives you the house you want, at the price of time and risk. Engel & Völkers says most villas take 12 to 24 months from approval to completion and puts luxury construction at AED 900 to 1,400 per sq ft, before land, design, approvals and interiors (Engel & Völkers, December 2025). Optimal Engineering Consultants puts permit issuance for straightforward villa projects at four to eight weeks from complete drawings, with construction typically 12 to 18 months (Optimal, 2026). Design and the developer's review come before any of that.
3bc49c988c6794ca: The comparison only works with every cost on the table: plot, registration, design, approvals, construction, a basement if you want one, pool and landscaping, interiors, contingency and VAT. Our villa build cost calculator gives a sourced first range for the house, and our guide to checks before buying a villa plot covers the rest.
89400ec67d9ff9e7: Dubai Islands is a Nakheel community, so the master developer comes first. On a plot, the house is designed to the development controls for that plot (coverage, height, setbacks and materials) and reviewed by Nakheel before your registered consultant applies for the building permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits. Allow for at least one round of Nakheel comments in the programme. For later changes to a completed home, Nakheel's guidance is that an NOC from its Urban Planning team is needed before any alteration, and before a contractor starts it requires a security deposit, a Site Access Permit and a PVC site fence (Nakheel customer FAQs). Our guide to the Nakheel NOC sets out that sequence. Your appointed consultant or licensed contractor prepares and submits each application; we track them and keep the programme realistic.
6a8540549026e699: What to investigate on a new island plot
cc838b5a795bc895: A new plot has no history, but it does have risks. None of the points below is a finding about any plot; they are questions to answer before you commit.
3bc3ac1a4ec109eb: The ground. These islands are reclaimed land by the sea. A ground investigation tells your engineers what the foundations and any basement must deal with, including groundwater, and a basement brings dewatering and waterproofing costs of its own.
4cf09ac277e9ad0a: Salt, wind and sun. Coastal plots need façade, metalwork and glazing specified for the exposure from the start, not upgraded later.
d2a4ce355e50d490: Services and access. When roads, water, power and drainage will reach your plot, and on what terms. A house finished before its connections is a house you cannot live in.
36695d7f7421c038: The rules in force. Whether the development controls you were given are final or draft, and what happens if they change.
e7b2303893f18f13: Neighbours. On a new island most neighbouring plots will be under construction before, during and after yours, which affects access, deliveries and protection of your finished work.
c24ba053c4122faf: Design guidelines. Coverage, height, setbacks and material rules decide the house you can actually build.
4584887a81ba26d4: Build-by deadlines. Check the sale terms for any obligation to start or complete construction, and what happens if you don't. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer.
0aa4470f47d95674: Total cost. Plot price plus design, approvals, construction, interiors and landscaping. Our plot review sets this out before you commit.
65c145f86fd9248d: Infrastructure timing. Roads, utilities and neighbouring construction will affect your programme.
ca426a471158f506: To see how these questions play out on one plot, read our Island E worked project example. It is a hypothetical illustration of our method, with assumed figures and invented events, not a completed project.

b5479236f876f89f: We review plots before purchase, then represent owners from the brief to the end of the defects period, alongside the registered consultant and contractor you appoint. On a new island, a realistic programme that matches infrastructure delivery is as important as the design itself. For owners of developer-built homes, we cover handover as one stage of a wider appointment, for example alongside upgrade work.

4991195fc7f0b117: Large plots, long sightlines over the golf course and some of the most ambitious private houses in the city. The scale is what makes control difficult.
21caec8890bf37e8: Emirates Hills was laid out by Emaar as a community of private plots around the Montgomerie golf course and its lakes, sold to owners to build the house they wanted. That makes it unlike most Dubai villa communities. There is no single standard villa type to work from; the streets mix original houses, remodelled houses and new mansions on cleared plots; and Emaar has continued to bring land to market here, with AGBI reporting a release of plots in 2022.
4277aeddcdf297c4: The plots are large, and so are the projects: deep basements, several wings, staff accommodation, pools and landscaped grounds facing the fairways or the water. Many owners appoint architects and interior designers from overseas, and specify stone, glass, joinery and lighting from several countries. Scale is what makes control difficult. A house of this size has more specialists, more long-lead items, more interfaces between architecture, structure, services and interiors, and more decisions waiting on the owner.
cd082d425699fa27: On the contractor's side, the largest houses we built were rarely lost on one big mistake. They were lost on hundreds of small, late decisions, each one priced as a variation and each one moving the programme a few days. The owner who controls the cost of an Emirates Hills house is usually the one who made decisions early and kept a record of them.
6e7c26b056ba81fe: Owners here face one of three projects, and the right choice depends on the house you have and the house you want.
a743d842dcacfc02: Building on a cleared plot. A full design and approval cycle, then a long build. The freedom is greatest and so is the owner's exposure: every specification decision is yours, and the design must be developed far enough to price properly before you sign a building contract. Under the UAE Civil Code (Federal Decree-Law No. 25 of 2025, in force from 1 June 2026), the contractor and the designing engineer are jointly liable for structural defects for ten years from delivery, and that liability cannot be excluded by contract. It is still worth knowing exactly who designed what before you sign.
d85ef67275d14d38: Remodelling an original house. You inherit a structure, services and an approval history. A condition survey with opening-up comes first; services that look serviceable need testing before you rely on them, and a remodel that moves walls, openings and floor levels can approach the cost of new structure without its freedom.
03047df236ac5b3a: Demolish and rebuild. Where the original house no longer fits the brief, a rebuild often gives a better result for a similar outlay once the remodel's true scope is priced. It adds demolition, a full approval cycle and time, so the comparison has to include the programme and the cost of living elsewhere.
acb9c249a28cbffc: At this level, published guides put luxury construction at AED 900 to 1,400 per sq ft (Engel & Völkers, December 2025), and Knight Frank put high-end villas at about AED 11,000 per square metre in Q2 2025, roughly AED 1,020 per sq ft. Those figures exclude land, design fees, interiors and landscaping, and the most ambitious houses here sit above any published band. Our villa build cost calculator gives a sourced first range, and our construction cost guide explains what the bands include and what they leave out.
b50572b5f7c726ac: Emirates Hills is an Emaar community, and Emaar's consent comes first. Emaar's Emirates Living community guidelines apply across Emirates Living, which includes Emirates Hills alongside the Springs, the Meadows and the Lakes. Gulf News reported Emaar's position that all home improvements need the consent of the community manager, that owners must submit plans and specifications before building, altering or improving a villa, and that significant improvements also need the authority's approval. Today owners apply for a home modification NOC through Emaar Community Management's online portal, and appointed contractors register and apply for community entry permits separately.
dc29b69052ff1f72: Emaar says its home modification guidelines exist to control the appearance of the community and preserve its design and architectural quality. In practice, the questions arise at the edges of the house: external appearance and materials, boundary walls, pergolas and shade structures, pools and landscaping. Gulf News reported, for example, that pergolas and exterior shades in Emirates Living must match the approved design. With Emaar's NOC in hand, your registered consultant applies for the building permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits.
2e7a157790b3deda: For a new house, Emaar's design review is a substantial stage, not a formality. Ask Emaar Community Management for the current guidelines for your plot before design starts; guidelines change, and summaries that circulate online may be out of date. Your consultant prepares and submits each stage. We track the comments, keep the decision log and make sure the programme allows for at least one round of revisions on a house of this size.
acf2f57d76f7dbfd: What matters most on a project this size
082ad2668ebea664: A fixed brief. On large houses, late changes multiply. A wing redesigned after structure is in place is an expensive decision, in money and in months.
0f9e7f2244264525: Interior integration. Joinery, lighting, automation, art and furniture are a large share of the total on houses like these. They need designing alongside the architecture, not after it, or the structure and services will be in the wrong place.
68f610e1423d8ed7: Procurement strategy. Whether to split shell-and-core from fit-out, and how to package specialist work, changes both cost and risk. Each package boundary is a place where scope can fall between two contracts.
59c671e539ea8327: Long-lead items. Stone, large-format glazing, lifts and bespoke joinery can take many months to make and ship. Late ordering is one of the most common causes of delay on large houses.
7bdc95a8b142601d: Cost visibility. With many specialists and long lead items, a monthly forecast final cost, built from what has been paid and what is still to be spent, is the clearest way to know where you really are.
27ea30a6984c9a6d: Building next to neighbours, and being the neighbour
130c6dce687097b9: Because Emirates Hills is built out plot by plot, there is often construction on one side of a house while a family lives on the other. Expect community rules on working hours, deliveries, site fencing and protection of the roads and verges, and price them into the contract rather than discovering them on site. If your plot backs on to the course or a lake, protecting that edge during construction is part of the job.

76a9c7b178b89da7: We represent you from the brief through to the end of the defects period: setting a budget that includes everything, coordinating the design and approvals programme with your consultant, helping you compare bids like-for-like and choose the right builders, and keeping cost, time and quality in front of you every month. 0f60a119957b3a73: New residential plots in Abu Dhabi
ca85672bc1fdb361: Modon launched its first residential plots community on Hudayriyat Island with more than 1,700 plots for four to six-bedroom villas, according to industry reporting. 079aa3cce3e1cb58: What that means for your project
e77a5ce51245a535: Book the team early. Good consultants and contractors fill up quickly when a community builds out at once.
b4dfafa374df07ce: Design to the guidelines. Modon's design guidelines come first, then the municipal permit through TAMM.

3a934dc8c7fdacce: Developer villas: handover and the first year
33a58a0c86a55183: Alongside the plots, Modon is delivering its own villa communities on the island. Gulf News reported in March 2024 that Modon had launched Nawayef, with 19 villa types from 350 to 2,700 square metres, and Al Naseem, a low-density cluster of villas from 490 to 620 square metres. When many villas are handed over in the same months, the developer's and contractor's aftercare teams are stretched, and defects reported late or informally tend to wait. Agree the handover inspection date in writing, attend it with the specification and the sale and purchase agreement in hand, and do not treat the keys as the end of the contract. Record meter readings and the condition of every room on the day, then log defects in writing as they appear through the defects period your contract sets: leaks after the first rain, air conditioning that cannot hold temperature in August, and cracking as the structure settles. Keep the developer's acknowledgements, because the end of the defects period is a deadline for you as much as for them. For structural defects beyond that period, the UAE Civil Code (Federal Decree-Law No. 25 of 2025) sets ten-year liability on the contractor and designing engineer; take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on how it applies to a purchase from a developer. We cover handover as one stage of a wider appointment, not as a one-visit report.

3006fbdc2bb897ac: Jumeirah Bay Island: ultra-prime, plot by plot
e4012efd2e5d7b2d: A small island of private plots and some of the highest land values in Dubai. When the plot costs this much, the house has to be delivered exactly as intended.
77e2da4ac508eae9: Jumeirah Bay Island, off the Jumeirah coastline, is a Meraas community of private villa plots. Owners here tend to commission internationally known architects and interior designers, specify materials from around the world and expect a level of finish comparable to the best private houses anywhere. The challenge is less about getting a house built than about getting this house built, without compromise creeping in under programme or cost pressure.
2daaa0130ebd7847: Island logistics. Restricted access, limited laydown space and strict community rules affect cost and programme. They need to be priced, not discovered.
a7751923d4487895: International design teams. Architects and designers based overseas need a local registered consultant of record and close coordination. Gaps between the two are where cost and time are lost.
c0690ef7a6cdddc3: Long-lead materials. Stone, glazing and bespoke joinery from overseas can take many months. Late ordering is a common cause of delay.
db9f4b6d1e915c90: Waterfront exposure. Coastal plots demand careful waterproofing, corrosion protection and façade detailing.
cb52a503ff5c5f50: We represent you between the international design team, the local consultant of record and the contractor, keeping a single programme, a single budget and a single decision log. We have spent two decades delivering waterside houses with demanding architects and complex finishes, and we bring that discipline to your project.

f4930011b3cef698: Meraas, part of Dubai Holding. Designs are reviewed against the community guidelines before the authority permit.
a4d25a06f8009675: Can I use an overseas architect for my Jumeirah Bay villa?
10f08588e22cd543: Yes, many owners do. You will also need a locally registered consultant to act as consultant of record for submissions and statutory duties. Coordinating the two well is critical.
b5eb8d1a1b3cfa80: Your consultant is responsible for the design and its statutory duties. Your contractor is responsible for building it. We represent you, from the plot to the day you move in.

04d5c6a77de579b7: Jumeirah Islands villas: renovations and extensions
a28385bf1722510b: Lakeside villas built in clusters on 46 man-made islands, now about twenty years old. Most serious work here is the renewal of an existing house, and it starts with Nakheel.
8eca0448d5fddc0d: This page sets out what is particular to Jumeirah Islands. It is one example of where we work, not a limit: we cover every community in Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
0abc1d71992d8499: Jumeirah Islands is a Nakheel community, which Nakheel describes as a collection of 46 islands set around scenic lakes, with homes that have large private gardens, verandas and roof terraces (Nakheel). When Nakheel announced in 2004 that the community had sold out, it described 736 four- and five-bedroom villas across 46 clusters, sixteen individually styled villas to a cluster, each with a private pool and garden, in four architectural themes: Oasis, Islamic, European and Mediterranean (Nakheel announcement, September 2004).
da241a1a1531d0cc: Three things follow from that history. The villas are of the same generation, so many roofs, waterproofing systems and services are of a similar age. That makes their condition a risk to investigate on every house, not a diagnosis: some will have been renewed or well maintained, others will not. The cluster themes mean the outside of each house is part of a set, which is why the master developer takes a close interest in façades, roofs and extensions. And the plots sit around lakes and landscaped edges, so access for materials, skips and plant is tighter than the size of the houses suggests.
76f7f9b9486993cd: A full interior renewal. New kitchens, bathrooms, floors, joinery and lighting, often with walls moved to open up the ground floor to the garden and the water.
318dd0766264e200: Services replacement. Air conditioning, plumbing, electrics and controls installed when the villas were built. When the ceilings come down for a new layout, it is the moment to test whether the old systems are worth reconnecting.
f195decea063b98e: Roofs, terraces and wet areas. Waterproofing on flat roofs, roof terraces, balconies and showers that may be original. This is where expensive surprises often sit, so test it before the price is agreed.
c0c52f3450dd237a: Extensions and outdoor works. Added rooms, enclosed terraces, pergolas, pool and garden remodels. These need Nakheel's agreement first and, depending on the scope, an authority permit.
7340d189b4d7049b: The original stock is a single generation of four- and five-bedroom villas, sixteen individually styled houses to a cluster in the four themes, each with its own pool and garden. Nakheel was awarding villa construction contracts for the clusters in 2004 (June 2004 report), so most houses are now around twenty years old. Age alone tells you nothing certain about a particular villa. It does tell you where to look before a price is agreed:
e41159a4ef8f0801: The approval history. Compare the house as it stands with the approved drawings. Enclosed terraces, roof rooms and garden buildings added by earlier owners may or may not have Nakheel's NOC. As the 2018 Gulf News report below shows, the cost can fall on whoever owns the villa when it comes to light.
0d3a1fd3385b2f40: Roofs and terraces. Flat roofs and roof terraces where the membrane may be original. Flood-test before you build over them.
21594acc51b3134e: The pool. Shell, tiling, pipework and plant of the same age as the house. A leak found after the new terrace is laid is an expensive one.
87e447058eac1f62: Services behind the ceilings. Air conditioning, wiring, distribution boards and plumbing. A condition survey tells you whether they can be kept, adapted or must be replaced, and that answer moves the budget more than any finish.
2aee90342a2f7cf1: Garden levels and drainage. On a lake plot, where water goes in a storm matters to the house and to the lake edge.
68757a85d5d45539: Most Jumeirah Islands owners renovate, and many want to extend. A full rebuild is a different proposition here: each villa belongs to a themed cluster of sixteen, so any new house has to satisfy Nakheel on how it sits within that set, and a design that departs from the theme may not be accepted. If the brief needs new structure, a new envelope and new services, price a rebuild alongside the renovation all the same, but put the principle to Nakheel before paying for a design. The comparison has to include demolition, the longer approval cycle, the cost of living elsewhere and the build programme. Our renovate-or-rebuild tool and guide to renovating or rebuilding a Dubai villa set out how to compare the two honestly.
5b06f79c1e229deb: Nakheel's own guidance is that owners may make changes as long as they do not affect the external façade and structure of the property, and that an NOC must be obtained from its Urban Planning team before any alterations, requested through Nakheel Online Services or the My Nakheel app (Nakheel customer FAQs). Anything touching the façade, structure or footprint needs Nakheel to confirm it is permitted at all before design work goes far. After the NOC, building work beyond the minor needs a permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits. Your registered consultant or licensed contractor prepares and makes those applications. We review the submissions with you, track them and keep the programme honest about how long they take.
00a1b0bd38a8cb7e: Nakheel also sets conditions before a contractor can start: a security deposit, a Site Access Permit, a PVC site fence, and workforce access permits, which it charges at AED 52.50 per person for construction, modification and extension work (Nakheel). None of this is large, but each item takes time, and a contractor who has not allowed for it will be standing at the gate.
ae5e0b3351f49bc3: Building first and asking later is expensive here. In 2018 Gulf News reported Jumeirah Islands owners being charged for added floor area, about AED 300 per square foot by their account, and an owner penalised when unapproved work came to light on sale; Nakheel said applications are assessed case by case and that various costs apply (Gulf News, 2018). Treat those as reported figures from 2018 and get current charges from Nakheel in writing before you fix the design. Our guide to the Nakheel NOC sets out the process in more detail.
0076ad00a866f05a: Property Finder's September 2025 guide to villa renovation in Dubai gives AED 900,000 to 1,400,000 and 120 to 150 days of works for a full upgrade of a five-bedroom older villa, naming Jumeirah Islands as one of its examples. For a luxury villa with structural work and premium materials it gives AED 1.5 million to 3.5 million or more, and 150 to 210 days (Property Finder, 2025). Those are contractor prices and works durations. Design, the Nakheel NOC, any authority permit, contingency and the cost of living elsewhere sit on top, before and alongside the works.
1610c4cb3edf6316: For your own figure, our villa build and renovation cost calculator gives indicative low, likely and high ranges with every source listed, and our villa renovation cost guide explains why an older villa's real cost depends on what is behind its walls. We do not publish a separate rate per square foot for Jumeirah Islands, because no published source supports a premium or discount by community.
484b9dcc20d2b0af: Where Jumeirah Islands renovations go wrong
a45978aef1786fa7: Pricing before opening up. On the contractor's side, the first thing we priced on any refurbishment was the risk we could not see. A few targeted openings in roofs, wet rooms and ceiling voids before the price is agreed turn a contractor's guess into a number.

0826844e7c6fac56: Palm Jumeirah villas: renovations, extensions and rebuilds
57f02cf76a549ce3: The fronds were largely built around twenty years ago. Today most serious work on the Palm is the transformation of an existing villa, and that brings a particular set of risks.
d550867790e7c7d6: Frond villa renovations, extensions and rebuilds
fd036881d78f4173: Palm Jumeirah is a reclaimed island built by Nakheel, and the villas on its fronds were delivered as a small number of standard types: Signature Villas, Garden Homes and Canal Cove townhouses. Neighbouring houses therefore started life almost identical, and much of what you see on the fronds today is the result of twenty years of owners changing them.
a444fefe67bc481b: That history shapes every project here in three ways. First, almost all serious work is a change to an existing house rather than a build on a fresh plot, so what the villa is today matters as much as what you want it to become. Second, Nakheel controls how far a standard type can move from its original form, and it looks at each application on its own merits. Third, the island sets the working conditions: narrow frond roads, neighbours close on both sides, strict community rules on hours and deliveries, and the sea a few metres from the back wall.
09626742bba4239b: The setting is also the technical challenge. Salt air, wind-blown sand, humidity and groundwater close to the surface work on twenty-year-old waterproofing, metalwork and services. On the contractor's side, we learned on coastal houses that the price is built from the outside in: the envelope and the water first, the finishes last. A Palm villa is no different, and the budgets that fail are usually the ones that started with the kitchen.
029c944a05a1aeaa: Owners on the Palm usually arrive with one of four briefs, and each puts the project on a different approval path with a different risk profile.
72f729a55b48affe: Interior renovation. Kitchens, bathrooms, floors, joinery and lighting. Nakheel's guidance is that owners may make changes that do not affect the external façade or structure, but an NOC from its Urban Planning team is still needed before any alteration. Once walls, wet areas or services move, the scope stops being cosmetic.
3a41318d792151fc: Renovation with external work. Larger openings to the water, a new pool, shading, terraces and landscaping. These change how the villa looks from the frond and the beach, so they sit squarely within Nakheel's review and need an authority permit as well.
557333a36fda037d: Extension. Adding built-up area on the ground or at roof level. This is where the Palm's arrangements for additional area and roof-level work apply, covered below.
f3489975a22d0e54: Rebuild. Demolishing the original house and building new. When the brief already needs new structure, a new envelope and new services, you are paying for most of a new house without the freedom of a new design. A rebuild takes longer and needs a full design and approval cycle, but it deserves to be priced alongside the renovation, not dismissed.
31edc231a2fa07ce: The comparison only works with real inputs: a condition survey with opening-up, a design developed far enough to price, and a programme that includes approvals and the cost of living elsewhere while the work is done. Our build and renovation cost calculator gives a sourced first range for both routes, and our guides to renovation costs and construction costs explain where the published figures come from.
8234f1221ed8f750: How approvals work on the Palm
25d6cd207404b746: Palm Jumeirah is a Nakheel community, so the master developer comes first. Nakheel asks owners to obtain an NOC from its Urban Planning team before making any alterations, requested online or through the My Nakheel app. Gulf News reported Nakheel's position that modification applications are assessed case by case, that various costs apply, that work must be carried out by approved contractors, and that owners with unpaid service charges are not permitted to modify their villas. With the NOC in hand, your registered consultant applies for the building permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits, through Dubai's unified permit window.
6d18c70889310799: Approval is not the same as access. Before a contractor starts, Nakheel requires a security deposit, a Site Access Permit and a PVC site fence, and it charges AED 52.50 per person for long-term workforce access permits on construction, modification and extension work. Our guide to the Nakheel NOC sets out the sequence in detail. Your appointed consultant or licensed contractor prepares and submits the applications. We keep the programme honest, so that the contractor's start date follows approvals in hand rather than the date the contract was signed.
d0371e5ea1d9d6a0: The Villa Status Report: start from what is really there
83539f847908aab4: Many Palm villas have already been altered, some with approval and some without: a covered terrace, an enclosed courtyard, a room on the roof. Before new work is considered, the question is how the villa as it stands compares with what Nakheel approved. Owners and agents usually call the inspection that answers it the Villa Status Report. Nakheel's own customer guidance confirms that for a completed villa an inspection report is required before an NOC for transfer can be requested, so the same question arises when you buy and when you sell.
3a8712f53d4415c8: The mechanism matters more than the name. Where the inspection finds built area or structures that do not match the approved drawings, those items generally have to be regularised or removed, and the cost falls on whoever owns the villa at the time. In another Nakheel community, Gulf News reported owners discovering unapproved work when they came to sell, and then paying a fine and a charge for the extra space. If you are buying a Palm villa that has been extended, ask the seller for the NOC and approved drawings for every change and have the house compared with them before you commit. If you already own the villa, establish its status before design starts, not after the drawings are finished.
30a3f48fa2372202: On the Palm, adding floor area is a commercial question with Nakheel as well as a design and permit question. Nakheel has sold additional land to Palm villa owners who wanted larger gardens, assessing each application individually, and owners extending villas in Nakheel communities have reported charges linked to the area added, on top of NOC and authority fees. Nakheel confirms the fees that apply when it reviews a request, and rates have changed over the years, so we do not publish a figure here. For your budget, the point is simple: have the charge confirmed in writing for your specific proposal before the design is fixed, and carry it as its own line in the cost plan rather than leaving it to the contingency.
397391b420186100: The roof looks like the obvious place to add space: a roof terrace, a pergola, a gym or a full additional floor. What is permitted at roof level depends on the guidelines for your villa type, the height and coverage limits that apply to your plot, and how the change affects neighbours' views and privacy along the frond. Nakheel decides what it will accept, and the authority permit follows. Some sales listings advertise extra floors and roof rooms; a listing is not evidence of approval. Ask for the NOC and approved drawings for anything above the original roofline, and put any roof-level idea to Nakheel early, before money is spent on detailed design.
950812892d0732c9: Roofs are also where water gets in. Any work at roof level is the moment to replace failed waterproofing properly, flood-test it and record the result, rather than building a new terrace on an old membrane.
a99bfe8da1b5a588: Water. Waterproofing that may be original, salt-laden air and high water tables. Roofs, terraces, wet rooms and basements are worth opening up and testing before the price is agreed, not after.
fb89fccb619e89af: Services. Original air conditioning, plumbing and electrical installations may not be worth keeping through a serious renovation. Have them surveyed before the budget assumes they can be reused.
214d4315a426abf6: Access and logistics. Fronds are narrow, neighbours are close and community rules on working hours and deliveries are strict. Contractors who have not worked on the Palm often under-price this.
addf7660cb6e74d4: Inherited alterations. Earlier work without approval, discovered after you have bought, designed and priced, can stop a project until it is resolved.
79c05a52209abf41: How we help on the Palm
98f5c72d4c040aab: We start by establishing what you actually own: the villa's approval history, a condition review arranged through the right specialists, and a straight renovate-or-rebuild comparison. Then we set a budget with a contingency matched to the age of the villa, help you choose a contractor experienced in occupied, tightly ruled communities, and represent you through the works and the defects period. eb8a257efa003d13: A realistic programme. New plot communities build out over years. Neighbouring construction, access and utility connections affect your timeline.
a226eba0a153fbe7: Not every Saadiyat owner is building on a plot. Aldar's Saadiyat Lagoons, launched in October 2022 with four- to six-bedroom villas, was reported by Gulf News at launch to have handovers expected from the second quarter of 2026. For an owner taking a villa from the developer, the handover inspection and the defects period that follows decide more about the house than any finish selection. Before you sign the handover documents, check the villa against your sale and purchase agreement and its specification, and make sure the warranties, as-built drawings and operating manuals are actually handed over. Then test what can only be tested in use: water on terraces, roofs and wet rooms, air conditioning under summer load, and drainage after the first heavy rain. Report every defect in writing, with photographs and dates, inside the defects period your contract sets, and keep the developer's acknowledgements. Longer-term structural defects are a separate question: the UAE Civil Code (Federal Decree-Law No. 25 of 2025) makes the contractor and the designing engineer jointly liable for ten years from delivery, and how that reaches you as a buyer depends on your contract, so take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer. Handover is one stage of our wider service rather than a stand-alone snag report; our villa snagging checklist shows what we look for.

28e1d1260afbf651: An owner's representative is a professional who acts only for the person paying for a building project. On a villa, we set the budget and programme, help appoint the consultant and contractor, control cost and time, report progress, handle variations and claims, and lead handover.
5e0b3ae70ed7ad98: Do I need an owner's representative to build a villa in Dubai?
084fd2d9115498e8: It isn't required by law. It is most valuable on bespoke villas, major renovations, and projects where the owner is often abroad or has not built before. We will tell you honestly if you don't need us.
771647015e830a41: How is that different from the consultant I have to appoint?
43e5eb40da6a1e49: In Dubai, a registered consultant carries the statutory design, submission and supervision responsibilities. They owe you proper professional care in that role. We add independent coordination and commercial scrutiny alongside them, acting only for you on cost, time, decisions, contracts and quality.
7280b40f4b82e499: Philip Chapman, our founder. He leads every appointment personally and is the person you speak to from the first conversation to handover. He is supported by a team of three project managers who attend site and provide cover when he is unavailable.
fd160f1c73f80327: Who attends site, and who covers when Philip is away?
0a6759b39e4bf52d: Philip leads every appointment and attends site himself. He is supported by a team of three project managers who attend site and provide cover when he is unavailable, for example when he is travelling. How often we attend site is agreed in writing in your appointment.
76ce0a9357ba196c: How often will you be on site?

b719c29b30c82867: In Abu Dhabi, a villa building permit is issued by the municipality through its services on TAMM, the emirate's government services platform, under regulations set by the Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT). Since June 2025, new private villa applications have been processed through Binaa, DMT's AI-assisted permits platform. In plot communities such as Saadiyat or Hudayriyat, you need the master developer's design approval first, and your registered consultant prepares and submits the application.
3eb07ee82e1c5474: If you have built or renovated in Dubai, the shape will feel familiar, but the regulator, the platforms and the villa rules are different. This guide explains the Abu Dhabi route from the owner's side, and where it departs from Dubai.
c478172039ec6dea: Who issues villa building permits in Abu Dhabi?
a66195d7ff758803: The regulator. DMT sets planning and building regulations for the emirate, including the private villa regulations it amended in September 2025 (DMT).
caa22b4ca135782f: The municipality. The permit itself is issued by the municipality for the region where your plot sits: Abu Dhabi City, Al Ain or Al Dhafra. Your consultant will confirm which applies.
af26d366c76017eb: The platforms. TAMM is the front door for government services in Abu Dhabi, and lists the building permit, renewal and related construction services (TAMM). Behind it, Binaa handles the technical review of permit applications, and DMT's Unified Permitting System carries later construction-stage submissions.
f28491a04c04cffe: On top of that, if your plot sits in a master-planned community, the master developer has its own design guidelines and review. Aldar on Saadiyat and Modon on Hudayriyat are examples. Developer approval comes before the municipal application, not alongside it.
bce5bd6125c45922: Hudayriyat Island, for illustration. Image: Modon (Hudayriyat Island).
3a887557dea25a58: What is Binaa, and what does it change for villa owners?
279b2992e501da35: DMT launched Binaa in June 2025 as a digital permits platform using AI review tools, Building Information Modelling, and virtual and augmented reality (DMT). At launch, DMT said AI review of 2D plans would be introduced gradually, with those plans reviewed manually in the meantime. A few points are directly relevant to a private client:
d0c4edc07084c258: Villas went first. Phase one of the rollout covered new private villas, which DMT said account for around 20,000 applications a year.
d1c8f1eb38e2e237: It looks for over-design. DMT says the platform is intended to flag designs that use unnecessarily complex methods or heavy materials for small villas. That is a cost question as much as a compliance one.
4dd87e5dfa03c9e9: Reviews are coordinated. Binaa was launched under an agreement with Abu Dhabi Civil Defence Authority, TAQA and e&, so that data, documents and technical reviews are shared rather than chased one by one.
42f78f059ef1b1ce: Owners can see progress. DMT says owners, consultants and contractors can monitor an application's progress on the platform.
9f82537d4f020255: The early results are reported by the government itself. In March 2026 the Abu Dhabi Media Office reported that the average time to issue a residential villa building permit had fallen by 57% since Binaa launched, that resubmissions had dropped by 53%, and that DMT issued more than 11,000 building permits in 2025 (Abu Dhabi Media Office).
d12e498f26ceeff3: What are the steps to get a villa permit in Abu Dhabi?
2c6d89952757009c: The sequence below is how we would plan it from the owner's side. Your registered consultant will confirm the detail for your plot and municipality.
e35fc1a6822daf8d: Confirm what the plot allows. Site plan, the master developer's design guidelines if any, and the current DMT villa regulations.
de0911fc86f847cb: Appoint a registered consultant. In Abu Dhabi, engineering consultants and contractors are licensed and classified through services on TAMM (TAMM). Check registration before you sign.
e8f5d9db9a7e3354: Design to the brief and the rules. Concept, then detailed design, including the Estidama Pearl requirements (see below).
ba7f55f6e167a680: Master developer approval. Where it applies, submit to the developer and obtain its approval or no-objection.
bd3d08f2bfab47e6: Municipal permit application. Your consultant submits the drawings and documents. TAMM's listing for a new building permit names approved plans and architectural layout drawings among the documents, and shows a 10 working day service time at the time of writing (TAMM).
5cdebd9b2fc01410: Start on site within the permit's life. TAMM's renewal service says a permit can be renewed once, provided it has not exceeded its six-month validity (TAMM). Do not let a permit lapse while you are still choosing a contractor.
4563e76c2aeeab38: Construction-stage reporting and inspections. Your consultant and contractor report through the Unified Permitting System, and the authority inspects.
abb2c4024aa49913: Completion and connection. Final inspections, completion documentation and utility connections before you move in.
c16e2d143c64dad0: Circular No. 9 of 2026, issued by DMT's Urban Planning and Permits Centre, replaces traditional phase-closure permits with certified technical reports for designated categories of project. The registered consultant responsible for supervising the works and the contractor prepare a dated, signed report with photographs covering the works, inspections and corrective actions, and the two share legal liability for non-compliance. The centre continues unannounced site visits. The circular does not waive mandatory field inspections where physical verification is required, or clearances from other bodies such as Abu Dhabi Civil Defence (WAM, Khaleej Times).
ff1a1a40179f51ea: For an owner, this is a meaningful shift. More of the assurance that work matches the approved drawings now rests on reports written by the people doing and supervising the work. That makes it more important, not less, that the owner has an independent view of what is actually happening on site.

Two differences catch owners out most often. First, a consultant who knows Dubai's process well is not automatically the right choice in Abu Dhabi; ask specifically about recent Abu Dhabi villa submissions and Estidama. Second, the villa regulations themselves differ, so a design brief written with a Dubai villa in mind may need rethinking before a single line is drawn.

e96f37c286abbd1b: What do Abu Dhabi's private villa regulations allow?
a996e0b30046db6a: DMT's September 2025 amendments loosened several rules that shape a villa's design (DMT):
3d986bbe0f03cf14: A closed, lightweight rooftop majlis can be added without affecting the land-use percentage.
faf789448421d3c1: The front setback from the street is reduced to 1.5 metres.
1d476fab8c7b9748: Guest annexes may have a first floor or a basement, provided they are not built against the boundary wall.
007063c248888fb9: Shading structures do not count towards the building footprint.
7975dab07a80ea52: The whole flat roof can be built on, provided a 1.5 metre setback is kept.
867d08847f20b7fa: Two villas can sit next to each other without a separating wall, with the owners' agreement.
6a39787f67fbe39c: This follows earlier changes in 2019, when Abu Dhabi reduced minimum sizes for bedrooms, kitchens, dining rooms and majlis areas, removed the requirement for an internal hallway, and cut the maximum side fence height from six metres to four (Gulf News). The direction of travel is towards flexibility, but master developer guidelines can still be stricter than the emirate's rules. Read both.
60811ec9594aae46: What is the Estidama Pearl rating, and does a villa need it?
c124fd5843898e07: Estidama is Abu Dhabi's sustainability programme, and the Pearl Rating System is its building rating tool. New villas must achieve at least a 1 Pearl rating, which means meeting all the mandatory credits, documented through the approvals process (DMT). Higher ratings need additional credit points. In our experience, requirements of this kind are cheapest when they shape the design from the start, and expensive when they arrive as a late compliance exercise.
88a5fae2df9e5bfa: Do I need a permit for a pool, extension or renovation?
a30264790f5ab254: Usually yes, but the route is lighter than a new build. Since August 2025, DMT has let contractors obtain permits directly for defined minor works on villas, farmhouses and holiday homes, including concrete and metal structures, extensions of up to 25 square metres, non-structural modifications, maintenance and interior finishing, swimming pools, canopies, shade structures and fences (DMT).
c7b6d341c0d9ea73: That is convenient, and it also changes who holds the paperwork. If your contractor obtains the permit, make sure the scope in the permit matches the scope you are paying for, and that you receive copies. In a master community, check the developer's own requirements as well.
b8df95764b0e5a0d: Can a foreign owner build a villa in Abu Dhabi?
00ce6060c347d917: Foreign nationals can own property in designated investment zones in Abu Dhabi (UAE Government portal). Confirm the ownership position for your specific plot with a UAE-qualified lawyer before you buy; this guide is not legal advice.
0743576c33e6d460: A view from the builder's side
4ef6b74c6985a9c0: For 21 years we were the contractor waiting on approvals, and we learned to read the start date from the state of the drawings, not the date of the application. The trouble usually began earlier: Drawings submitted before the owner had really decided the brief, then revised after comments. A contractor appointed on permit drawings that were never detailed enough to price properly. A start date that slipped because nobody had booked the team while the application was in.
1249c9433345b7a6: On our side of the table, a fast permit was only good news if the drawings behind it were complete. When they were not, we priced the gaps as risk, and later as variations. Abu Dhabi's faster digital review is genuinely helpful. It does not remove the need for the owner to settle the brief, check the design against the budget, and have the contractor selection running in parallel, so that a permit with a limited life turns into a start on site.

a6842db4be4604ef: Insist on three things every week or month: a dated photo report, an updated cost-to-complete, and a decision log showing what you approved and when.
d700c8a364461da2: Never release a payment you cannot tie to an agreed milestone and a valuation from the consultant, however urgent the request sounds.

b932d04ec515b155: Yes, you can build a villa in Dubai while living in the UK, and many owners do. Design development, approvals, payments and most progress monitoring can be handled remotely if the reporting is disciplined. What cannot be delegated without risk are a small number of decisions about the plot, the design freeze, finishes and handover, and the habit of checking every payment against something you can verify.
8ed3f9f864e23f9f: This article sets out what works from a distance, what needs you in the room, and where we see absentee projects drift.
fa7a21a075231d9e: What can you do remotely on a Dubai villa build?
65d697f4f5c8f49e: More than most people expect. Dubai's permit process is now largely digital: the authorities run a single window for building permits that links Dubai Municipality, the Dubai Development Authority, Trakhees and the service providers (Dubai Municipality). Your registered consultant makes those submissions; you do not need to be in Dubai for them to happen.
1083aa2efe22475e: From the UK you can realistically:
d39a59d577af036a: Review and comment on concept and developed designs over video calls and shared drawings.
a0508a625ab4ea7d: Approve the brief, the budget and the programme.
48a5116fbcfe5fd8: Compare contractor bids, with help, and decide who to appoint.
f45e22db904ab2a5: Approve or reject variations, provided you have a clear process for doing so.
9f17004c9df33c54: Release stage payments against agreed milestones.
3a351f0853ea9408: Follow progress through photographs, video walkrounds and written reports.
bfe04d62c224b361: The design and approvals phase is the easiest part to run remotely. One Dubai engineering consultancy puts the permit stage at four to eight weeks for a straightforward project once the drawings are complete, and construction at typically 12 to 18 months (Optimal Engineering); Engel & Völkers says most villas take 12 to 24 months from approval to completion (Engel & Völkers). Until construction starts, most of the work is on paper. We break the timeline down in how long it takes to build a villa in Dubai.
bd326090fb8f00f1: Dubai Hills Estate, for illustration. Image: Emaar.
9ff7e7e1dbd92735: Which decisions need you there in person?
ff635b37c7a336b3: In our experience, four moments justify a flight.
25648ef3935243da: Orientation, views, neighbours, access and noise do not show up on an affection plan. See our plot checks.
8a21e2d07d4d7e17: Walking the plot with the drawings in hand catches level, view and privacy problems while they are still cheap to fix.
932467b0e55d7f26: Stone, timber, joinery samples and lighting look different under Dubai sun than on a screen. Approve physical samples and keep them on site as the reference. See sourcing materials abroad.
030520de6a602573: Snagging is a physical exercise. You need to open, run, flush and test things. Our snagging checklist covers what to look at.
4928027f4a3f3485: A mid-construction visit, when the structure is complete and first-fix services are in, is also worth making. It is the last point at which you can see what is going into the walls and ceilings before it disappears.
432f4b8b74028ad3: What reporting should you insist on?
9baaba59a21e302b: On the contractor's side, we learned that the clients who asked for structured information got a better-run job, because the discipline of producing it forced us to look at our own numbers. Ask for the following from the start, and write it into appointments where you can.
36d608cef2986e5e: Dated, labelled photographs organised by area, not a stream of images on a messaging app. Each set should show the same locations week on week so progress (or lack of it) is obvious. Include close-ups of anything about to be covered: waterproofing, insulation, pipework, cable routes, structural connections.
d81aec3e5d801030: Not just what has been paid, but what it will cost to finish. A sound cost report shows the original contract sum, approved variations, pending variations, provisional sums spent and remaining, contingency used, and a forecast final cost: what has been paid to date plus the forecast cost to complete, never the whole contract sum added to what has already been paid. If the forecast only changes when someone asks, it is not a forecast.
683017dd4661595c: The current programme against the baseline, with the critical path marked and any slippage explained. Look for activities whose dates quietly move each month.
b5644513cb21af9d: A single running record of every decision you have made: what was asked, what you approved, the date, and any cost or time effect. When disputes arise months later, the decision log is usually the most useful document on the project. It also protects you from the phrase "the client asked for it" being applied to things you never approved.
18f263df4c1764fc: Our site visits and reporting and cost and programme control services are built around exactly these documents.
e02d43b37a0408cb: How do payments and banking work from the UK?
50d712a2b01f5bc0: Keep this simple and auditable. Practical points, in general terms:
1e5debed9172926a: Pay against milestones, not requests. Stage payments should follow a schedule in the contract and a valuation of work done from the consultant. Treat any request for money "to secure materials" or "to keep the crew on site" outside that schedule as a conversation, not a payment.
3ad8d56d24e29ad9: Use a UAE account where sensible. Many owners open a local account to make payments to contractors and authorities more straightforward. Banks' requirements for non-residents vary, so ask them directly.
e8e6294d59a296cc: Watch currency exposure. The dirham has been pegged to the US dollar at AED 3.6725 since 1997 (Gulf News), so a build funded from sterling carries sterling-to-dollar exchange risk over a programme that may run well over a year. Some owners convert in tranches against the payment schedule. Speak to your bank or a currency specialist.
4e33ce8178a57e0d: Keep a payment register. Every payment, its reference to a milestone or approved variation, and the supporting valuation. Reconcile it against the cost report monthly.
25adb6761a072176: Know what you are holding back. Retention and advance payment arrangements should be clear in the contract and tracked, because they are your main leverage at the end of the job.
c1bb3e41b6af8bdf: None of this is financial or tax advice. If the build has UK tax implications for you, speak to your own advisers.
d4a49cfef023913a: Time zones: the hidden programme risk
9e6e4fcc9166344e: The UAE is four hours ahead of the UK in winter and three hours ahead during British Summer Time, and does not change its clocks. That sounds manageable, but it has a real effect. Site teams often start early in the day to avoid the heat, so by the time a UK owner is at their desk, the site has been working for hours. A question raised on site at 8am Dubai time may not get your answer until their afternoon, and a decision needed on a Friday may wait until the following week.
79855a6191577879: A fixed weekly call at a time that suits both sides, with a written agenda and minutes.
074fd7931cdef469: A defined turnaround for owner decisions, for example 48 hours, agreed with the contractor and consultant.
ffbcbc3c9b7f4ea3: Someone on the ground with clear, limited authority to deal with small site queries so they do not stall work.
bd533690f54311e6: Do you need a power of attorney?
00e09a474473eb8f: Sometimes. A power of attorney can make life easier for authority submissions, utility connections, handover formalities and signing documents when you cannot travel. It can also be dangerous if it is drawn too widely. A general power of attorney over your property affairs is a very different instrument from one limited to specific tasks on a specific project.
96903b7fa4aa8553: A power of attorney signed in the UK typically needs to go through notarisation and attestation steps before it can be used in the UAE. On the UK side, the Legalisation Office can attach an apostille to a document such as a power of attorney, provided it has first been certified by a UK public official such as a notary or solicitor (GOV.UK); UAE attestation follows. The detail changes and depends on the purpose, so take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on scope, form and process before you sign anything.
6c8a87c2ce0f770b: How does UAE construction practice differ from the UK?
1ff799e24ce215fb: Owners who have built in the UK often assume the same rules apply. The principles are familiar, but several things are different.
ee8ba5098602c112: In the UK, most private residential work uses JCT forms, with an architect or contract administrator issuing instructions and certificates under the contract. In Dubai, the Municipality publishes standard forms for engineering consultancy and construction contracting for private villas (Dubai Municipality), and many projects use FIDIC-style terms. Read our guide to villa construction contracts in the UAE for more, and have any contract reviewed by a UAE-qualified lawyer.
d3c6e68eca01f820: In Dubai, the registered consultant typically designs the villa, makes the authority submissions and carries the formal site role through construction, including assessing the contractor's payment applications. That is a regulated role: under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, no one may carry out engineering consultancy in Dubai without authorisation, and an office needs a valid trade licence and registration with Dubai Municipality to present itself as an engineering consultancy (Dubai Media Office). The owner appoints the consultant and the contractor separately, and the consultant's position sits between the two. An owner's representative such as Eastbridge is a different role: we act only for the owner, alongside the consultant and the contractor, and do not replace either. Our article on owner's representative vs project manager vs consultant explains the difference.
c8dc66538ffd61fc: UAE law imposes a ten-year liability on the main contractor and the engineer for serious structural defects, now set out in Articles 821 to 824 of the new Civil Code in force from 1 June 2026; it cannot be contracted out of (Charles Russell Speechlys). The ten years run from handover, and the liability covers total or partial collapse and defects that threaten the building's stability or safety, not finishes or ordinary services faults (Kayrouz & Associates). There is no direct UK equivalent for a one-off private house, though the protection is narrower than many owners assume. Take legal advice on how it applies to you.
9c071125f4af66c4: UK residential contractors are used to clients who visit regularly and argue every variation. In Dubai, the volume of work and the spread of contractor capability are both wide. Some firms run well-documented, transparent jobs. Others rely on the owner not being there. Your reporting regime tells the contractor which kind of client you are.
b4d922aef7817dae: Common failure modes for absentee owners
97496a27e16b4129: Every builder sees these from the other side of the table. They are not unique to Dubai, but distance makes each one worse.
d4fc04337725d5c6: Verbal approvals. A quick "yes, fine" on a call becomes a variation nobody priced. Every approval should go into the decision log, in writing, with its cost.
bde9b4983535a018: Payments ahead of progress. Once the contractor has been paid for work not yet done, your leverage has gone. This is the single most common way absentee builds get into trouble.
70e2ee5df93d2e32: Design that was never truly frozen. Small changes during construction cost far more than the same changes on paper, and each one gives the contractor a legitimate reason to ask for more time.
0787fa3d0dbc075c: Provisional sums left vague. On the contractor's side, the first thing we looked at on any job was where the provisional sums sat and how loosely they were described. That is where final accounts grow.
8a0161c03308a21f: Nobody independent looking. Photographs chosen by the contractor show what the contractor wants you to see. An independent visit, unannounced where possible, sees what is actually there.
baf4803a6e27db0d: Late finishes decisions. If you have not chosen tiles, sanitaryware or joinery when the programme needs them, the delay is yours, and so is the cost.
abe0baa9839cf2d6: Handover from a distance. Accepting the keys without a proper snagging inspection usually means a long defects period of chasing by email.
b1e4b76f3f3af5e0: If a project has already drifted, our stalled project rescue work starts by rebuilding the cost, programme and decision record so you can see where you stand.
be02015eb2a15aba: We represent owners who are building in Dubai and Abu Dhabi but cannot be there every week. We work alongside your registered consultant and your contractor, carry out independent client-side site visits, and give you clear reporting on cost, programme and decisions so you can approve things with confidence from the UK. Our overseas owners page explains how we structure that. If you are planning a build or already part-way through one, get in touch.
