bc6681593b6cf1a3: Why plot checks matter more than the price
8217643cf409cc3e: On the contractor's side, we priced many houses on plots the client had already bought, and the most expensive surprises were almost always baked in on the day they exchanged: a level change nobody had surveyed, a restrictive covenant, a drain running across the garden. The negotiation over a few percent on the land price mattered far less than these.
70d83b2256ebfc10: In Dubai the same logic applies, with the added layer of master developer rules. A plot is only worth what you are allowed, and can afford, to build on it.
225f01429b94db4c: Dubai Islands, for illustration. Image: Nakheel.
2148724108faab88: Freehold status. In Dubai, foreign ownership is permitted in areas designated as freehold under Regulation No. 3 of 2006 (UAE Government portal). If you are buying as a foreign national, confirm the plot sits in one.
b56bc7027ff2b9ba: Ownership and title. Confirm the seller owns the plot and is entitled to sell it, and whether there is a mortgage or other restriction registered. Your lawyer will handle this through the proper channels.
d57cf3aae30578b6: Affection plan. The official plot plan sets out the plot number, area, boundaries, permitted use and other key details. Check the area matches what you are paying for, and that the permitted use is residential villa.
9baa3eee58050152: Site plan. Where the plot falls under the Dubai Development Authority, the site plan is a legal document issued in the plot owner's or lessee's name and used to obtain construction approvals (DDA). Whichever authority applies, ask for the current plan, not the one from the original sale.
6806420445eadff5: Payment status. If the plot was bought off a master developer on a payment plan, confirm what has been paid, what remains, and what the developer requires to transfer. Plots not yet fully paid sit on the Dubai Land Department's provisional register; registering an initial sale there costs 2% of the sale value each for seller and purchaser, plus small fixed fees (Dubai Land Department). Your lawyer will confirm which fees apply to your transaction.
49234214128c98ba: Master developer consent. Transfers in master communities usually need a no-objection letter from the master developer, which may depend on service charges being up to date.
3e8171cb6ce18c4b: Every master community has rules on what you can build. They sit on top of the authority's building regulations, and they are where a plot's real capacity is decided. Ask for the current design guidelines for the specific plot, not a brochure summary.
aa2af30ea16a95ad: To see what a master developer's control looks like in practice, take a Nakheel design approval issued in June 2026 for a plot in one of its communities. It checks the design against that plot's development control regulations, allows any non-standard item only by name, is valid for six months, and is personal to the purchaser: it does not pass automatically to a new buyer if the approved design has not been built (Nakheel). If the seller tells you a plot "comes with approved drawings", ask whether that approval is still valid and whether it can be transferred to you.

42c3d48cd6b31183: Build-by deadlines deserve special attention. If you are buying a plot to hold rather than to build on straight away, an obligation to start construction within a set period can change your plans and your finances. Read the sale documents closely and take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer.
9df1435d27aef7d0: Remember too that authority rules can change. In Abu Dhabi, for example, the Department of Municipalities and Transport amended private villa regulations in September 2025, including changes to rooftop majlis, a 1.5 m front setback and annex basements (DMT). Your registered consultant should confirm the current rules for your plot, in Dubai or Abu Dhabi.
2a2ae91bf7621e27: Which authority will approve your villa?
78117820578e055b: Start with who will design it. Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, no one may carry out engineering consultancy in Dubai without authorisation, and an office needs a valid trade licence and Dubai Municipality registration to present itself as an engineering consultancy (Dubai Media Office). Appoint a registered consultant early enough to read the guidelines with you before you buy.
acad16f0e84f213e: In Dubai, permits come through a single unified window that links Dubai Municipality, the Dubai Development Authority, Trakhees and the utility and service providers (Dubai Municipality). Which authority applies depends on where your plot sits. Your consultant will confirm this; in master communities you will typically also need the master developer's approval or no-objection before the authority permit. Our design and approvals page explains how we support that process.
fe74b29d1b6ffe4c: Plots in master communities usually carry service charges from the day you own them, whether or not you have built. Check:
a720c82b9e2d4b9e: The current annual charge and how it is calculated.
d0c5fa2a2a25ee1a: Whether charges are up to date (arrears can delay transfer).
6a0757de80cb3112: Any planned increases or special levies for infrastructure.
945cd70dd16b09eb: How charges change once the villa is complete.
8fd4a86a50f02b88: Much of Dubai's prime villa land is reclaimed or coastal, and ground conditions vary. Before committing:
d3cca37abc49c3a3: Ask whether a geotechnical investigation exists for the plot or nearby plots, and read it.
ac4d36644559e724: Understand the likely foundation type. Piled foundations cost significantly more than shallow ones.
e483a6557afc996e: If you want a basement, ask about groundwater level. Dewatering during construction and long-term waterproofing of a basement below the water table add cost and risk.
e873e5c12d9d7f1c: Check for any fill or contamination issues the seller or developer is aware of.
c8e4edfd369da760: In our experience, foundations and below-ground work are where early budgets move most, because they are priced before anyone has dug a hole.
cea61b743c898bfb: Are water, power, sewerage and telecoms available at the plot boundary now, or are they promised?
482f72c3d5b35fa6: Who pays for the connections, and are there capacity limits?
7c7e5e4dd8bc2fd4: Is the road access complete and adopted?
326dea53346d515b: For newer communities, what is the delivery schedule for infrastructure, and what happens if it slips?
acfcfe366d1131fb: One Dubai engineering consultancy puts a permanent DEWA connection at roughly AED 10,000 to 40,000, and authority approvals in total at AED 80,000 to 250,000 (Optimal Engineering). Treat that as a guide, not a quote. The same Nakheel approval requires the owner's side to obtain NOCs from the utility and service providers and caps the plot's power load at the level the master developer allocated (Nakheel), so ask what load is allocated to the plot before you design a villa that needs more.
91c98f3c795401a1: Stand on the plot and look around. Then check what the guidelines allow your neighbours to build. A vacant plot next door today may become a three-storey villa that overlooks your pool. Ask:
1f3098776e457068: What is the maximum height and setback on adjoining plots?
dff700fe07594904: Are any neighbours already building, and in what state is their site?
62011cdc2aeb381f: Will a neighbour's construction affect your access, noise or programme?
096e50d70873ffa4: Is there anything planned nearby, such as a road, a utility building or a commercial plot?
a84242c9af56ecfe: Realistic build budget against plot price
9417557dfe560a93: This is where many plot purchases go wrong. Owners spend months negotiating the land and then discover the villa they want costs far more than expected.
6dc70e543057c12b: Published construction-only ranges for Dubai villas, 2025 to 2026, from Engel & Völkers:
9c87ad6dac272b0a: On top of construction, add design and engineering (Engel & Völkers quotes AED 50,000 to 150,000 for design, engineering and permits; Optimal Engineering puts multi-discipline consultants' fees at 6 to 12% of the construction contract value), a contingency (Engel & Völkers says 10 to 15% of total project cost is widely recommended), pool, landscaping and furniture. Interiors alone run from about AED 200,000 for a basic villa to AED 800,000 to over AED 1 million for a high-end one, according to Engel & Völkers.
9cd743d3c4078dc0: Take the maximum built-up area the guidelines allow, or the area you actually want.
e3a258e3e1775a62: Apply a construction rate matched to the specification you expect.
69949001b62780fb: Add design, approvals, contingency, pool, landscaping and furniture.
448c9c90a56adeac: Add finance and holding costs, including service charges, for the duration of the build.
2c5664773394f443: On a prime plot, the villa can easily cost as much as, or more than, the land. Our guide to villa construction cost in Dubai goes into more detail.
5295f3758989d56b: Ask the hard question early: what would this finished villa sell for? Compare plot price plus total build cost against recent sales of comparable completed villas in the same community. If the combined cost is close to or above that figure, you are building for lifestyle rather than investment, which is a legitimate choice, but it should be a conscious one. Use an independent valuer for this.
97e0385e2a302053: New plot markets: Hudayriyat, Dubai Islands and Palm Jebel Ali
7a7c4567ae682683: Several newer communities are now selling plots for private villas.
f8c68b36cc4de6c4: Hudayriyat, Abu Dhabi. Modon launched its first residential plots community on Hudayriyat Island, with more than 1,700 plots for four to six bedroom villas (Middle East Construction News). Abu Dhabi's approvals run through a different system from Dubai's, under the Department of Municipalities and Transport. See our Hudayriyat page.
7af164bed8fea53c: If you are buying in Abu Dhabi, our guide to villa permits in Abu Dhabi explains how approvals there differ from Dubai.
3f1f4dcb6e9fc1d1: Dubai Islands and Palm Jebel Ali. Both are Nakheel master communities where plots are being sold for private villas. As newer markets, they have fewer completed villas to benchmark against, so evidence on actual build costs, timelines and resale values is thinner. That can be an opportunity, but it raises the importance of checking infrastructure delivery dates, the precise design guidelines, any build-by obligations and the master developer's approval process. See our pages on Dubai Islands and Palm Jebel Ali.

f8317230c66ae2ad: Costs · 1 November 2026 · 10 min read · By Philip Chapman
dde2c919277600f1: Client-side project managers usually charge in one of three ways: a fixed fee for a defined review, a monthly fee, or a percentage of construction cost.
2fa135b4ef24528e: A percentage means little until you know what it is applied to: the approved budget, the accepted tender or the final cost of the works.
1f4bbe97cbcca1bb: The fee should name the people doing the work and say how often they attend site, because that is most of what you are paying for.
c8bbe0a474e337d8: Agree in writing what happens to the fee if the build overruns on cost or time, before anything goes wrong.
dea5a537fc5559dd: Compare proposals against a written scope of works, not against a headline rate.
88ac98ebcf64ee90: What is a percentage fee calculated on?
6ed8fa7526b0c914: Who will do the work, and how often will they be on site?
8781769f275f7184: What is usually excluded from a project manager's fee?
fe8a4ca6bdfbaee4: What happens to the fee if the build overruns?
738dc652c995dc90: What questions should you ask any project manager about fees?
9d4a60cc95ee7000: A client-side project manager in Dubai will usually charge in one of three ways: a fixed fee for a defined review, a monthly fee, or a percentage of construction cost. The headline number matters less than three details behind it: what the percentage is applied to, who actually does the work and how often they are on site, and what happens to the fee if the build overruns. There is no published Dubai benchmark for these fees, so the only fair comparison is proposal against proposal, each priced against the same written scope of works.
553aa14e370ebd38: This guide explains the fee models, the small print that changes what you pay, and the questions to ask any firm, including us. Our own published ranges are on our fees page.
859cbb79e859add1: How do client-side project managers charge?
08abc1defe42888b: The Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS) guidance note Appointing a project manager (GN 107/2013) groups project management appointments into four generic types: lump sum, time based, target, and term or framework (RICS GN 107/2013). It notes that a lump sum can be expressed as a single figure, a schedule of prices, or a percentage. On a private villa, those reduce to three models in practice.
1574260492f202ad: One price for a defined piece of work, such as a plot, design, contractor-quote or stalled-project review, ending in a written report
91e879571ed1ff70: What the report covers, and whether a follow-up meeting is included
788e74a3bd8c4551: A set amount each month for an agreed level of input
fa0adc080b4dd73a: Projects where length or scope is uncertain
b91e239bb02b2037: What happens when the programme runs long
70c346abcfeb55d3: A percentage of the build cost, paid in stages
f609774767b91f22: A well-defined build from start to handover
5808fefcaa10518e: What the percentage is applied to
4fa66ed2c59c7677: RICS also describes time-based (reimbursable) appointments, where you pay hours at agreed rates, and target arrangements that share savings or excesses. These are more common on larger commercial work. For time-based appointments, RICS suggests an "upset limit": a ceiling the charges cannot pass without your prior written agreement. The same idea works on any model.
8493d2e849f69e0f: FIDIC's Client/Consultant Model Services Agreement, the White Book (5th edition, 2017), is the international standard form most often used to appoint consultants. FIDIC describes it as "one of the most widely used forms of construction professional services contract currently being used globally", suitable for services including project management and the administration of construction (FIDIC). It does not set fee levels. Its value to an owner is the structure: a defined scope of services, a procedure for varying that scope and agreeing the effect on the consultant's remuneration, and a programme the consultant must follow (Curtis).
27d2506919963a04: What is a percentage fee calculated on?
f88bf46c887ca40d: This is the question most owners never ask, and it can move the fee more than the percentage itself. RICS is direct: when using a percentage, "it is important to define and agree what the percentage will be applied to, e.g. the approved budget, the accepted tender for the construction contract or the final cost of the works."
8e709be05b688cc9: The approved budget. The fee is known from the start. If the build later comes in under budget, you still pay on the budget.
75f57fbf94cf2af7: The accepted tender. The fee is fixed once the contract is signed. It does not rise when variations are added, so the project manager has no financial reason to welcome them.
22181e5c34a97310: The final cost of the works. The fee follows the actual cost. That sounds fair, but it means the fee rises when the cost rises.
13a51537b67299e2: Ask also what "construction cost" includes. Does it cover loose furniture, landscaping, the pool, specialist joinery bought directly by you, or authority and connection fees? Each inclusion widens the base the percentage is applied to.
b4aea17b9ce63527: RICS adds a caution worth repeating: "As the complexity of the project increases the use of percentage of construction cost becomes less reliable." On a truly one-off villa, where design and specification keep developing, a percentage is a reasonable guide but a weak contract on its own. It needs a written scope beside it.
4e976969cd99d5a0: There is a wider point here. A fee that grows with the build cost sits awkwardly with the job of controlling that cost. In August 2025, Dubai Municipality warned several engineering consultancy offices that villa structural designs had gone "beyond safety requirements in the Dubai Building Code" and "ended up unjustifiably raising construction costs" for homeowners (Gulf News). That warning was about designers, not project managers, but the lesson carries: understand how everyone you appoint is paid, and whether a higher build cost pays them more.
607da14744a50ff6: Who will do the work, and how often will they be on site?
96a6f44f82c45a03: A project management fee is mostly the cost of people's time. Two proposals at the same percentage can buy very different things if one names a senior person attending site regularly and the other names nobody.
790d3a7938ba1a27: RICS lists "key (and other) personnel" among the elements every appointment should include. In its typical criteria for assessing project management proposals, "key personnel (qualifications and experience relative to proposed role)" carries the largest suggested weighting, 30% to 40% of the quality score. The people are the service.
aa6e3d7e6ec0ca56: Ask any firm to put in writing:
d5edc9ed04cfb389: The person who leads your project, by name, and what they personally do.
292c480fee417967: Who covers when that person is unavailable.
8310a6eb96c6e7d9: How often someone attends site at each stage, and which meetings they attend.
8c26f68ff01c42a7: What you receive after each visit, and each month.
12ebd4b6293d8290: Whether the named lead can be replaced without your agreement.
b6f0d40096f078e8: At Eastbridge, our founder, Philip Chapman, leads every appointment personally, supported by a team of three project managers who attend site and provide cover. Site attendance is agreed in writing in the scope of each appointment.
42db87ab7a996995: From the builder's side, we can tell you how this looked on the other side of the table. On a contractor's team, you quickly learn which client representatives actually turn up, and which ones read the monthly report and nothing else. The ones who appeared at the right moments, before concrete was poured and before walls were closed up, were the ones whose questions we prepared for. Site presence changes behaviour in a way that a report alone does not.
0935d3d948d4b638: What is usually excluded from a project manager's fee?
66c2ea6df6dfaa12: Exclusions are where like-for-like comparison fails most often. Read them as carefully as the price. Common exclusions on a Dubai villa include:
4e8be5de1490827c: The registered consultant's fee. Design and the statutory engineering role belong to a Dubai Municipality-registered consultancy. Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, only registered offices may practise engineering consultancy or present themselves as consultancy offices (Dubai Media Office, Law No. 14 of 2025). That appointment is separate, with its own fee. Dubai Municipality publishes guidance contract forms for consultancy and contracting on private villas, in Arabic, which it describes as for guidance rather than mandatory (Dubai Municipality).
8dc38205070d7cbf: Other specialists such as a quantity surveyor, a structural or condition survey, or a UAE-qualified lawyer, appointed and paid by the owner.
9296ac916cc26113: Authority, master developer and utility fees, which are paid by the owner whoever prepares the paperwork.
525be1ff52ae8772: Travel, especially overseas trips to source stone, joinery, lighting or fittings. Check whether it is charged at cost or with a margin.
bcef7f8bf5598ee2: Disputes. Work on a claim, adjudication or arbitration is often excluded or charged separately.
cb2c1699189c1ed3: The defects period. Some appointments end at handover; others run to the end of the defects liability period.
de7f0770337720bf: VAT. UAE VAT is charged at the standard rate of 5% on taxable supplies of services, unless an exemption or zero rate applies (Federal Tax Authority, Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Article 3). Ask whether a quote includes it.
9ede6d000f7d0f90: What happens to the fee if the build overruns?
3ae41b577192f6b1: Agree this before anything goes wrong. Overruns come in two forms, cost and time, and each fee model reacts differently.
ca781bf3a130539b: Cost overruns. A percentage applied to the final cost rises with it. As an illustration only, using our published full-service range: on a build of AED 12 million, a fee of 2.5% is AED 300,000. If the final cost rises by 10% to AED 13.2 million, the same fee applied to the final cost becomes AED 330,000. Applied to the accepted tender, it stays at AED 300,000. Neither is wrong, but you should know which you have signed.
2759c017b4068f71: Time overruns. A monthly fee rises with every extra month: a four-month delay adds four months of fees. Percentage fees can also extend in practice, because a firm that has priced eighteen months of attendance will reasonably ask to be paid for twenty-four.
a449770c51838626: The FIDIC White Book shows how a standard form handles this. Clause 4.4 of the 2017 edition gives the consultant additional fees for "delay, impediment or prevention caused or attributable to the Client" and to "the Client's other consultants, contractors, or other third parties" (Beale & Co, via ACE). In plain terms, a contractor's delay can increase your project manager's fee. That is fair, because the extra months are real work, but it should be visible and priced in advance.
50dc0b741d987822: Which base the percentage is applied to, and whether it is fixed at the accepted tender.
7ad260a66e5c81dc: A ceiling, or "upset limit", that the fee cannot pass without your written agreement.
a0f65be4392947ea: How extra months are priced if the programme extends, and who decides that it has extended.
b2744912675b3830: Whether part of the fee is tied to stages, so you are not paying ahead of progress.
a5acbf3bb48531e9: On long projects, how rates are reviewed. RICS recommends that rates and prices be fixed for no more than four years, with an annual review against an appropriate index preferable.
781b099832e4b02f: What questions should you ask any project manager about fees?
abaf4b77e6794cf1: Ask every firm the same questions, including us, and ask for the answers in writing. Fees are only part of the choice: our guide to choosing a client-side project manager covers independence, who does the work and how to compare firms.
f817683ac1a2d6f0: What exactly is in the scope of works, and what is outside it?
417f20a959d6980e: Is the fee fixed, monthly or a percentage? If a percentage, what is it applied to, and what does "construction cost" include?
1d715e75a0afa81c: Who leads my project, by name, and who else will work on it?
76fb99052c4ca621: How often will someone attend site at each stage, and what will I receive afterwards?
fe3d9a10b792d3d7: What happens to the fee if the cost or the programme overruns?
d4778702bce52c67: How is work outside the scope priced, and will I see that price before the work starts?
3aef054adea5d2a7: What is excluded: travel, other specialists, disputes, the defects period, VAT?
93bd0e4c0b647701: Do you receive any payment from contractors, consultants or suppliers on my project?
4463d1828d3cdc7b: Can you instruct the contractor or approve a payment without my written approval?
0d19a11fbc7f9175: How does the appointment end, and what do I receive at the end?
bbe78efdc2790670: The last two matter more than they look. RICS lists "authority levels" among the key elements of an appointment. The person representing you should not be able to spend your money or commit you to a change without your written approval.
c9a6d866d6925f32: Every one-off villa is different, so we do not publish a day rate, an hourly rate or a fixed price. We agree a written scope of works after a free first call, and any work outside that scope is quoted before it starts. Our published ranges reflect the level of input:
dfe5200b49a1ca64: A plot, design, contractor-quote or stalled-project review, with a written report
40cffe011f201fc8: Cost, contract and payment reviews and monthly reporting, without regular site presence
ae287c3e62d8a1ca: A monthly fee agreed in the written scope
597227eaf97137b7: Representation from brief to handover, with site attendance, every review, and sourcing trips with you (travel at cost)
fe56542a26eb3da1: Where a fee sits within its range depends on how often we attend site, how much sourcing travel is involved, the complexity of the design and the length of the programme. The details, including what each level includes, are on our fees page.
636db4e4ea498a1e: If you are comparing proposals from project managers, or wondering whether you need one at all, we are happy to talk it through on a free first call. We will tell you plainly what level of input your project needs, and whether a single review, such as a contractor and consultant selection review or a plot review, would be enough. For a full appointment, see owner's representation, read how we think about independence, or contact us.

Eastbridge publishes ranges by level of input: a review costs AED 9,500 to 15,000, part service is a monthly fee agreed in the written scope, and full service is typically 1.75% to 3% of build cost. The exact fee is agreed in a written scope of works after a free first call.
0d8eeba862d099c3: Is a percentage fee better than a monthly fee?
8fec13180388ce1d: Neither is better in every case. A percentage suits a well-defined build and ties the fee to the size of the job; a monthly fee suits a project whose length or scope is uncertain. RICS guidance notes that a percentage of construction cost becomes less reliable as complexity increases, so check what each model does if the cost or programme changes.
c1db3aa5e4e0178a: Does a project manager's fee go up if the contractor overruns?
72ee9dd4f5bd068d: It can. A percentage applied to the final cost rises with the cost, and a monthly fee rises with every extra month. Agree in the appointment whether the percentage is fixed against the accepted tender, whether there is a ceiling, and how extra months caused by others are priced.
61a5a9c26ea95cba: Is VAT charged on project management fees in the UAE?
d6bf0362120bc51f: UAE VAT is charged at the standard rate of 5% on taxable supplies of services unless an exemption or zero rate applies. Ask whether a quoted fee includes or excludes VAT.
4fadec7cf4210670: Does the project manager's fee include the registered consultant's design fee?
919c701470407a79: No. In Dubai, design and the statutory engineering role belong to a registered consultancy, appointed and paid by the owner under its own agreement. A client-side project manager's fee covers representing the owner, not design.

be45753f264ed9c0: Handover · 5 November 2026 · 9 min read · By Philip Chapman
81b78c8f1985bc96: Two different protections apply after handover: the contractual defects liability period (its length is whatever your contract says) and the statutory ten-year decennial liability for collapse and defects that threaten stability or safety.
023de064b61ee996: Decennial liability was in Articles 880 to 883 of the 1985 Civil Transactions Law; the new Civil Transactions Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 25 of 2025) took effect on 1 June 2026, and commentary says it keeps the regime in Articles 821 to 824.
0b9c77213ce6cb0e: Retention is usually released in two parts: some at handover, the rest when the defects period ends and the contract's certificate confirms it. The end of the period is your last real leverage.
217c8d20a6708cbd: Use the first year to test the villa in conditions it has not yet seen: a full summer of air conditioning, the first heavy rain, and months of daily use of every wet area.
91e48468ee12493d: Notify every defect in writing, as your contract requires, with a dated photograph and a grade, and take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on time limits.

932b664c78be07e6: After handover, a UAE villa is protected in two different ways. The contractual defects liability period, whose length your contract sets, covers ordinary defects such as leaks, failed seals and under-performing systems. Separately, the Civil Transactions Law makes the contractor and the engineer jointly liable for ten years for collapse and for defects that threaten the building's stability or safety. The first is where most owners' problems are found and fixed; the second is a backstop for the serious failures.
71d7d3d2a24a5566: This guide explains both, how retention is released, what to test during the first twelve months, how to grade defects, and how to notify them. It does not give legal advice: on time limits and how the law applies to your contract, take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer.
0c4d208fdbba0586: What is the defects liability period?
10113a30420d11d9: The defects liability period is a stretch of time after handover, set by your construction contract, during which the contractor must return to put right defects that appear. FIDIC's 2017 forms call it the defects notification period. Its length is a contractual choice, not a statutory one. Commentary on UAE practice gives twelve months for building works as an example, with mechanical and electrical works usually given longer (Kayrouz & Associates).
b44e753b298ba4ed: It usually starts at handover, which in the contract may be called taking over or practical completion. In Dubai that follows the authority's completion inspection and completion certificate (Dubai Municipality). Check three things in your contract before you accept the keys: how long the period is, whether different parts of the work have different periods, and what notice you must give to require the contractor to return.
4e15ea61e5b314c5: If you are still at the snagging stage, start with our villa snagging checklist. Anything you record and agree at handover should not need to wait for the defects period.
f8e36bc7544a7eb7: What is decennial liability in the UAE?
0df700fd02a4d6bd: Decennial liability is the UAE's statutory ten-year liability for serious building failure. Under the 1985 Civil Transactions Law (official text):
db5da8bd4acc3d12: Article 880 makes the contractor and the engineer jointly liable for ten years for total or partial collapse of the building, and for defects that threaten its stability or safety. The period runs from delivery of the work, which in practice is usually the date in the taking-over certificate (Kayrouz & Associates).
3f6029acdda1cae5: Article 881 limits an engineer who only designed, and did not follow the work on site, to liability for defects in the design.
3152ba63279caa35: Article 882 makes void any clause that tries to exclude or limit this liability. The parties can agree a longer period, not a shorter one.
9a7b25c75c4cbc1b: Article 883 requires a claim to be brought within three years of the collapse or the discovery of the defect. The clock runs from discovery, not from handover.
991db25cda7ef916: Did the 2026 Civil Transactions Law replace these articles?
e837ad0023b66fc3: Yes. Federal Decree-Law No. 25 of 2025 repealed and replaced the 1985 law with effect from 1 June 2026. It does not generally affect transactions concluded before that date unless it expressly says so (Bracewell). So a villa contract signed before June 2026 is generally still governed by Articles 880 to 883.
fae97c9ab771a268: For contracts made from 1 June 2026, commentary says the new law largely keeps the ten-year regime, now in Articles 821 to 824. It refers to the "engineer" rather than the "architect", clarifies joint and several liability, and preserves the contractor's right of recourse against subcontractors and suppliers (Kayrouz & Associates). Other commentary notes that the new law reaffirms joint liability for collapse and expressly keeps decennial rules out of the relationship between the main contractor and its subcontractors (Chambers and Partners). Commentary does not yet settle every detail, including how the three-year claim limit carries over, so check the current text with a UAE-qualified lawyer.
696bfabcadc68d8a: If you bought a completed villa from a developer in a jointly owned property in Dubai, Article 40 of Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019 adds a further layer. The developer is liable for structural defects for ten years from the completion certificate, and for defective mechanical, electrical, sanitary and sewerage installations for one year from handover of the unit (Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019). Whether that law applies to your villa depends on how the community is set up; a lawyer can tell you.
24de98f610be3859: As your contract says; often twelve months for building works
ba1ff02de42b0fc2: Handover, as your contract defines it
0100b4e8608e1863: Collapse; defects threatening stability or safety
2b172b4cb5404380: Civil Transactions Law 1985, arts 880–883; new law arts 821–824 for contracts from 1 June 2026
71ea422cbf4d7396: Collapse or discovery of the defect
9c92a8b47a4d2426: Completion certificate; handover of the unit
4477d524e2b7aaee: Retention is money deducted from each payment to the contractor and held as security for defects. RICS describes the general principle: a portion is released when the works are completed, and the remainder when the defects period has expired and the contract's certificate confirms it (RICS GN 90/2012).
186839aff66e42cb: FIDIC's 2017 forms follow that pattern. Under Sub-Clause 14.9, half of the retention is released when the taking-over certificate is issued and the other half after the last defects notification period expires. The performance certificate follows within 28 days of the end of that period, and the final statement after it; commentary warns that claims left out of the final statement can be lost (Kayrouz & Associates). Some contracts allow a bank guarantee in place of cash retention.
9ce7680cd41fc89b: The practical point is simple. Once the second half of the retention has gone, your leverage on any open defect is a legal claim rather than a payment. Book the end-of-period inspection several weeks before the period ends, so there is time to list, notify and re-inspect.
12fc0e555aa43357: What should you test in the first twelve months?
ae185132b9ba7590: The first year is when a villa meets conditions that were not present at handover. A house handed over in the spring has never run its cooling through a Dubai summer; a house handed over in the summer has never seen heavy rain. Plan the year around those tests.
bee918e34c424124: Every wet area in daily use: showers, baths, basins, kitchen, laundry
a33858eda534cf8d: Slow drains, staining on ceilings below, damp at skirtings, loose or hollow tiles
f5c7af8c2ba7191f: Water tests on terraces, balconies and roofs, if not recorded before handover
8f27e1be7cc3a43a: Water inside at thresholds, sills and corners; ponding on flat roofs
a67abc531f5bfabb: Air conditioning under full summer load, every unit running for a full day
4c0cd07dc7df2654: Rooms that do not hold their set temperature, condensate leaks from ceilings, noisy outdoor units
369a8d30becd9b91: Roofs, gutters, outlets, terraces, basement and site drainage
9ec1a809b5faace9: Blocked outlets, water tracking towards thresholds, damp in basements, standing water in the garden
bd878bbef94ea9c7: Pool level, plant room and pumps
fc0d7a62961059a3: A falling water level, pump noise, leaks in the plant room
71c485c3b1a14b92: Façade sealants, stone and render after a season of heat
9d4baa350c4506a5: Open joints, hairline cracks, staining below sills and copings
169fcb9059bad528: A full re-inspection of the whole villa
042d7550c58eae02: Everything above, plus anything the household has noticed
ff070c99cbefaecd: Rain deserves a plan of its own. In April 2024 more than 250 mm fell in under 24 hours in one area of Al Ain, and the National Centre of Meteorology described the event as exceptional in the UAE's climate record (Khaleej Times). Heavy rain is infrequent, so a roof or terrace detail that fails may not show it until the first storm. When it rains, walk the house that day, photograph what you find, and notify it.
74b0ce4dfa4bdae2: Grade every defect when you report it. The grade tells the contractor what to attend to first and tells you what to hold back. This is our working classification, consistent with the one in our snagging checklist; it is not a legal category, and your contract decides the contractor's obligations.
c81fe0fccd3eef7b: Cracking in structural elements; water coming through a roof, terrace or basement; an electrical safety fault; an insecure balustrade
319850b9e1d93a15: Immediate make-safe, investigation of the cause, a remedy agreed in writing with your registered consultant, and a joint re-inspection. If it may threaten stability or safety, take legal advice early, because decennial liability may be relevant
e46d81089f0da74d: AC that cannot hold temperature in summer; wrong falls to drains or terraces; a pool losing water; failing glazing seals
ed5013a51b3cee54: A written date for the repair, the cause identified rather than the symptom treated, and a re-test under the same conditions
13eb3976289a9b18: Cracked grout, sticking doors, sealant shrinkage, small cracks in paint and plaster from drying out
362eef8f48ec5842: Logged, photographed and batched for a single return visit, closed before the end-of-period inspection
9063fa5826592784: Follow the notice clause in your contract to the letter: who notices go to, in what form, and within what time. As a general practice:
9bcdf6d61d5e2739: Notify in writing, to the address the contract names, with a copy to your registered consultant.
3e2e752030e14c6a: Keep one numbered defects log for the whole villa, with the date found, a photograph, the location, the grade and the date notified.
9f6fd13ea046c14e: Give the contractor access to inspect and repair; most contracts give the contractor the first opportunity to put defects right.
0979dbb5f6c9cf41: Do not engage others to repair a defect at the contractor's cost without checking the contract and taking advice; a misstep can weaken your claim.
feb13907ff8f6ee1: Keep records of every repair visit and re-test.
c49a3e778172b285: On time limits, two things are worth knowing. Contractual notices can have short deadlines, and statutory periods run independently of the contract. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer before any deadline approaches, not after.
d5aeb4f125b8b5f1: The builder's side of the defects period
611891ffa5611daa: We ran the contractor's side of defects periods for two decades. Here is what we saw.
b7288e1d03221f92: By the time the defects period starts, the contractor's site team has usually moved to the next job and the subcontractors have been paid. Every return visit is a cost with no new income attached. On our side, the visits that happened quickly were the ones backed by a clear, graded list and a meaningful sum still held. A stream of individual emails, each describing one item loosely, tended to wait until there were enough items to justify sending a trade.
d83605c0185a5d9f: The end-of-period inspection was always the one that mattered. A client who walked the house properly in month eleven, with a full list, got it closed. A client who called in month thirteen, after the retention had gone, usually got a polite reply and a long wait.
ae493aaf1c5b5997: Handover and the defects period are part of our full client-side service rather than a stand-alone product. On a villa we represent, working alongside your registered consultant and contractor, we keep the defects log, track the contractor's return visits, plan the end-of-period inspection and advise on how retention should be handled commercially. Our snagging and handover page sets out how we work, and our villa construction contracts guide covers the clauses to check before you sign. If your villa is nearing handover or already in its first year, contact us.

3a89eeb697e654de: There is no single statutory period for ordinary defects: the length is set by your construction contract. Commentary on FIDIC-based contracts gives twelve months for building works as an example, with mechanical and electrical works often longer. Separately, decennial liability for collapse and defects that threaten stability or safety runs for ten years under the Civil Transactions Law.

15a448c90c481270: When should retention be released on a villa?
1bfa1ffca647c41c: Follow your contract. A common pattern, used in FIDIC's 2017 forms, releases half of the retention when the works are taken over and the other half after the defects notification period expires. Release nothing early while defects you have notified remain open.

566c22e0aa8b2341: The single point of accountability is real, but the risk it transfers is priced into the tender, and the designer then works for the contractor rather than for you.

4c9b3c5863074c17: Which route is right for your villa?
916335a516607001: Design and build can work well for a Dubai villa, and the argument for it is partly right: one contract does close the gap between designer and builder, and that gap causes many disputes. What it does not do is make the price free of risk, or give you anyone independent checking the design, the price or the payments. If you choose it, the protection comes from what you write into the contract and from who reviews the contractor's work for you.
864361da1ecc884d: This article sets out the two routes fairly, the risks that move between them, and what to put in place if you go with a design-and-build firm. It is general information, not legal advice; take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer before you sign.
9332114cd40bd842: What is the difference between design and build and a separate architect?
ff5ddd9109f03a62: On the traditional, consultant-led route, you appoint a registered engineering consultancy to design the villa. The design is priced by contractors, and you sign a construction contract with the one you choose. The consultant works for you and normally carries the statutory site role during construction. FIDIC's Red Book is written for this arrangement: "building and engineering works where the employer bears the design responsibility" (FIDIC).
465d636800e91893: On the design-and-build route, one firm takes responsibility for both the design and the construction under a single contract. You describe what you want in a set of employer's requirements, the contractor answers with its proposals and a price, and it then develops the design and builds it. FIDIC's Yellow Book is written for this: works "designed by the contractor" (FIDIC). Its Silver Book goes further and puts almost all design and construction risk on the contractor for a fixed price.
52777be39199fca0: In Dubai, one thing does not change between the routes. Under Law No. 14 of 2025, engineering consultancy across the emirate, including free zones, may only be practised by registered offices (Dubai Municipality; Al Tamimi). A design-and-build firm still needs a registered consultancy to design the villa. The question is who appoints it.
315b5a6f09f19841: Where does design and build genuinely help?
9f71aed094026729: It is worth being clear about what integrated firms do well, because the case for them is not empty.
2f3f501a3df1d75e: One contract and one point of responsibility. If the design does not work on site, there is no argument between architect and builder about whose fault it is. The contractor owns both.
2ade8240d7a7def5: Buildability. The people pricing and building the villa shape the design, so details tend to suit the way the contractor works.
1a83418834ea3dae: Speed. Design and procurement can overlap, and some packages can start before every drawing is finished.
eefc7ac917a04cb4: Fewer interfaces for the owner. You manage one relationship instead of two or three.
832faa709fe68fba: On a simple, well-defined villa, with an owner who knows what they want and has the time to follow the job, those advantages can outweigh the drawbacks.
406a415df64165ae: What risk does design and build transfer, and what does it cost?
8f4c083470f265b9: The single point of accountability is real. But risk is never moved for nothing. A contractor that takes on design and coordination risk prices it. A paper published by FIDIC on its Silver Book puts it plainly: a fixed price of this kind "will include contingency allowances to hedge against the risk of things costing more or taking longer", and owners "expect to pay a premium" for it (Hosie, FIDIC). The Silver Book also deems the contractor to have checked the employer's requirements and makes it responsible for their accuracy, with only limited exceptions. That is a large risk, and it is priced accordingly.
961287d53774e2e9: So "costs no more" can be true, and it can be false. It depends on three things:
24212a5694616ff4: How complete your requirements are. Thin requirements leave the contractor free to choose the cheapest compliant answer, and anything better becomes a change.
ad31ff40e3be7d90: How much competition there is. When each bidder prices its own design, the quotes are hard to compare like-for-like, and some owners end up negotiating with one firm.
27dfdbd5cc57e865: How changes are defined. RICS guidance on design and build notes that a contractor developing its own design to build the works or meet statutory requirements is not a change (RICS). Equally, anything you ask for beyond the employer's requirements is. Where that line sits decides who pays.
b7b2ac40c5c8238f: On the contractor's side, we priced design-and-build work in the UK for many years. Our founder, Philip Chapman, ran P Chapman Construction for 21 years. The first thing we read was the employer's requirements, and the thinner they were, the more room there was to make margin through design choices the client would never see. That is not dishonest. It is how a fixed price with design risk works, and owners should go in knowing it.
16906425faae14bd: This is the honest weakness of the route. Under design and build, the designer works for the contractor. RICS guidance says the employer's representative under a design-and-build contract is "not responsible for and not required to approve drawings or design development", and must not interfere with the contractor's control of its design team (RICS). The same guidance notes that some employers keep a "shadow" design team, such as an architect or engineer, to support them through the project.
44e722b2bdeb1794: In practice you have three ways to keep the design honest:
8867ea7358723415: Keep your own registered consultant to review the contractor's design against your requirements, the Dubai Building Code and your budget. This costs a fee, but it gives you a designer who works for you.
ca20eb5cc9544c8a: Write review periods into the contract, so that design packages come to you for comment before work proceeds. Make it "review and comment" rather than approval, so the contractor's design responsibility stays where it belongs.
a1bfbbf67bcde89f: Have an owner's representative review the commercial side: specification changes, value engineering proposals, allowances and the effect of each design decision on cost and programme.
2ad863f5d9624ad0: Over-design is a risk on any route, not only this one. In August 2025 Dubai Municipality warned consultancies that some villa structural designs went beyond the Dubai Building Code's safety requirements without a proven need, raising construction costs (Gulf News). Under design and build the incentive usually runs the other way, towards the leanest compliant design. Either way, someone on your side should be asking why.
e8b426160da79f10: Who checks what under each route?
aee9287296c34c17: The table below shows the typical arrangement on a private villa. Contracts vary, and in Dubai a registered consultancy designs the villa and holds the statutory role on every route.
aa0f21cf0652ef12: Usually the owner alone, comparing totals
b5f0faebf5cfda22: The owner, unless an adviser is appointed; bids on different designs are hard to compare
9b3220bd43f9428e: The consultant, against its own drawings and specification
50a0dba938f0a6bd: Reviews the quote line by line and compares bids like-for-like; the owner decides

0420116163b4ffc7: Priced by the contractor; "design development" claims are argued by the owner
d42053f0a974804a: Assessed by the consultant under the contract

d361f5e397dad91c: The contractor's team and the consultancy it appoints

9a4cb2b4acdc3a10: Observes and records on site, and raises concerns for the registered consultant to confirm

4f75e1b2275590cd: What should you put in a design-and-build contract?
4ce193192f65a56e: If you choose design and build, these are the points we would want settled before signing. Dubai Municipality's guidance contract forms for private villas, in Arabic, are a sensible baseline, and a UAE-qualified lawyer should review any amendments.
5c179d545ae2301b: Detailed employer's requirements. Room schedule, finishes, systems, performance standards and the budget for allowances. If you want the villa to be fit for a stated purpose, say so in writing. Al Tamimi notes that under UAE law there is no implied term that a contract must be fit for purpose, and that a contractor may meet its obligation by exercising reasonable care unless the contract says otherwise (Al Tamimi). The same article notes that most professional indemnity policies only cover negligence, which limits what a strict obligation is worth in practice.
d6ddfda493a18a37: Order of precedence. Which document wins if the employer's requirements and the contractor's proposals disagree.
334cc58dd6b13af6: Design submissions and review periods. What comes to you, when, and how long you have to comment.
d7a4ba17a327ef66: The registered consultancy. Who appoints it, who pays it, and whether it will owe you a duty directly.
d709001e95a7ea21: A clear definition of a change, separating design development, which is the contractor's cost, from changes you instruct, which are yours.
54bfe0a83d9efdcc: Listed provisional sums and allowances, each with a figure and a rule for how it is adjusted.
b33fabffc1f857d1: A payment schedule tied to work done, not to design milestones that let money run ahead of progress, with retention and bonds defined.
cc70b29610ce9d42: A licence to use the drawings if the contract ends early, so you can finish the villa with someone else.
51f3a6133b5ae2ec: Handover documents: as-built drawings, warranties, manuals and authority completion paperwork.
8ea37e83f980456e: Design and build does not change the law on structural safety. UAE civil law makes the contractor and the architect or engineer who oversaw the works jointly liable for ten years for collapse or defects that threaten the building's stability, and that liability cannot be excluded by contract (Al Tamimi). The new Civil Transactions Law that took effect on 1 June 2026 keeps this regime, according to commentary (Legal 500). See decennial liability in our glossary, and our guide to villa construction contracts in the UAE for variations, delays and payment.
cc31af026f7034f3: Using a design-and-build contractor? What an owner's representative still does
85f0e4c0eff61301: An in-house project manager at a design-and-build firm may be very good. But they report to the firm's owner, and their job is to deliver the contract the firm signed. That is not a criticism; it is the structure. Nobody in it is paid to ask whether you are getting value.
6f2929d33ee3b4f1: Alongside a design-and-build contractor, a client-side project manager:
4691cd64c41d7c1a: reviews the employer's requirements before tender, so the gaps are closed while they are cheap to close
84de3d7a7b8a0a03: runs or benchmarks the tender, so you can compare bids that rest on different designs
7ad2050b44409639: reviews payment applications against progress seen on site, and recommends what to pay
7425addfa6e05f4f: reviews variations and design development claims against the contract, and keeps the register
750b3d988b76d433: owns the decision log, so every choice you make is recorded with its cost and programme effect

1880f0a5e0f99fbd: It does not redesign the villa, manage the contractor's team or instruct the contractor; you remain the one who instructs. If the villa is simple and you can follow it closely yourself, you may not need this at all. On a bespoke villa, or when you live abroad, it is usually where the value is.
df69da823f3cc35c: Which route is right for your villa?
cb83f33508394243: Design and build tends to suit a villa with a clear, well-defined brief, a conventional specification and an owner who wants speed and one contract. A separate architect tends to suit a bespoke villa, a design you want to own and shape, or a site with unusual constraints, where you want a designer who works only for you. Either can work. What decides the outcome is whether someone independent is checking the price, the payments and the changes. For choosing the firm itself, see how to choose a villa contractor in Dubai.
88a804fd9ced268f: We sit on the owner's side of either route. We can review a design-and-build proposal and contract before you sign, help you compare bids like-for-like, and then review payments and variations through the build, working alongside your registered consultant and the contractor. 72dc763f43774093: Is design and build cheaper than using a separate architect and contractor?
93af98e475674fec: Not necessarily. Design and build can save time and some coordination cost, but the contractor prices the design and coordination risk it takes on. A paper published by FIDIC notes that a fixed price carrying this much risk includes contingency allowances, and that owners should expect to pay a premium for it. Whether it costs more or less depends on how well your requirements are defined and how much competition there is at tender.
849886b68d31cd2e: Who checks the design in a design-and-build villa contract?
a1fce99407baba37: Unless you arrange otherwise, the contractor's own design team, including the registered consultancy it appoints. Your options are to keep your own registered consultant to review the contractor's design, to write review periods into the contract, and to have an owner's representative review cost, programme and specification changes for you.
4e92d3eec0b65e2f: Does design and build remove decennial liability?
b12a32c3bfecb6a3: No. UAE civil law makes the contractor and the architect or engineer jointly liable for ten years for collapse or defects that threaten a building's stability, and commentators agree it cannot be excluded by contract. A new Civil Transactions Law took effect on 1 June 2026 and law-firm commentary says it keeps this regime. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on your contract.
b508dcbbb67056a9: Can I use an owner's representative with a design-and-build firm?
af2de17f9ee35ee6: Yes. The owner's representative does not redesign or manage the contractor's team. It reviews the employer's requirements and the price, checks payment applications against progress, reviews variations and claims of design development, and reports only to you. The design and statutory roles stay with the registered consultancy.
d3d112d2378a8532: Is the FIDIC Yellow Book used for private villas?
f9d63bdfca75f0c9: FIDIC forms are written for larger projects and are not standard for private villas, but they set out clearly how design responsibility moves between the parties. c8b1a8d10b40e996: A villa building permit in Dubai is applied for online by your registered engineering consultant, not by you. The consultant submits the drawings and fees through the unified building permit window to Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits; service-authority NOCs are gathered through the same system; and the permit is issued with stamped drawings. The owner's part is to appoint the team, provide the plot documents, approve a design that is genuinely finished, and pay the fees on time.
216fbd50d4e2b691: Who issues villa building permits in Dubai?
158b583ba8e8eaec: Three authorities issue building permits for private villas in Dubai: Dubai Municipality, Trakhees and the Dubai Development Authority. Which one applies depends on where your plot sits, and your consultant will confirm it at the start; our guide to which Dubai authority covers your villa explains why it follows the plot, not the community.
244a472d4879d8a0: Since 2022, building permits across Dubai Municipality, the Dubai Development Authority, Trakhees and DIEZ have run through a single unified e-window, with Civil Defence, RTA, DEWA, Etisalat and du linked in (Dubai Municipality). In October 2023 Dubai Municipality launched the Build in Dubai platform, which covers the whole life of a project: land, design, permits, construction, completion, connection and later alterations (Dubai Media Office). The Dubai Building Permits app was relaunched in August 2024 with a registry and ratings for consultants and contractors.
095ca8d195ea09a0: Designs are checked against the Dubai Building Code, whose 2021 edition has a dedicated part for villas (Part K). In practice that means the code, not a reviewing engineer's preference, is the yardstick your drawings are measured against.
3ed54f49c8379771: The sequence below follows Dubai Municipality's published procedure for residential buildings, with the master-developer step that applies in most private villa communities. Other authorities follow a similar logic with their own portals.
04dfae3b5a6a3a72: Affection plan, master-developer guidelines and site constraints reviewed; consultant appointed
a9bcb40b040e04ac: Signs consultancy agreement, provides title and plot documents
84bf83d2be5a8c9d: Layout, massing and areas fixed; optional initial design concept approval
1bde0db7f788b36e: Signs developer forms, pays developer fees
f184b7ae8b0ebef2: Architectural, structural, MEP, insulation, drainage and civil defence drawings
ac296d7bfa9848bf: Answers design questions, freezes the layout
761eae18b69dd76d: Drawings, building card details and fees submitted online
75e57dd3ba1ae0cf: DEWA, Civil Defence, telecoms and others review through the unified window
0774505d1923483f: Usually nothing, unless a design change is needed
f1fcaefb48ec7f33: Permit and stamped drawings issued, printable online
4dd607df17526894: Checks the permit matches the design you approved
a78c5e608135ca56: Hoarding, excavation, shoring and piling, then the building itself
ef95adb894ef9925: Contractor, under the consultant's statutory role
91b039b02e20f7af: Shoring, foundations, slabs and similar stages inspected
67f5a9246e0091c2: Keeps decisions on time so inspections are not missed
6edb589d202a808a: Joint completion inspection, completion certificate, service connection
91b81ea57d8b5eee: Steps 5 to 10 follow Dubai Municipality's residential procedure. The document list in step 4 and the step 5 detail come from Dubizzle's guide to the new building permit; the site preparation permit in step 8 is described below.
d0a2e0232a02cdcf: What does the consultant actually submit?
4eb5e6c90292e82a: For a new villa, the submission covers architecture, structure, electromechanical systems, insulation and drainage, road layouts and civil defence, together with building card details and fees, through the Dubai Building Permits System (Dubizzle). Your consultant may also choose to seek an initial design concept approval before the final design; Dubizzle describes this as optional, a preliminary check of the architecture against codes and planning standards that does not allow work to start.
0857c9ffe95bb4d0: Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, engineering consultancy in Dubai, including in free zones, may only be practised by registered firms (Law No. 14 of 2025). That is why the submission sits with your consultant. It is also why the quality of the consultant you appoint has more effect on your permit timeline than anything the authority does.
2205efcadeb88fb4: The owner does not prepare drawings or make the technical submission, but the owner's signature and documents sit underneath all of it. In our experience, the owner's side typically covers:
3ba25bc69160e116: The consultant's appointment. Dubai Municipality publishes standard contract forms for consultancy and construction on private villas, in Arabic, which are a sensible baseline. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer before signing.
ef9a1125d3826b24: Proof of ownership and plot documents. Title deed, affection plan and any master-developer agreement or conditions attached to the plot.
b93a696119657117: Master-developer forms. In master communities the developer's NOC application normally needs the owner's authorisation and fees.
296939cf80a6dbbc: Design approval. A written sign-off of the drawings that will be submitted. This is the signature that matters most, because every change after it costs time.
de92fadb453c64b7: Fees. Authority, developer and service-authority fees. Optimal Engineering puts a Dubai Municipality building permit at AED 15,000–60,000 for a standard villa, a permanent DEWA connection at AED 10,000–40,000, and authority approvals in total at AED 80,000–250,000.
8072d31147ed250d: The construction contract. Signed with the contractor you choose, ideally on a design that has already been permitted.
fa1bd81bdec17266: Your consultant will confirm the exact list for your authority and community. Ask for it in writing at appointment, with a date against each item.
4be328d303002686: How long does a Dubai villa permit take?
e72640dae62cf524: There are two honest answers, and a range between them. Dubizzle's guide says it typically takes around three working days to get a building permit once a complete application is in the system. Optimal Engineering allows 4–8 weeks for approvals on a straightforward project, and a property information website puts the whole approvals stage at 2–3 months.
c40574eead954d1d: The gap between those figures is the real story. Three working days describes a single clean decision. Two to three months describes what usually happens around it: master-developer review, service-authority NOCs, comments to answer, drawings to revise and resubmit, and owner decisions that arrive late. For how the permit fits into the whole build, see how long it takes to build a villa in Dubai.
94ef90eba646e344: Two recent changes point to faster decisions. In August 2026 Dubai Municipality announced an AI system to assess permit applications for private and investment villas against the Dubai Building Code, with a 26-week rollout in three stages: development and testing, a pilot with selected consultancy firms, then rollout to villa applications through Build in Dubai (Dubai Media Office). It was announced as a project to be implemented, not a service already live. Separately, since October 2025, Dubai Municipality has accredited engineering consultancies to issue self-build permits for Emirati citizens' villas without prior review by municipal engineers. Neither removes the need for a complete, coordinated design. An automated check is quicker to say no, too.
a3eb14d81a812a94: How long is a building permit valid?
3ccc587a58cefe77: Dubizzle's guide says a Dubai Municipality building permit is valid for six months from issue and can be renewed. Treat that as a reason to time the permit sensibly against contractor selection. A permit obtained long before you have a contractor ready can lapse, and a renewal is one more task on a programme that already has enough.
12ecbb9116d88606: Can work start before the building permit?
fced98620e9f139a: Early works run under their own permit. Dubai Municipality's site preparation permit covers hoarding, excavation, shoring and piling. It is applied for by the consultant through Build in Dubai, and the shoring and excavation application needs a soil test report, structural drawings and calculations for excavation, shoring and foundations, and third-party insurance. Dubizzle reports that it is valid for six months from issue.
77538077f1e686c7: On a programme-critical plot, especially one with a basement, using this route well can save weeks. It only works if the ground investigation was commissioned early, which is an owner's decision, not the consultant's.
a3493d8cc0e1a852: Where do villa permit programmes slip?
92a4f21835aa2527: From the builder's side, we saw the same pattern for two decades. The programme we were given assumed the permit would arrive on a date; the permit arrived later; and the reasons were almost never the authority's. Our founder, Philip Chapman, ran P Chapman Construction in the UK for 21 years. The regulators were different, but the causes of permit delay are much the same in any jurisdiction.
6eb341b890fec192: A design submitted before it was finished. When an owner is impatient, the temptation is to submit and resolve the detail later. Comments come back, the drawings change, and the resubmission takes longer than finishing the design would have. The fastest submissions we saw were the ones held back a fortnight to close out coordination.
ae57ff53a8d2d749: Changes after design sign-off. Moving a wall, adding a basement room or enlarging a terrace after submission can mean revised structural calculations, a new master-developer review and a fresh round of NOCs. What looks like a small change on the owner's side is a resubmission on the consultant's.
ae7756c6c23ce50d: An over-designed structure. In August 2025 Dubai Municipality warned villa engineering consultancies about over-designing structures and inflating construction costs (Gulf News). Over-design does not only cost money; it is often the reason a tender comes back over budget, the design is cut back, and the drawings go round again.
9bd8cdb2e86c6c90: The master developer treated as a formality. Developer guidelines on heights, setbacks, materials and colours are specific, and a design that ignores them is returned before the authority ever sees it.
a898a6dd83f2d670: Ground information arriving late. No soil report means no shoring design, and no shoring design means no site preparation permit. Commission the ground investigation as soon as the plot is secure.
dce9c42f79fcf0f2: The contractor appointed too late. The contractor needs to be registered and insured before works can start under the permit. A permit with no contractor ready is a permit ticking towards its expiry date.
601280ac71f6e7af: On the contractor's side, the first thing we checked on any new job was whether the permit drawings and the tender drawings were the same set. Surprisingly often they were not. Every difference between the two became a variation, and every variation became a conversation about time.
ad8d590b349f0737: How do you keep the permit stage on track?
a36067251f6eafae: Three habits make the most difference.
94b885165b63c363: Fix the brief before design starts. A written brief with rooms, areas, a basement decision and a budget is the cheapest document in the project to change. Our guide to what it costs to build a villa in Dubai helps set the budget honestly.
b8fbc70114637235: Ask for an approvals tracker. One page, updated weekly: what has been submitted, to whom, on what date, what comments are outstanding and who owes the next action. If your consultant cannot produce it, that tells you something.
47278436d9f2fc6b: Plan the contractor in parallel. Run contractor selection while the permit is in progress, on the permit drawings, so that the contract is signed shortly after the permit is issued. Our guide to choosing a villa contractor in Dubai covers what to compare, and how to build a villa in Dubai sets the permit within the full journey from plot to keys.
a37cbf972db285f2: If you are planning a renovation or extension rather than a new build, the same authorities apply, but the route starts with an alteration application; our guide to renovating a Palm Jumeirah villa shows how a Nakheel NOC fits ahead of the permit.
5674cacaca8d38ea: We represent the owner through design and approvals, alongside your DM-registered consultant, who prepares and submits the drawings. We help you write the brief, review the design against your budget before it is submitted, and keep an approvals tracker so you always know what is waiting and on whom. Our design and approvals management service explains how we work. To talk through your plot and programme, contact us.

8b79eead0409383b: How can you shorten the time to build a villa?
532b880de4666aec: A custom villa in Dubai typically takes 12–24 months from plot to keys, and 24–36 months for a custom luxury villa, according to a property information website. Construction itself is usually 8–14 months; the rest goes on design, approvals, choosing a contractor and handover. On most projects the months that are lost are lost on paper, before and during the build, not in the concrete and blockwork.
1d5962a46f196d17: That last point is the one owners rarely hear. What follows is where the time actually goes, which steps you can shorten and which you cannot.
0eeead9c98a197ef: Here is the full journey, with published durations where they exist and our own planning allowances where they do not.
096c87e109d1ec2d: Sum of phases above, end to end
7d9d8e6c2dff5b12: The phase durations come from a property information website, the only phase-by-phase breakdown we have found published. Industry sources broadly agree on the whole: Engel & Völkers says most villas take 12–24 months from approval to completion, and Optimal Engineering allows 4–8 weeks for approvals on a straightforward project and typically 12–18 months for construction.
e231257e835d529e: The published 12–24 months is shorter than the phases added end to end because it assumes some of them overlap. Two things stand out. First, roughly a third to a half of the elapsed time passes before anyone breaks ground. Second, the phases are not fixed blocks. A well-run project overlaps some of them, for example by preparing the bid package while approvals are in progress. A poorly run one stretches each of them, usually because a decision is waiting on someone.
7f9d877251032de0: For the step-by-step sequence and who does what at each stage, see our guide on how to build a villa in Dubai.
6f9705a83a65c1a5: Where do the months actually go?
fc4265d2cd806213: On paper, a villa programme looks like a construction programme with some design at the front. In reality, the critical path runs through information for most of the project.
653838eb87b67400: Design. Three to four months is realistic for a resolved design across architecture, structure and MEP. It is not realistic if the brief is still moving. Every change to room sizes, a basement or the façade sends the design back a step, and each step means redrawing, recoordinating and, later, repricing.
c1dc223f31248a4e: Approvals. The permit comes from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits, and the service-authority NOCs are now gathered through one online window. In a master-planned community, the master developer's own design review and NOC usually comes first, and that review can take longer than the permit.
0bf0fb905293827f: Bidding. Inviting bids, answering bidder questions, comparing returns like-for-like and negotiating the contract takes weeks, not days. Rushing it is a false economy, because the months you save here are often lost in variations and disputes later.
540fe667dae93227: Construction. This is where owners expect the time to go, and where it is easiest to see. It is also where earlier slippage surfaces, because late design information shows up as stoppages on site.
004b948aab1710c9: Handover. The building can be physically complete weeks before you can live in it. Dubai Municipality's residential procedure describes a joint completion inspection, the completion certificate and then service connection. Snagging runs in parallel.
82af31ca214b6136: From the contractor's side, we could usually tell within the first two months whether a job would finish on time. It was rarely the ground or the weather that told us. It was how quickly the client and the design team answered questions.
0485f9f91335b632: How long does a villa building permit take in Dubai?
6920f9e5e3a83038: Once the drawings are right, the permit itself is not usually the slow part. In August 2026 Dubai Municipality announced that it is developing an AI system to issue villa permits automatically, to be piloted and then rolled out in phases through Build in Dubai (Dubai Media Office); it is not yet the standard route. The months go on preparing a compliant submission, master-developer review and rounds of comments; our guide to the Dubai villa building permit sets out each step and where programmes slip. Abu Dhabi has moved the same way with its Binaa platform; see our Abu Dhabi villa permit guide.
40d0842e5050d262: How long does villa construction take, stage by stage?
43a4a0bf35a6674c: Published guidance puts construction at 8–14 months. The table below is our own rule of thumb for how that time is typically spread on a two-storey villa without a basement. Stages overlap, so the durations do not simply add up.
627bff70a005b65c: Ground conditions, water table, any basement
10c7b65257026d84: Number of floors, spans, authority inspections
881fe22402a6628e: MEP first fix and internal walls
307feceb0a3874e0: Add a basement and the substructure stage can easily double. Dubai Municipality's procedure refers to staged inspections, such as shoring, foundations and slabs, so each structural milestone also carries a short wait for inspection, which a good programme allows for.
64ed89d6b51182fb: Does the summer slow construction in Dubai?
78f7546a313c1eea: It changes the working day. The UAE midday break, run by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, bans outdoor work under direct sunlight from 12:30pm to 3pm every day between 15 June and 15 September. 2026 was its 22nd consecutive year. Exemptions include concrete pours and asphalt laying where the work cannot be interrupted (Khaleej Times).
8151c2fbb1006667: Contractors adapt with early starts, shaded work areas and by shifting internal trades into the hottest months. Even so, three months of shortened outdoor days, combined with heat and humidity, reduce output on structural and external work. In our view, a programme that shows the same weekly progress in August as in January has not been thought through. Ask the contractor how the summer is reflected in its programme, and which activities it plans to do then.
41dc6d26c8a1c893: What makes a villa build take longer?
8893f16468491550: In our experience, these are the usual culprits, roughly in order of how often we saw them:
cd3970b8ef8ab7c8: Late owner decisions. Tiles, sanitaryware, joinery and automation chosen after the programme needs them. The delay is the owner's, and so is the cost.
eb5f86930c96abf2: Design changes after the permit. Moving walls or adding floor area can mean resubmission and lost months.
5aa6c0e3a89e7d4c: Long-lead items ordered late. Large-format or structural glazing, imported stone, bespoke joinery, lifts and specialist cooling equipment can take months to arrive. If they are not ordered early, the programme waits for them.
db5a1ffd1b3c2562: Basements and difficult ground. Waterfront and reclaimed plots in particular can need shoring and dewatering that add weeks before the frame begins.
9d492bf7e6b90c2c: Slow answers to site questions. Each request for information from the contractor that waits a fortnight is a fortnight someone can claim.
545de41fd393f3c3: Contractor resources and cash flow. A contractor stretched across too many sites, or short of cash, slows down quietly. A valuation running ahead of physical progress is an early warning.
e36a4a49498e6d08: The end of the job. Commissioning, completion inspections, connections and snagging are often under-planned, and the last 5% of the work takes a disproportionate share of the time.
aaa7d07de436410c: On the contractor's side, we always planned the programme so that the client's decisions sat on the critical path. That is not sharp practice; it is how programmes are drawn. It does mean that any late owner decision becomes immediate, claimable delay. We explain how float works in what a builder knows that most villa owners don't.
42f2148a2c3993a3: Why does delay cost so much?
879b3c71fc6ef282: Because many of the contractor's site costs are time-related. Turner & Townsend's 2025 UAE market intelligence puts contractor preliminaries in Dubai at 12% of construction cost on a 2,500 m² project, and 14% on a 50,000 m² one (Turner & Townsend). Those costs are priced per week or per month, so every extra month on site carries its own cost before any additional work is done. Add the owner's own costs, such as rent elsewhere, finance and currency exposure, and a three-month overrun becomes a significant line in the budget. Our guide to what it costs to build a villa in Dubai sets out the full budget.
3315c492e81fbfb5: How can you shorten the time to build a villa?
f4326ce425687263: You cannot compress concrete curing or authority inspections. You can remove most of the waiting around them.
4fe9881403dc0772: Fix the brief before design starts. The cheapest month to change your mind is the first one.
5660e0459e2681ce: Finish the design before pricing. A complete design gives real bids, fewer provisional sums and fewer stoppages on site.
514c40b1632adb1f: Overlap where it is safe. Prepare the bid package while approvals run, rather than after.
fd6aaf410e77600c: Order long-lead items early. Identify them during design and agree when each must be ordered.
5faf29d95638c90d: Agree a decision schedule. List every owner decision with the latest date it can be made, and have the contractor confirm those dates against its programme.
4e455236f05eed0c: Test the programme at bid stage. An unusually short programme with low preliminaries is often a claim waiting to happen.
fd30fe258eb03382: Review progress monthly against the programme, not just the payments. Small slippage is easy to recover in month three and very hard in month eleven.
d38f6b5d8b1b8c0a: Plan the end early. Commissioning, inspections, connections and snagging should be on the programme from the start.
286293ffa9195ea1: If you are building from abroad, decision speed matters even more. Our guide to building a villa in Dubai from the UK covers how to keep approvals moving across time zones.
4ed7a2b2678c666c: We represent the owner, alongside your DM-registered consultant and your contractor. Our founder, Philip Chapman, ran P Chapman Construction for 21 years, so we read a contractor's programme the way a builder does: where the float sits, what is on the critical path and what will be claimed if it slips. Our cost and programme control service helps you set a realistic timeline, keep decisions ahead of the programme and track progress independently. To talk through your plot and timeline, contact us.
