26df0a2d0d9825de: Does the summer slow down villa construction in Dubai?
67eccca95447b6bd: It changes how sites work. The UAE midday break bans outdoor work under direct sunlight from 12:30pm to 3pm between 15 June and 15 September, with exemptions such as concrete pours that cannot be interrupted. Contractors adjust shift patterns, but a realistic programme allows for fewer productive outdoor hours in summer.
66f6cb5ce94010a9: How long does construction take once the contractor starts on site?
d6bb8e8c7087262d: Published guidance puts construction at 8–14 months for a villa in Dubai; Optimal Engineering says typically 12–18 months. A large luxury villa with a basement, structural glazing and bespoke finishes will usually sit at or beyond the top of that range.

87deacce473a452c: To build a villa in Dubai you check the plot, set a brief and budget, appoint a registered consultant to design it, secure master-developer and authority approvals, choose a contractor, build, then complete inspections, connect services and hand over. A property information website puts the whole journey at 12–24 months from plot to keys, and 24–36 months for a custom luxury villa. The owner appoints every party and makes every key decision; the order in which those decisions are made decides most of the cost.
e3d2ff268dd5cf11: What are the stages of building a villa in Dubai?
cda73b008065a95b: The process is well defined. Dubai Municipality's "Building in Dubai" platform, launched in October 2023, covers the whole life of a project: land, design, permits, construction, completion, connection and later alterations. Since 2022, building permits across Dubai Municipality, the Dubai Development Authority, Trakhees and DIEZ go through a single unified e-window, with Civil Defence, RTA, DEWA, Etisalat and du linked in.
877c3b216ca85079: Durations without a label are from a property information website, the only phase-by-phase breakdown we have found published; Engel & Völkers, for comparison, says most villas take 12–24 months from approval to completion. The others are our own planning allowances and depend heavily on the owner's speed of decision. For a closer look at where those months go, see how long it takes to build a villa in Dubai.
4f73135fd39f3f0e: Stage 1: Check the plot before you commit
e4aac1c5fc4276ea: Before you buy, or before you design on a plot you already own, establish what can be built on it. That means the plot affection plan, the master developer's design guidelines, setbacks, height and coverage limits, existing utility connections, access, and any outstanding service charges or developer conditions. Ground conditions and the water table matter too; a basement on a waterfront plot is a very different exercise from one inland.
df3014e9ed175cd6: Who does what: the owner commissions the checks; the consultant interprets planning and design constraints; a UAE-qualified lawyer should review title and any developer agreements. Our guide to plot checks in Dubai goes through them in detail.
e848505fc5727e2e: Stage 2: Set the brief and the budget
9b39691aba5816c3: The brief is the most valuable document in the project and the cheapest to change. Bedrooms, basement or not, pool, staff quarters, home automation, the level of finish, how you will live in the house. Write it down and attach a budget built from the full cost picture, not just a rate per square foot. Our article on what it costs to build a villa in Dubai sets out every line.
2ad87740a592c1cf: Stage 3: Appoint your consultant and design the villa
69e3f3f90b842b71: Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, engineering consultancy in Dubai, including in free zones, may only be practised by registered firms (Law No. 14 of 2025). Your consultant designs the villa across architecture, structure and MEP, prepares the drawings for approval, and normally carries the statutory site role during construction. Dubai Municipality publishes standard contract forms for consultancy and construction on private villas, in Arabic, which are a useful baseline.
0d67345cd19f5db5: The BPS app, relaunched in August 2024, includes a registry and ratings for consultants and contractors, and is worth checking before you appoint. Design normally runs from concept through to detailed design. Every hour spent resolving detail at this stage is cheaper than any hour spent resolving it on site.
acd3e8accf44aaa3: Stage 4: Master-developer NOC and building permit
e18f42899eee3f3e: In a master-planned community, the master developer reviews the design against its guidelines and issues its NOC (no objection certificate). In Nakheel communities, for example, renovation and extension approvals begin with a Nakheel NOC application through its portal before the authority permit.
b87adad7e8de5689: The authority permit then runs through Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits. Under Dubai Municipality's published villa procedure, the consultant submits the drawings and fees online, the service-authority NOCs are issued through the unified window, and the permit is issued with stamped drawings (Dubai Municipality). In August 2026, Dubai Municipality announced that it is developing an AI system to check villa applications against the Dubai Building Code, to be piloted with selected consultancies and then rolled out in phases through Build in Dubai over 26 weeks (Dubai Media Office). Until that rollout is complete, plan on the current review process. In practice, cleaner drawings should mean fewer rounds of comments. Our guide to Dubai villa building permits sets out each step, what the owner signs and where the permit stage slips.
3b3e29052ab00dc2: Who does what: the consultant prepares and submits; the master developer and authority review and approve; the owner pays fees and answers design questions quickly.
6b6b28c8699cdf4c: Run a competitive process on a complete design. Your consultant normally prepares the bid package; you, as owner, decide who is invited and who is appointed. Compare bids like-for-like: scope, exclusions, provisional sums, preliminaries, programme, payment terms and retention. The lowest number is not automatically the lowest cost. Our guide to choosing a villa contractor in Dubai explains what to look for, and our guide to villa construction contracts covers the agreement itself. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer before signing.
78f49084b1837dbd: The contractor mobilises, builds and manages the site. The authority inspects at defined stages; Dubai Municipality's procedure refers to staged inspections such as shoring, foundations and slabs. Your consultant fulfils the statutory site role. Monthly valuations measure work done, and you pay against them.
4e6610437dbd8acb: The owner's job during construction is to make decisions on time, approve samples and mock-ups, and keep an independent view of cost and programme. On the contractor's side, we always knew which clients read the monthly report and which did not. The ones who did not were the ones whose sites drifted.
ea5460d38cdac5ba: At the end, Dubai Municipality's procedure describes a joint completion inspection involving Building Control, Survey, telecoms and Civil Defence where needed, followed by the completion certificate and service connection. In parallel, the villa is snagged, defects are listed and rectified, operating manuals and warranties are handed over, and the defects liability period begins. Our villa snagging checklist covers what to inspect.
4184fb9bedaf4d91: Who does what on a Dubai villa build?
3b226a2104cea1bc: Owner: sets the brief and budget, appoints every party, makes decisions, pays.
3a87657461596dff: Owner's representative: represents the owner commercially and practically; cost and programme control, independent site visits and reporting, bid comparison, change control.
328232ebe0acfc80: registered consultant: designs, prepares approval drawings, carries the statutory technical role.
3adaf4b2a6a960d0: Contractor: builds, manages the site, its subcontractors and its programme.
714ea0f97c62f1c1: Master developer: enforces community guidelines and issues its NOC.
fba589c996364d36: Authority: Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits; issues the permit, inspects and issues completion.
f3ce48bdca56dead: How those roles differ, and where they overlap, is covered in owner's representative vs project manager vs consultant.
1436febc0ed78d02: Which decisions cost the most if made late?
2198a914ec5c7f7f: In our experience, these are the decisions that are cheap at design stage and expensive afterwards:
056627216884b190: Basement or no basement. It changes structure, waterproofing, shoring, excavation and programme. Adding one late is effectively a redesign.
714fe8e8945f7253: Overall size and layout. Moving walls after the permit can mean resubmission and lost months.
cd91992e8055b6cd: Glazing and openings. Large-format and structural glazing has long lead times and drives the structure around it.
f13351fba7036b21: MEP strategy. Cooling, home automation, AV and lighting control need their routes and plant space designed in. Adding them later means chasing walls and ceilings.
b744f42c7d7b1af8: Pool and external works. These interact with structure, drainage and levels.
c8dfd0d924572b9d: Finishes and specification. Stone, joinery and sanitaryware chosen late are usually priced as variations, without competition.
126434aa33d3c496: From the builder's side, a late change was rarely a problem for the contractor. It was an opportunity. That is not cynicism, just how the commercial model works.
f0eb62c90428fab3: How do you keep a villa build on programme?
e988fcc181cd18ed: Most delay on a private villa is not caused by bad weather or a shortage of labour. In our experience it comes from information: drawings that arrive late, samples that sit unapproved, questions from site that wait a fortnight for an answer. Three habits make the biggest difference.
01b52dde5d80f264: Agree a decision schedule at the start. List every choice the owner has to make, from tiles to door handles to automation scenes, with the latest date each can be made without holding up the work. Ask the contractor to confirm the dates against its programme.
aa1ea13e1c36490c: Answer site questions quickly. Every request for information from the contractor should have a named person responsible and a target response time. Unanswered questions turn into delay claims.
d4f6a06f5e7a3619: Review progress against the programme monthly, not just against payments. A valuation tells you what has been paid for. The programme tells you whether the villa will be finished when you expect. Both need reading together.
61d8ef2c9a461d62: If you are building from abroad, these habits matter even more, because decisions made by email across time zones take longer. Our guide to building a villa in Dubai from the UK covers how to set this up.
3da501a47fd66188: We sit on the owner's side through every stage, working alongside your registered consultant and your contractor. We help you set the brief and budget, compare bids and choose, then provide independent client-side site visits and progress reporting through to handover. Our villa construction project management service covers the whole journey, and if you are overseas, see our overseas owners page. To talk through your plot, contact us.
4e648bd1206a3510: A property information website puts design at 3–4 months, approvals at 2–3 months, construction at 8–14 months and snagging at 1–2 months, giving 12–24 months from plot to keys, or 24–36 months for a custom luxury villa. Engel & Völkers says most villas take 12–24 months from approval to completion.
4c8eca73e3bee6d1: Who applies for the building permit in Dubai?
cb4aaaf794d40f82: Your registered consultant (or in some cases the contractor) submits drawings and fees online through the unified permit window. The owner appoints the consultant and signs off the design, but does not usually make the technical submission.
322c008edbaa9cad: Do I need the master developer's approval before the authority permit?
ef71f2bd1d37fb9a: In master-planned communities, the developer's design guidelines and NOC normally come first. In Nakheel communities, for example, renovation and extension approvals start with a Nakheel NOC application through its portal before the authority permit.
498caa7e0ce810c2: Can I build a villa in Dubai while living overseas?
618731f7e837eb36: Yes, many owners do. It works best when decision-making is planned, with regular reporting and a clear schedule of the choices you need to make and when.

1021ec225f0b0795: To choose a villa contractor in Dubai, first confirm each bidder is properly registered using official sources, then compare prices only on the same drawings and specification, with preliminaries, provisional sums and exclusions set out side by side. After that, judge the people who will actually run your site, call recent clients, and agree payment terms that follow work done. The cheapest headline figure is rarely the cheapest villa.
169abcaa774d68a4: We spent twenty-one years as the builder before moving to the client's side, so this guide is written from both ends of the table. The twelve questions below are the ones we would want answered before any owner signs.
af1bb4e8c6100347: Before you ask anything: get the basis right
f334f486c51ee34a: Contractor selection goes wrong most often before the first bid arrives. If bidders are pricing from incomplete drawings, a vague specification or different assumptions, you will receive numbers that cannot be compared.
c486c7542674ebdc: Your registered consultant should provide a complete, consistent set of drawings and a specification. Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, only offices with a valid trade licence and registration with Dubai Municipality may present themselves as engineering consultancy offices (Dubai Media Office), so check the consultant's registration as carefully as the contractor's. Every bidder prices exactly the same thing, on the same form, by the same date. The owner then appoints. Our role at Eastbridge is to help you compare the bids like-for-like and choose, alongside your consultant.
e13671071a55d9d6: If you are considering a single firm to design and build the villa instead, the comparison works differently, because each bidder prices its own design. See design and build or a separate architect.
e293fcdec4d4540e: Gooden Heane, Portreath, Cornwall. Built by P Chapman Construction.
0de1271eb073bc64: The 12 questions to ask a villa contractor
4ef7255c2a89be68: 1. Are you registered for this type of work, with this authority?
c9bcf092e9e22c8f: Do not take a logo on a website as proof. Dubai Municipality's relaunched BPS app includes a search for consultants and contractors registered in Dubai, and lets owners look at information such as a firm's current status and the type and number of projects it is handling. The Build in Dubai platform is the wider gateway for the permit process. Check the trade licence, its expiry date and its licensed activities: Dubai Economy and Tourism's online licence information service shows a mainland firm's licence status, expiry date, legal type and activities when you search by name or licence number (Khaleej Times). Then confirm the firm can work under the authority your plot falls within: Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits.
2b8bdfa643f0e831: 2. How many villas like ours are you building right now?
391be273a61b481d: Workload matters as much as track record. A firm with too little work may be under financial pressure; a firm with too much will spread its best people thin. The BPS app's project information is a useful starting point for this conversation.
d3c49334c9422f30: 3. Who will run our site, and can we meet them?
29402c93caec02a6: The site manager or project manager who turns up every day decides the quality of your villa. Ask for names and CVs of the key staff, ask whether they will be dedicated to your project, and ask what happens if they leave. Make the named people a condition of the contract where you can.
11740e2418d3e170: On the contractor's side, we knew that the strongest site manager went to the job with the most demanding client and the best-run paperwork. That is not cynicism; it is how a builder protects its reputation with limited resources.
4af5926923d42f7c: 4. Is your price based on our drawings and specification, with nothing substituted?
3b1b27ad985913cf: Ask every bidder to confirm in writing that they have priced the documents as issued, and to list any alternatives separately. Substituted products and "equivalent" finishes buried in the pricing are a common way of shaving a headline number.
08cf3420c5b3792a: Preliminaries are the cost of running the site rather than building the villa: site staff, welfare, hoarding, temporary power and water, insurance, scaffolding, plant, cleaning and waste. Turner & Townsend's 2025 UAE market intelligence puts preliminaries in Dubai at 12% of construction cost on a 2,500 m² project and 14% on a 50,000 m² project. A villa sits at the small end of that scale, so treat 12% as the reference point. A bid with preliminaries far below it is either very efficient or has moved costs elsewhere, or has left them out to be claimed later. Ask for a breakdown, and ask how the monthly figure changes if the programme extends.
82efea7e8c3061f1: 6. What provisional sums have you included, and why?
d75f797a523296e3: A provisional sum is an allowance for work that cannot yet be fully defined. They are legitimate in small numbers. Large or numerous provisional sums mean the true price is still unknown. When comparing bids, list every provisional sum side by side and, where possible, set common figures for all bidders so the comparison is fair.
1c1273ef870bc755: Read exclusions as carefully as the price. Pools, landscaping, external works, kitchens, wardrobes, lighting control, AV, authority fees and service connections are frequently excluded or qualified. Two bids with the same total can be several hundred thousand dirhams apart once exclusions are priced back in.
7b7f2d6d3d9df39b: 8. What is your programme, and what does it depend on?
8077984c35f1f920: Ask for a programme showing the main stages, the critical path and what the contractor needs from you and when: design information, selections, approvals, payments. A programme that looks fast but depends on you making every decision instantly is not a real programme. See how long it takes to build a villa in Dubai for typical durations.
9ca22c869368ab18: 9. Can we speak to your last three villa clients?
3c82c46e8ed3c158: Not the three the contractor chooses to show off; the last three completed. And call them. Useful questions are: did the final account match the contract price, and if not, why? Was completion on time? How were defects handled after handover? Would you use them again? Whenever you can, visit a finished villa and a live site.
5b158022384c0a93: 10. What payment terms are you asking for?
abd1edb593068d84: Avoid schedules that pay large sums upfront or against calendar dates. Payments should follow work actually completed and checked. Agree how each payment is valued, who checks it and how long you have to pay once it is agreed. Our article on villa construction contracts in the UAE covers how payments are valued in more detail.
7747a6af8bf758f0: 11. What security will you provide: bonds, retention, insurance?
83f7094b251e2c2f: Ask whether the contractor will provide an advance payment guarantee against any mobilisation payment, a performance bond, and accept retention held back until completion and the end of the defects period. Ask for evidence of contractors' all-risks and third-party insurance. A contractor that resists all of these is telling you something about its balance sheet. Solvency matters beyond handover too: UAE law makes the contractor and the engineer jointly liable for ten years from handover for collapse or defects that threaten structural stability or safety, and that liability cannot be excluded by contract (Kayrouz & Associates). It is only as valuable as the firm standing behind it.
e74659f4f75f3f50: 12. How do you handle changes and delays?
728769a0db524e55: Every villa changes during construction. Ask how the contractor prices variations, how quickly it gives you a cost before carrying out changed work, and how it notifies delays. A clear answer here predicts a calmer project. A vague answer predicts arguments.
cf6d0fa639a8df60: Once the bids are in, put them on one page before anyone looks at the bottom line.
6f1016733913415b: Then hold a short clarification meeting with each serious bidder. Ask the same questions of each, record the answers, and have any changes confirmed in writing before you decide. This follows RICS guidance on tendering: queries raised by one bidder are answered to all of them, qualifications and assumptions are reviewed in detail, insurances are checked like-for-like, and a qualification that is resolved is confirmed by the bidder in writing.
8d88933720048266: Before you compare, also be clear what kind of contract you are pricing. RICS practice information on contract selection describes the main choices for the contract sum as a fixed-price lump sum, remeasurement or a target cost, and the choice changes how much of the bid is really fixed. Our guide to villa construction contracts in the UAE explains the difference.
0acfd154143c990e: Red flags when choosing a contractor
27984e0bd976ef17: A price far below the others, with no clear explanation.
c8fb38343b1f63db: Pressure to sign quickly, or to pay a deposit before the contract is agreed.
4e6dda5bca162369: Reluctance to name the site team or provide references.
c718f37d978e85b4: Heavy qualifications, long exclusions or "subject to" language throughout the bid.
e1d99e9b548eaa69: Payment schedules weighted to the front of the job.
b4c135e84a916b17: No appetite for bonds, retention or proper insurance.
66320d07271cb963: Suggestions that work can start before the permit is in place.
167ecd229cbfbbf9: A firm that cannot show you a finished villa of comparable quality.
3a00ae91ac7b0719: What a good contractor wants to see from you
c09043b4c6e2f57b: This is the part owners rarely hear. From our years on the builder's side, the best contractors choose their clients as carefully as clients choose them, and they price accordingly.
88a2f5cd34900a72: A good contractor wants to see:
713d9c0cd0f70d15: Complete drawings and a clear specification. Uncertainty is priced as risk. The clearer the documents, the sharper the price.
32e40de6287a7710: A decisive client. Late selections and changing minds are what delay villas. A contractor who sees an organised decision process prices less contingency.
a9997156d061edf9: Proof the money is there. Contractors worry about being paid. Clear payment terms, a sensible cash flow and a track record of paying on time make you a preferred client.
5b3168a32dc1a8e1: A fair contract. One-sided terms do not make a project safer; they make good contractors walk away and leave the bidders who plan to recover their margin through claims.
f3bbda2089d82587: Someone on the client side who understands construction. Contractors prefer dealing with a knowledgeable client representative to dealing with confusion. Disputes are expensive for them too.
656d723c00ba9f97: On the contractor's side, the jobs we priced keenest were the ones where the drawings were finished, the client knew what they wanted, and we trusted we would be paid on time. Those are all things an owner controls.
7367ecb2a1d4617d: We help owners compare contractor bids like-for-like, question the assumptions behind them and choose with confidence, working alongside your registered consultant. The appointment is always yours. Because we spent two decades pricing work as the builder, we know which parts of a bid hide the risk. If you already hold a quote, our contractor quote review looks at the scope gaps, provisional sums, payment schedule, variation clause and exclusions before you sign. c79e779533e1bde8: How many contractors should I ask to bid?
87154dd956eb512a: In our experience three to five serious bidders is enough. Fewer gives you no comparison; more wastes everyone's time and the best firms may decline to price a long list.

35aa0e040706648f: Choosing a team · 5 November 2026 · 9 min read · By Philip Chapman
c7f74844d3fc7757: Start with independence: ask who pays the firm, and whether it receives anything from the contractors, consultants or suppliers on your project.
04a7ad08f298571f: Get the limits of authority in writing: the person representing you should not be able to instruct the contractor, agree a variation or release a payment without your written approval.
3c23413dfcf44991: Ask who will actually attend site, by name, how often at each stage, and what you receive after each visit and each month.
cfe8b611fad555aa: A percentage fee means little until you know what it is calculated on and what happens to it if the build overruns.
9926929f0c3f13dc: In Dubai, design and the statutory engineering role belong to a registered consultancy; a client-side project manager works alongside it and should never present itself as one.
2c7fb52ce2a4fb31: What does a client-side project manager do on a Dubai villa?
6de79c280d1c4fc6: What authority will the project manager have?
dc7505e86247550e: Who will actually attend site, and how often?
28fcc7457d48728c: Questions to ask any client-side project manager, including us
5de560b9fb4bfb27: Red flags when choosing a project manager
63953f04f4d3d86a: To choose a client-side project manager for a Dubai villa, test five things in this order: independence (who pays them, and whether anything comes from anyone else on your project), limits of authority, who actually attends site and how often, what you receive in reports, and how the fee is calculated. Ask every firm the same questions, in writing, against the same scope of works. A good firm will answer each one plainly; a vague answer is itself an answer.
df6281104eb0d58f: This guide explains what to test, the conflicts to look out for, the questions to ask any firm, including us, and the red flags. If you are still deciding whether you need a client-side project manager at all, start with owner's representative, project manager or consultant and what a client-side project manager is worth.
00162d1f80186a22: What does a client-side project manager do on a Dubai villa?
d33bb5c5bfbb6201: A client-side project manager (also called an owner's representative) acts for you, the owner, on cost, programme, contract and decisions. It sits beside two other appointments you make directly: your registered consultant, who designs the villa and carries the statutory technical role, and your contractor, who builds it.
1eb018cfbc88fb8c: That division matters in Dubai. Under Law No. 14 of 2025, nobody may practise engineering consultancy without authorisation, and individuals or offices may not present themselves as engineering consultancy offices without a valid licence; registered offices must record their licensed scope, classification and technical staff with Dubai Municipality, and fines run up to AED 100,000 (Dubai Media Office, Law No. 14 of 2025). A client-side project manager who is not a registered consultancy should say so clearly, and should never offer to stand in for your consultant.
787e7eef4d58f4b4: Independence is the first test because everything else depends on it. A project manager checks other people's work: the design against your budget, the contractor's price against the market, payment applications against progress. That only works if the checker has no stake in the answer.
293de548cb860866: The professional bodies are clear about this. The Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS) says a member "must not advise or represent a client" where doing so would involve a conflict of interest, unless everyone affected has given prior informed consent. It treats a conflict between a client's interests and the firm's own interests, an "own interest conflict", as carrying greater risk (RICS, Conflicts of interest). The Project Management Institute's code requires project managers to "proactively and fully disclose any real or potential conflicts of interest" (PMI Code of Ethics).
f4b0d2973a58509f: Who pays you? The answer should be "only you".
b0e4c410b7abc4ec: Do you receive anything from anyone else on the project? That includes commissions, referral fees, rebates, discounts or hospitality from contractors, consultants, subcontractors or suppliers.
70f95b6b3e042db2: Do you, or any related company, design, build, supply or fit out? If so, how is that kept apart from your project?
02c6dbd96d7dbb80: Will you put the answers in the appointment? A promise in a meeting is not the same as a clause.
65834cc1ce494f67: Our own answers are in our independence pledge. Hold us to the same questions as everyone else.
454762218d7c759a: Conflicts with design-and-build and contracting arms
63b2a3a2faf4c515: Some firms offer project management alongside design, contracting or interiors, either in the same company or through a sister company. That is not wrong in itself, but it changes what you are buying. A firm cannot independently review a design it produced, a price it submitted or progress it is responsible for.
2ae8ef494ac1c919: RICS makes a related point: in UK practice, a surveyor's appointment "is unlikely to include the roles of both designer and project manager", and there is "a clear distinction between the two" (RICS GN 107/2013). If you choose a firm with a design or contracting arm, ask how it would handle a recommendation that went against its own sister company, and who would make that call. We look at the trade-offs in more detail in design and build versus a separate architect.
122934ac0a5a799f: How people are paid also shapes what they recommend. In August 2025, Dubai Municipality warned engineering consultancy offices that some villa structural designs went beyond the safety requirements of the Dubai Building Code and raised construction costs without justification (Gulf News). That warning concerned designers, not project managers, but the lesson carries: understand whether a higher build cost pays anyone you appoint more.
c5fec4dc314dddab: What authority will the project manager have?
833ca69632264b19: RICS lists "authority levels" among the elements every project manager's appointment should include, and says a project manager should "always act within the terms of their authority to avoid conflicts of interest and dispute" (RICS GN 107/2013). On a private villa, authority is where owners most often lose control without noticing.
168760419aed3918: Decide in writing which decisions stay with you. Our own limits of authority are simple: we never instruct the contractor or approve a payment without the owner's written approval. Whatever firm you choose, the table below is a useful starting point.
092452858f2800fc: What the project manager should do
78896c2e9e0d82f3: You, or your consultant where the contract gives them that role
79f515fe32eb29f4: Advise, draft and track, but not issue without your written approval
2e473dba2d0b10ef: Variations that change cost or time
8e52040ef0e12962: Check the price and the time claimed, and recommend
1cfa1c778fe28dba: You, on your consultant's checked figures
ac78418d8bfdfe0c: Check applications against progress and contract rates, and recommend
6cad205b51579d35: Choice of consultant, contractor and suppliers
67ad67d6ef7cffb3: Help you compare bids like-for-like and choose
cb5cfe12d625f691: Raise cost, programme and buildability questions
fdd3936a0d6cb998: Watch for an appointment that gives the project manager open-ended power to "act as the owner's agent". It sounds convenient when you live abroad, but it removes the check you are paying for.
218aa65f1d38394a: Who will actually attend site, and how often?
8287bfe48c4d78d9: A project management fee is mostly the cost of people's time, so the people are the service. In RICS's suggested criteria for assessing project management proposals, "people" (key and other personnel) carries the largest typical weighting, 30% to 40% of the quality score (RICS GN 107/2013).
dd6db844fa0905ff: Who covers when that person is away, and whether the lead can be replaced without your agreement.
3508af7fdddb50b2: Who attends the moments that matter: before concrete is poured, before walls and ceilings are closed, at commissioning and at the snagging walkround.
c293508768a3cc2d: From the builder's side, we can tell you how this looks on the other side of the table. For 21 years we ran the contractor's site, and we knew within a month which client representatives would turn up unannounced and which would only read the monthly report. We prepared for the first kind. Questions asked on site, before something is covered up, change what gets built. Questions asked from a report change what gets argued about later.
330cc612b1730ee8: Reporting is how you see the project when you are not there, which for many owners is most of the time. Ask for a sample or template report, with names removed, and check it answers four questions: where is the money, where is the programme, what has changed, and what do you need to decide.
e35838cff23d74b1: The FIDIC White Book, the international standard form for appointing consultants, which FIDIC describes as suitable for services including project management (FIDIC), treats reporting as an absolute obligation in its 2017 edition, alongside a programme the consultant must provide within 14 days of commencement (Curtis). Whatever form you use, the scope should say what reports you receive, how often, and what each contains: photographs, cost to date and forecast final cost, programme against plan, open variations, risks, and the decisions needed from you. Our site visits and reporting page shows the shape of ours.
9791922fe89a72cf: Fee models are covered in detail in client-side project manager fees in Dubai. When choosing between firms, three points matter most:
40a6a0ed5c9f8abe: What a percentage is applied to. RICS says it is important to agree whether a percentage applies to the approved budget, the accepted tender or the final cost of the works (RICS GN 107/2013). On the final cost, the fee rises when the cost rises.
db238613b85c3633: What is excluded. Your registered consultant's fee, other specialists, travel, disputes and the defects period are commonly outside a project manager's fee.
d1abf2ef372afa3c: What happens if the build overruns. Agree how extra months and extra cost are priced before anything goes wrong.
f0bcda004892f388: Our published ranges are on our fees page: a review costs AED 9,500–15,000 per review, part service is a monthly fee agreed in the written scope, and full service is typically 1.75–3% of build cost. Dubai Municipality also publishes guidance contract forms for consultancy and contracting on private villas, in Arabic, which are worth reading beside any appointment you are offered (Dubai Municipality).
33a3b886372471d5: Questions to ask any client-side project manager, including us
ee0b7bc1ee33ab25: Who pays you, and do you receive anything from anyone else on my project?
efe644db4c42eaff: Do you or any related company design, build, supply or fit out?
f7433825b9908535: Are you a registered engineering consultancy? If not, how will you work alongside mine?
0bf379ae95f4b4af: Who leads my project, by name, and who covers for them?
b594bdebbfffc695: Can you instruct the contractor, agree a variation or release a payment without my written approval?
2a4c466b9d373c9f: Is the fee fixed, monthly or a percentage, and if a percentage, of what?
b40d2942eeb96c2d: What is excluded, and how is work outside the scope priced?
f2dcf6e2f0dbbbcc: Can I see a sample or template of your monthly report?
a8f3aee104adc109: Red flags when choosing a project manager
371a7919fb5adad9: A vague answer about who pays them, or a reluctance to put it in the appointment.
18c121398dc917ad: A preferred contractor list you are expected to use, rather than help to compare the contractors you choose to invite.
2486f0be56299a33: An unnamed team, or a senior person at the pitch who never appears again.
78a536adae3defa6: No stated site attendance, or attendance described only as "as required".
322744d9e19bcb56: Open-ended authority to instruct, agree variations or release payments without asking you.
58fc3f2e09693ff2: A percentage fee with no stated base and no position on overruns.
e34c2fcfb41b527f: An offer to replace your registered consultant, or to take on roles the law reserves for registered offices.
6fd81557ca7e7e4e: No questions about you. A good project manager asks about your budget, your timescale, how decisions are made in your family and how often you are in Dubai, before proposing anything.
6fe3a16dcd96181b: We are a client-side project manager for private villa owners in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, and we expect to be tested on every question above. If you are comparing firms, we are happy to talk it through on a free first call, and to tell you plainly whether your project needs a full appointment or a single review. See owner's representation, our Island E worked example (a hypothetical worked example of how we would approach a waterfront villa), or contact us.
40862c898e406f3c: Client-side project manager fees in Dubai explained
8c028705e9127795: What should I look for when choosing a client-side project manager in Dubai?
1cbe74c845e679c7: Look first at independence (who pays them, and whether anything comes from the contractor or suppliers), then at limits of authority, the named people who will attend site, how often, what they report, and how the fee is calculated. Compare every firm against the same written scope of works, including us.
804d7f82e4930152: Can a design-and-build company also act as my project manager?
8f442e42d33d3e58: It can offer project management, but a firm that designs or builds your villa cannot be independent when it reviews its own design, price or progress. If you use design and build, consider a separate client-side representative who has no interest in either.
bd461a722566ac01: Should a client-side project manager be able to approve payments to the contractor?
86d1d434793deef1: Only if you decide to delegate that, in writing, with limits. Many owners prefer the project manager to check payment applications and recommend, while the owner gives the written approval. The appointment should say exactly which decisions are delegated and which are not.
d078aba88485b83c: Is a client-side project manager the same as my registered consultant?
1319ee25631a6b96: No. Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, only registered offices may practise engineering consultancy or present themselves as consultancy offices. Your registered consultant designs the villa and carries the statutory technical role; a client-side project manager represents you on cost, programme, contract and decisions, working alongside the consultant.
560bf226674d5502: What are the red flags when choosing a project manager?
78b73c630478097b: Vague answers about who pays them, an unnamed team, no stated site attendance, an open-ended authority to instruct or pay, a fee with no stated base, a list of preferred contractors you are expected to use, and any suggestion that they can stand in for your registered consultant.

Only then should anyone start on site. Most renovations that overrun went wrong in the first half of that list, not the second.
ade789cef9e06a48: This page is our renovation hub. Each step below has a short summary of what matters and links to the guide or tool that covers it in full.

adfdbac89f13be7b: Step 1: Decide whether to renovate or rebuild
28977b4cacb1db58: Start with what you want the villa to do: more bedrooms, a better layout, a modern kitchen and services, a pool, a different look. Then ask honestly whether the existing house can get you there. A renovation keeps the old structure, slab levels and ceiling heights; a rebuild resets them, but takes far longer and costs more per square foot.
ddc8c66bb64e4781: Our renovate or rebuild guide compares the two with sourced rates and a worked example, including the months the family spends out of the house. The renovate-or-rebuild tool runs the same comparison on your own villa size and specification. When the brief keeps growing towards new structure, new services and a new envelope, it is usually time to look at the rebuild figures properly.
89ac7ff01267a106: Step 2: Learn what your community allows
6d3f8ee6024df5ac: In Dubai's master-planned communities, the master developer decides what can change before any authority sees the drawings. Nakheel says an NOC from its Urban Planning team is needed before any alteration (Nakheel). In Arabian Ranches, Emaar Community Management says any alteration needs Emaar's approval through a home modification NOC, and external changes that alter the look of the villas are not permitted (Emaar Community Management).
d5a9749cd4be4a55: That makes your community the second question, not an afterthought. Our area guides set out the master developer, the approval route and the typical villa stock:
12f9c457b1c16baf: Palm Jumeirah, with our detailed guide to renovating a Palm Jumeirah villa: older frond villas, salt exposure, Nakheel's site requirements.
38c69a11cbaf718e: Jumeirah Islands: a Nakheel community where owners have reported charges for added floor area and penalties for unapproved work (Gulf News, 2018).
20e631c9c2af3994: Arabian Ranches: an Emaar community with sub-community home modification guidelines.
17c875a5b7784a9b: Emirates Hills (Emaar) and Dubai Hills Estate (Emaar with Meraas): each guide sets out the master developer's approval route.
c9ec928d188ad82e: If you are unsure whether a piece of work needs approval, assume it does until the master developer has said otherwise in writing.
fd370562c8552bd6: Step 3: Survey the villa before anything is designed
640f7ea6a0eb5845: An older villa hides its condition behind finishes. Air-conditioning, wiring, plumbing, drainage and waterproofing are the usual unknowns, and structure sometimes is too. A condition survey arranged through the right specialists, with some opening-up of walls, ceilings and wet areas, answers those questions while answers are still cheap. Our article on rewiring and replumbing an older Dubai villa covers the services survey in detail.
5e692243888ebae1: Our guide to villa renovation mistakes puts skipping this step near the top of the list, for a simple reason: whatever the survey does not find, the strip-out will, and by then the contractor is on site and pricing the answer.
1f5d3c3ba294e817: Step 4: Set a budget for the whole project
45355cd4f1fc8474: Published renovation figures disagree. Property Finder runs from AED 250,000–400,000 for a three-bedroom townhouse refresh to AED 1.5–3.5 million or more for structural work on a luxury villa, while a Dubai renovation contractor's 2026 guide puts mid-range work at AED 400,000–800,000 and luxury from AED 1 million. Both are mostly the contractor's price.
3d2e05c5ad41afd5: A real budget adds design fees, approval charges, any master-developer charge for added area, external works, furniture, the cost of living elsewhere and a contingency. Engel & Völkers says a contingency of 10–15% of total project cost is widely recommended (Engel & Völkers); on an older villa with original services we would plan at the upper end. Our villa renovation cost guide works through a 6,000 sq ft example, and the villa cost calculator gives a sourced range for your own size and specification.
938d0a9bd748718b: On site, published guides put a smaller interior refresh at about two to three months and structural work on a luxury villa at 150–210 days. Survey, design, approvals and tender come before that. Our villa renovation timeline breaks the whole journey into phases with our planning allowances, and explains what stretches a Dubai programme: the summer midday break from 15 June to 15 September (Gulf News), shorter working hours in Ramadan, NOC comments and long-lead imports.
0fdbacb63f262a3e: If time out of the house has a cost, the delay cost estimator shows what each month of slippage adds in rent and finance.
bf56a0e19f915a85: Step 6: Design, then get the NOC and any permit
3ee2329a76c3c50a: The design should be priced as it develops, so that what goes for approval is something you can afford. Your DM-registered consultant then submits to the master developer and, with the NOC in hand, applies for the permit where the scope needs one, to Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits. Service-authority NOCs are gathered through Dubai's unified permit window (Dubai Municipality), and the Build in Dubai platform covers alterations as well as new builds (Build in Dubai).
8fd3866d2d3cd3ef: Our Nakheel NOC guide explains what triggers an NOC, what Nakheel asks for and the site requirements that follow. Our guide to which Dubai authority covers my villa explains how to confirm the permit route for your plot, and the Dubai villa building permit guide covers that stage step by step.
0eecdc9d71887efd: Step 7: Choose the contractor and agree the contract
52688afc6a824149: Renovation is a different skill from building new. Ask bidders about comparable renovations, how they handle discoveries after strip-out and how they price provisional sums. Give every bidder the same survey findings and approved drawings, then compare the exclusions as carefully as the totals. Our guide on how to choose a villa contractor in Dubai lists the questions to ask, and an independent contractor quote review sets bids side by side on the same basis.
1d1c9752071c9956: The contract should tie the start date to approvals in hand, set out how changes are priced and agreed, and link payments to work done. Our guide to villa construction contracts in the UAE explains the main forms and clauses; take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer before you sign.
9e8ac75d74742b3f: Step 8: Run the works with your hands on the controls
a01c39179f8f5dd6: Three things keep a renovation under control once it starts. First, finishes chosen and long-lead items ordered against the programme, not after the strip-out; our guide to sourcing materials abroad covers lead times, shipping and customs. Second, every change agreed in writing, with its price and its effect on the programme, before the work is done. Third, payments that follow progress rather than run ahead of it; the stage payment planner shows how a schedule should track the work.
d5d965311200f8c5: On the contractor's side, we knew within the first few weeks of a renovation which clients would end up paying for changes. It was rarely the ones with the most ambitious briefs. It was the ones who agreed things on site, by word of mouth, and found out the price at the next valuation. Our founder, Philip Chapman, spent 21 years running P Chapman Construction in the UK, and the habit of writing every change down before it is built is still the single most valuable one an owner can have.
3c397663ad46df42: Step 9: Snag it properly before you accept it
f7039a8f7336b1c0: Handover is the last point at which you have real leverage. Test the air-conditioning, water pressure and hot water, drainage, electrics and lighting controls, glazing and doors, and look closely at finishes in good light. Our villa snagging guide goes room by room, and the printable snagging checklist adds a severity column and a snag log. Keep the retention, if the contract has one, until the snags are closed.
730b11869f37935b: We act for the owner from the first renovate-or-rebuild question to handover, alongside your DM-registered consultant, who prepares and submits the NOC and permit applications, and the contractor you appoint. We arrange the condition review, set the scope, budget and programme, help you compare bids like-for-like and choose, and report on progress and payments in plain English; we never instruct the contractor or approve a payment without your written approval. See our villa renovation project management service, or get in touch to talk through your villa.

9a7f31c81383984b: How long does it take to plan and complete a villa renovation?
76a8151d4eb4d11e: Published guides put the work on site at about two to three months for a smaller interior refresh and 150–210 days for structural work on a luxury villa. e3ce7acb9822badb: A Nakheel NOC is the master developer's written no-objection to the works you want to carry out on your villa, and in Nakheel communities it is the first approval on the critical path. Nakheel's own guidance is that you must obtain an NOC from its Urban Planning team before making any alterations, requested through Nakheel Online Services or the My Nakheel app (Nakheel). Once you have it, your consultant applies for the building permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits (see which Dubai authority covers my villa), and only then should the contractor mobilise.
2738ccb67adc5242: This guide covers what triggers an NOC, what Nakheel wants to see, how it fits with the authority permit, and the part most guides leave out: how to sequence your contractor around it so the approvals do not cost you money.
54256228401d8f2c: Nakheel describes an NOC as a No Objection Certificate it issues to customers to carry out various activities within Nakheel properties (Nakheel). There are several kinds, from resale to private events. The one that matters for a renovation is the modification NOC issued by Nakheel's Urban Planning team.
7b3ce327ca4c7c38: It is worth being clear about what the NOC is and is not.
18d7b66fb2d6b6c6: It is the master developer confirming that your proposal is acceptable within its community: design guidelines, plot limits, the look of the street, and the protection of shared infrastructure and neighbours.
d31188fff62cc1c1: It is not a building permit. The permit comes afterwards from the relevant authority, and the works are inspected under that permit, not under the NOC.
c7fd92b6d9ad7536: It is not permission for the contractor to arrive. Site access is a separate set of Nakheel requirements, covered below.
f73e4413a9e10862: Nakheel's day-to-day community services now sit with Nakheel Community Management, the company it set up in 2020 to run community and facilities management (Gulf News). Nakheel lists help@nakheelcommunities.com and 800-NAKHEEL as the contact points for NOC queries.
cf2daf78c87b8f6a: Which renovation works need a Nakheel NOC?
6a8fdeffd4a4a4cf: Nakheel's customer FAQ says owners can make changes as long as they do not affect the external façade and structure, and that an NOC from its Urban Planning team is needed before any alteration (Nakheel). Whether façade, structural or extension work is possible at all in your community is for Nakheel to confirm in writing before you design it.
aefd62617e6f494f: Nakheel publishes its rules to owners through its portal, and requirements change. The table below is our planning guide, not Nakheel's published rules: treat it as a guide to how the conversation usually goes rather than a ruling.
4b0c0093767a4d0a: Extension, new room, enclosing a terrace or balcony
c1ff9dbde01be9d4: Yes, if Nakheel permits it in your community
9158c576109b0270: Plot limits, setbacks, added floor area, structure
df343e4571dcdee3: Façade change: new openings, glazing, cladding, colour
1baca55d221a011a: Structural change: removing walls, new beams or stairs
864b7861c151d077: Pergolas, shades, boundary walls, hard landscaping
faaf150368236b30: Visibility from the street, height, materials
88e991bfd5628b95: MEP replacement: new AC, rewiring, re-plumbing
c9744c65deaf6a84: Depends on scope and service authority
e7f8da0fe9b48751: Kitchen and bathroom refit, same layout and services
e94e3bcd9f9273e2: Our rule of thumb: if you are not sure whether a piece of work needs an NOC, assume it does until Nakheel has said otherwise in writing. An email from the community team is worth more than any number of contractors telling you "nobody bothers for that".
e91fd4de5a0a18ba: What does Nakheel ask for in an NOC application?
91bc8b79e2b01c11: The detail depends on the scope, and Nakheel confirms the requirements when it reviews a request. For anything beyond light interior work, expect your consultant to assemble:
dc36350f5c8e1c9d: proof of ownership (title deed) and the owner's identification;
58fdc0796b29a2ae: the plot's site or affection plan and the existing villa drawings;
904c689a0c7757c4: proposed architectural drawings showing exactly what changes, and structural drawings and calculations where structure is affected;
1a27c7ce96791295: the details of the consultant and contractor who will carry out the work;
f079b6523e0514be: written landlord consent if a tenant is applying.
f57e2dbb7fa25014: Fees are not published as a single schedule. Nakheel told Gulf News that villa modification applications are "assessed on a case-by-case basis" and that "various costs apply"; owners in that report described charges tied to the added floor area of extensions (Gulf News). The practical point is simple: on an extension, the Nakheel charge for added area is a real line in the budget, so ask for it to be confirmed before the design is frozen, not after.
15d294e368e097d4: How does the Nakheel NOC fit with the building permit?
3432377f97a6e607: Think of two gates in series.
9b79bf8b716813ab: Nakheel NOC. The master developer reviews the proposal against its community rules.
8e849c3a0f28b9a0: Building permit. With the NOC in hand, your DM-registered consultant applies for the permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits. The master developer NOC is one of the documents uploaded with the permit application (Dubizzle).
85a884382339cfbc: Service-authority NOCs are gathered through Dubai's unified permit window (Dubai Municipality); our guide to the Dubai villa building permit explains that stage in full. The Build in Dubai platform covers alterations as well as new builds (Build in Dubai). After the permit is issued, the work is inspected in stages and closed out with a completion inspection and certificate (Dubai Municipality).
8be6631177cbc2e0: Two consequences follow. First, if the design changes after the NOC, you may need to go back to Nakheel before the permit can follow. Second, the permit authority will not fix a weak NOC submission; time lost at the first gate carries straight through the second.
3486574692864ad0: What does the contractor need before starting on site?
ecce89c3c9bc70be: This is where owners are most often caught out. Even with the NOC and permit, the contractor still has Nakheel's site requirements to meet. Nakheel's guidance states that contractors must pay the required security deposit, submit the Site Access Permit and fix the PVC fence before starting construction (Nakheel).
c06b6d644bfc52b0: On top of that, every worker needs an access permit:
4fe8cf0e34f60fb2: Long-term access permits run from one week to six months, with no renewals or extensions, so a longer job needs fresh applications in good time.
c8105d7188e14432: Lead time is three to four working days, with approval typically taking one to two days.
5c01076a657c05e1: Charges of AED 52.50 per person apply to construction, modification and extension work that requires an NOC.
423bc451d1cb9024: Daily permits are free and valid for one, two or three days, which suits a site visit or a one-off delivery, not a working crew.
8628d017b0c21901: All of this comes from Nakheel's published FAQs (Nakheel). None of it is difficult, but every item has a lead time, and on a renovation with several trades the access permits alone become a small administrative workstream. Ask at tender stage who carries it and whether the deposit and permit costs are in the price.
206279cc22dbc0d0: How should you sequence contractor mobilisation around the NOC?
6071b22658bf79fa: This is the builder's-side view, and it is where real money is made or lost.
fccc5af492f6ca6c: On the contractor's side, we always wanted the contract signed and the start date fixed as early as possible. A signed contract with a commencement date secures the job, releases the advance payment and starts the programme clock. If the approvals then ran late, that was not the builder's risk: a crew ready to start, kept off site because the client's permissions were not in place, is a textbook delay and cost claim. Our founder, Philip Chapman, ran P Chapman Construction in the UK for 21 years, and the pattern is the same anywhere: whoever controls the approvals carries the risk of them running late.
3cdaa0adc1568ea7: So on a Nakheel renovation, the sequence we recommend is:
6ec6c35c4a3fec09: Survey and brief. Condition survey and opening-up of the existing villa before the design is fixed.
d11f533995d3b3dd: Design to NOC level. Enough drawing for Nakheel to review, priced at the same time so you do not seek approval for something you cannot afford.
e5dee511d6db6ff5: Nakheel NOC. Submitted by your consultant through the Nakheel portal.
dc963f06f529a04f: Detailed design and authority permit. Through the unified window.
9ba64c88779e9f36: Tender on the approved drawings. Contractors price what has actually been approved, which removes a whole category of later variations. Our guide on how to choose a villa contractor in Dubai covers the comparison.
29be41d34262f534: Contract with a conditional start. The commencement date is defined as a set number of days after the permit is issued and Nakheel's site requirements are met, not the date of signature.
592ba00d9066c95f: Mobilisation. Deposit paid, Site Access Permit and fence in place, workforce permits issued, then the crew arrives.
2f2902d1784cf55d: If programme pressure means you must appoint the contractor before approvals land, keep the early phase small and defined: surveys, enabling design input, ordering long-lead items you would buy anyway. Do not pay a large advance against a start date nobody controls. Our article on villa construction contracts in the UAE covers how to word this, and for the contract itself take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer.
b622de9275362739: What goes wrong with Nakheel NOCs?
ac7b2ebcb0d9c7bc: In our experience the problems are rarely the NOC itself. They are about timing and scope.
a05dcc70b27b6224: Starting before the NOC. Gulf News reported owners in a Nakheel community who discovered the approval requirement only when they came to sell, facing a fine and a charge for the added space (Gulf News).
832c81182b31d38d: Scope creep after approval. A terrace becomes an enclosed room, or a window becomes a door. If it changes what Nakheel approved, it may need to go back.
6a9269d4a2b48de8: Treating the NOC as permission to start. The contractor arrives, the access permits are not in place, and you pay for standing time.
8369d2e8198e59c5: Access permits expiring mid-job. Long-term permits cannot be extended, so a slipping programme needs fresh applications.
02c525740c92f4cd: Exclusions in the bid. Deposit, fencing and permit charges left out of the price come back as extras.
686f9e19c68e3e24: For a fuller picture of renovating in one Nakheel community, see our guide to renovating a Palm Jumeirah villa. For the wider mistakes that push renovations over time and budget, see villa renovation mistakes, from the builder's side.
982ff50b3cfb9fcf: We represent the owner on villa renovations in Nakheel communities, working alongside your DM-registered consultant, who prepares and submits the NOC and permit applications, and your chosen contractor. Our part is to make sure the brief, budget, design and approvals line up, that bids are compared like-for-like on the approved drawings, and that the contract ties the start date to approvals rather than signature. Having spent two decades on the builder's side, we know how delay claims are built and how to avoid handing one over. 77d80ddb3e059473: It is a No Objection Certificate issued by Nakheel, as master developer, allowing an owner to carry out a defined activity in a Nakheel community. For renovations it is issued by Nakheel's Urban Planning team and is requested through Nakheel Online Services or the My Nakheel app.
b08fc524546d94db: Do I need a Nakheel NOC to renovate the inside of my villa?
d302c82fc52c3556: Nakheel's own guidance says changes are possible provided they do not affect the external façade and structure, and that an NOC must be obtained before any alterations. In practice, confirm any interior scope with Nakheel in writing before work starts, particularly if walls, services or wet areas are involved.
b9019d0385e0597f: How long does a Nakheel NOC take?
a22a42cd409bd134: Nakheel assesses villa modification applications case by case and does not publish a single turnaround for them. Allow for at least one round of comments on anything beyond a simple scope, and do not fix a contractor start date until the NOC and the authority permit are both in hand.
9df117f03cbd78da: How much does a Nakheel NOC cost?
54060a713b3e0204: Nakheel says various costs apply and confirms fees when it reviews a request. Owners extending villas have reported charges linked to the added floor area, and Nakheel separately charges AED 52.50 per person for workforce access permits on works needing its NOC. Get the fee confirmed before you commit to the design.
daa7e6c4a5d75af4: What happens if I renovate without a Nakheel NOC?
54c4bc6f44cc2b0c: Unapproved work tends to surface when you sell, extend again or a neighbour complains. Gulf News reported owners in a Nakheel community facing a fine and a charge for the added space after building without approval, so it is far cheaper to apply first.

112b11086d134437: In an older villa, the mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) systems are where most of the unknowns sit, and they are hidden behind finishes until strip-out.
0a62abab9f8f4189: Survey and open up before you tender: electrical tests, a pressure test on the water pipes, a camera survey of the drains and a check of the age and condition of the air-conditioning plant.
37b116bdebcfee83: Villas permitted before Dubai's green building regulations became mandatory for all new buildings in March 2014 were not designed to today's energy and water rules, so a full MEP replacement is often a redesign, not a like-for-like swap.
7523e3ca4e30bdb6: Contractors price what they cannot see with provisional sums, schedules of rates or a large risk allowance; only the first two keep the owner in control of the money.
ae9fbb98a3e4ed4d: Any alteration in a master-planned community needs the developer's approval first, and the owner's DM-registered consultant decides whether the MEP changes also need an authority permit.
08f0cd74513154e5: Why MEP is the biggest unknown in an older villa
063c49683fe7a9f1: What we typically find behind the walls
2f4755efb0461ee2: How contractors price what they cannot see
2e8c2e4a485d2b87: What we do and what we don't
69924024ec71ce38: In an older Dubai villa, the wiring, water pipes, drains and air conditioning are where most of a renovation's surprises sit, because they are hidden behind finishes until the strip-out. The way to control them is to survey and open up before you tender, decide what you will replace rather than repair, and make sure the contractor prices what nobody can see in a way you can check.
fc55339dfbef469d: This article covers what we expect to find, how to find it early, and how contractors price the unknown. For the wider picture, start with our guide on how to plan a villa renovation in Dubai.
f685fba0afebac23: Why MEP is the biggest unknown in an older villa
29bf15c67cd03784: Mechanical, electrical and plumbing work (MEP) sits in walls, ceilings, floor screeds and the ground. Finishes, kitchens and joinery are visible and easy to price; services are not. A contractor quoting from a walk-round sees sockets, taps and air-conditioning grilles, not the cable behind them, the joints in the pipes or the fall of the drains.
064cb9b514beeb31: Age matters for a regulatory reason too. Dubai Municipality made its green building regulations mandatory for government buildings in January 2011 and for all new buildings in March 2014. Circular No. 183 of 2011 required solar water heating on new single-owner buildings, including private villas, from 2012. The Dubai Building Code, which unified design rules previously spread across Dubai Municipality, the Dubai Development Authority and Trakhees, came into force at the end of 2021. A villa permitted before these dates was designed to the rules of its time. When you replace its services wholesale, your consultant will tell you which current requirements the new work must meet, so a full MEP replacement is often a redesign rather than a like-for-like swap.
daa8af028d8a24e6: On the contractor's side, the first thing we priced on any old house was the services, because they decided whether the job made money. A tidy kitchen quote is worth little if the first day of strip-out finds a corroded pipe run behind it.
b0c2ed70989d7fd1: Arabian Ranches, for illustration. Image: Emaar.
dbb37146738b3eb4: What we typically find behind the walls
8b0fb196d39747f3: Every villa is different, and only a survey tells you about yours. These are the items we look at first in an older villa, what tends to show the problem and how a contractor will usually want to price it.
b04aa1a628237506: What tends to show a problem
d38dc994caf7f25f: How it is usually priced if found
4bbe09b506c1081a: Age and condition of distribution boards; protective devices; labelling
88db794e5449ce6c: Heat marks, loose terminations, missing labels, boards with no spare ways
11a34fb38a108274: Lump sum once surveyed; schedule of rates for extra circuits
ded06ebe6832f29e: Test results; cable condition at accessories; added circuits
30b2ebb69911ef91: Poor test results, brittle insulation, extensions and junctions buried in walls
8288c8e0754fee87: Provisional sum for a rewire, or rate per point
b79b6ef1e9330a24: Pipe material; pressure test; joints and valves
f29f1e8a2695262e: Pressure loss, discoloured water, corroded or seized valves, repeat leaks
5362cbaaa110fc7d: Rate per metre and per fitting, or a provisional sum
cecb35017a50cec8: Sediment, a poorly sealed lid, a noisy or cycling pump
6f215337532b37fd: CCTV camera survey; falls; gully and inspection chamber condition
5e6893d380bfb53c: Root ingress, displaced joints, standing water, recurring smells
74888c765c610095: Provisional sum until the survey is done
538f252120bed642: Heater type and age; solar thermal if present
3706354ec7f64b95: Scale, corrosion, poor recovery, no isolation
05b46430ecef389b: Plant age and condition; duct condition and insulation; condensate drains
1440e7b603fb865e: Poor cooling in some rooms, wet ceilings near units, damaged duct insulation
aca30c9df7187595: Fixed price for plant; rates for ductwork
9378b8a6fa8fb0f2: Staining in rooms below, loose tiles, hollow screeds
b61d90a1661e61b3: Two patterns repeat. First, earlier owners add circuits, sockets and air-conditioning units over the years, often without updating drawings, so the record is wrong before anyone starts. Second, services fail at the joints and edges: where pipes pass through walls, where drains connect to chambers and where cables terminate. That is where to open up.
1d90391b17ba311a: How to survey before you tender
6c73e36452e62a46: The aim is to turn unknowns into priced items before the contract is signed. In our experience a few days of investigation repays itself many times over.
a2fe0ed09731df1f: Get the drawings. Ask the developer or the community management office for the original approved drawings and any later NOCs. They show what was approved, which is not always what was built, but they tell you where to look.
e393844d3365b27e: Electrical testing. Have a qualified electrical contractor inspect and test the installation and report in writing on its condition, the distribution boards and the capacity of the existing supply.
5e66bc8c7f7c7224: Water pressure test. A pressure test on the supply pipes shows leaks you cannot see. Ask for the pipe materials and any corroded valves to be recorded.
4fa622e6f52ded4b: CCTV drain survey. A camera survey of the drains, with a short video and a marked-up plan, shows root ingress, displaced joints and poor falls.
76164d4338b16774: Air-conditioning inspection. Record the age and condition of each unit, the condition of the ducts and their insulation, and where the condensate drains run.
6680f3aa312a052d: Targeted opening up. Agree with the owner a handful of spots to open: behind one shower, one section of ceiling under a bathroom, the kitchen sink wall. Make good afterwards.
c0a1a10c8aa50f36: Then write the findings into the scope. Our renovation project management work includes coordinating this survey with the owner's consultant and contractor, and turning it into a scope that bidders can price on the same basis.
b94855bc9e7197d7: Once the survey is in, each system falls into one of three decisions. The table shows how we think about them.
7b6b3200d8377aa9: Tests are good; the layout is not changing; the system has years of life left
344ac5a39d172f46: Repairs behind new finishes are hard to reach later; record them on drawings
acaedc34c144a883: Condition is poor but the layout and loads are unchanged
980b5ddbb0459477: Your consultant confirms which current requirements the new work must meet
fcb0c5aadcb810f8: New kitchen, more bathrooms, new air-conditioning layout, pool, EV charging, an extension
b6ef736424d28fa1: Needs the consultant's MEP design, the developer's approval and possibly an authority permit; check the supply capacity early
10b6ae5e2b5c2918: If the new loads need more capacity than the existing electricity supply provides, the change to the supply goes through DEWA, which offers an electricity network modification service. Your consultant manages that application; we make sure it is on the programme, because a supply upgrade on a finished villa is the kind of item that holds up a handover.
57fcdc538e8d4cb3: How contractors price what they cannot see
f94f74ae736df6c3: A contractor who cannot see the services has three ways to deal with the risk:
a7e63a6368eac819: A provisional sum. A placeholder amount for work that cannot be defined yet, adjusted to the actual cost when it is known. It is transparent, but only if the contract says how the actual cost is measured and approved. Our article on villa construction contracts in the UAE covers the clauses to look for.
e18bf44615ad8d2a: A schedule of rates. Agreed prices per metre of pipe, per electrical point or per drain repair, applied to whatever is found. This works well for MEP because the quantities are uncertain but the type of work is predictable.
0342be04859bd80e: A hidden risk allowance. A lump sum loaded into the price. The owner pays for the risk whether or not it happens, and the contractor has every reason to argue that a discovery falls outside it.
6a6a57de74c2ff51: When we compare bids like-for-like, MEP is where quotes differ most. One contractor includes a full rewire; another prices only "make safe and test"; a third excludes drainage altogether. Lining them up against the same survey-based scope is the only fair comparison.
779a136782c397b8: Published cost guides rarely separate out MEP. Property Finder, for example, groups plumbing with painting and tiling in its standard villa band and lists permit fees from AED 500 to AED 15,000 depending on the type of work. Our article on villa renovation costs in Dubai sets out the published ranges and what they leave out.
3c86524860360c87: In master-planned communities the developer's approval comes first. Emaar's guidance for Arabian Ranches, for example, says any alteration to the villa has to be approved by Emaar through the community portal, that interior painting and regular maintenance do not need a NOC, and that contractors need an entry permit to work in the community. Nakheel communities follow a similar route, with the Nakheel NOC before any authority permit; see our article on the Nakheel NOC for villa renovations.
ba3ba10dee4d29c5: Whether the MEP work also needs a building permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits, is a question for your DM-registered consultant. Replacing a tap is maintenance; relocating bathrooms, adding air-conditioning plant or changing the electricity supply generally is not. Do not fix the contractor's start date until the answer is in writing.
6850200188051c87: MEP sits in the middle of the programme and drives everything around it:
747f3a062e4d790f: Strip-out and opening up confirm the survey. Allow a short hold point here to price any discoveries before work continues.
c4fcbda98514bd36: First fix (cables, pipes, ducts and drains before walls and ceilings close) is the last chance to see the services. Our site visits and reporting include an owner's visit before close-up, with photographs of every wall and ceiling so you know where everything runs.
80e4658c14d6d560: Testing and commissioning before finishes: electrical test certificates, pressure tests and air-conditioning commissioning records should be in the handover file.
a03e4ed6db5848a1: Second fix and finishes follow, then snagging and handover.
ba0ad5ab3065b25e: Long-lead items matter here too. Air-conditioning plant, distribution boards and water heaters can set the date more than the site work does; our villa renovation timeline shows where they fit.
a83971ad2c8046b4: What we do and what we don't
5fbcc629ba4005b6: We represent the owner. We work alongside your DM-registered consultant, who designs the MEP and handles the approvals, and your contractor, who carries out and certifies the work through its own qualified trades. Our part is the survey brief, a scope bidders can price on the same basis, like-for-like bid comparison, cost and programme control, and independent client-side site visits with photographs before anything is closed up. If you are weighing a full MEP replacement against a rebuild, our renovate-or-rebuild tool is a useful first step, and you can contact us to talk it through.
c022433247666b74: Should I rewire an older villa in Dubai?
7ec57caa5e6e3ebc: Not automatically. Have the installation tested by a qualified electrical contractor first. If the tests, the condition of the distribution boards and the planned new loads (kitchen, air conditioning, pool, EV charging) all point the same way, a full rewire during the renovation is far cheaper than doing it later through new finishes. If the tests are good, targeted upgrades may be enough.
54d51eb611ab04c1: How do I find out what is behind the walls before I renovate?
77bed0511b810d7a: Commission a survey that includes electrical testing, a pressure test on the water supply, a CCTV camera survey of the drains and an inspection of the air-conditioning plant, then open up a few agreed spots in wet areas and ceilings. It costs a little and a few days, and it turns many unknowns into priced items before you sign a contract.
afd1f47d29835e2c: How do contractors price unknown MEP work in a renovation?
69907aa3eac04fb8: Usually in one of three ways: a provisional sum (a placeholder amount adjusted to the actual cost), a schedule of rates (agreed prices per metre, per point or per item, applied to what is found), or a lump-sum risk allowance hidden in the price. The first two are transparent; the third means you pay for the risk whether or not it happens.
bc20f63a5adcf364: Do I need approval to replace the wiring or plumbing in my villa?
1b44314729807f19: In most master-planned communities any alteration needs the developer's approval, usually as a NOC, and contractors need an access permit. Whether the work also needs an authority permit depends on its scope and on where the plot sits, so ask your DM-registered consultant before you fix a start date.
