992e37598f28f0c5: Home/Insights/Owner's rep vs project manager vs consultant in Dubai
495768f7b61adc26: Choosing a team · 29 October 2026 · Updated 1 November 2026 · 7 min read · By Philip Chapman
958472727c3c74a7: Your registered consultant designs the villa and carries the statutory technical role; only registered firms may do this under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025.
63f13016d484f5b2: A project manager organises the project; an owner's representative does that and acts solely for the owner, with no stake in the design or the build.
897d1b8c58d83a5f: Design-and-build firms and consultants reviewing their own design have built-in conflicts that the owner should understand and manage.
41dbd82a4c33ca38: Each appointment should state scope, deliverables, authority to instruct, fees, reporting and how the role ends.
7efaa409bf3160ac: A simple villa with an experienced owner on the ground may not need an owner's representative; a complex or remote build usually benefits from one.
de74d2ddc5dcf641: When do you need an owner's representative, and when don't you?
10188c1aa286d07d: What should you ask before appointing an owner's representative?
7f83f3fa467e617d: On a Dubai villa build, your registered consultant designs the house and carries the statutory technical role, your contractor builds it, and an owner's representative acts solely for you on cost, programme, contract and decisions. A "project manager" can be any of these things depending on who employs them, which is why the title matters less than whose interests the person serves. The roles complement each other; none replaces the consultant.
1a4913b743a9e049: What does each role actually do?
24ac0283ae82eee8: The confusion is understandable. In the UAE, "project manager", "owner's rep", "PMC" and "consultant" are used loosely, and firms describe themselves differently. Focus on function and on who pays them.
0e867e1f9d9cd404: Owner, within professional and statutory duties
3e6864f744a00e56: No; reviews design against brief and budget
6a407bc52dcbc048: Helps the owner compare like-for-like and choose
40abaf5f1c5b57ad: The consultant role is defined by law. Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, only registered consultancies may practise engineering consultancy or present themselves as engineering consultants, and the law applies across Dubai including special development zones and free zones (Law No. 14 of 2025, Dubai Media Office). The other two roles are defined by contract.
ae76874b1df5f6ff: Your consultant is your designer and your statutory technical professional. They take the brief, design the villa, coordinate the engineering, prepare and submit the approval drawings, and normally carry the statutory site role during construction. They are essential. You cannot build without one. Dubai Municipality publishes standard consultancy contract forms for private villas, in Arabic, and the BPS app lists registered consultants with ratings.
4ae195227a1d9a4a: "Project manager" describes an activity, not an allegiance. A contractor has project managers. Some consultants offer project management as an add-on. Some independent firms offer it to owners. The work is planning, coordinating, chasing and reporting. Before you rely on a project manager, ask who appoints them and who pays them.
f7d9bb543ccb8306: An owner's representative manages the project from the owner's side of the table only. Typical scope: setting and controlling the budget, the programme and the decision schedule; helping the owner compare bids and choose; reviewing valuations and variations; independent client-side site visits and reporting; and keeping the consultant and contractor accountable to the brief. The owner's representative does not design, does not make authority submissions and does not take on the consultant's statutory role. The value lies in having no stake in the design fee or the construction price.
c8d73c20a5a75653: Where are the conflicts of interest?
999b106841209b05: Every party on a villa build has a legitimate commercial interest. Conflicts arise when one party is asked to check its own work.
f3ff61bd1b788d22: Design-and-build firms. One company designs, prices and builds. That can be efficient, with a single point of responsibility. But the same firm decides how much building the design contains, prices it, and then prices every change. Nobody independent is testing whether the design is efficient or the price is fair, unless you arrange it.
157dc0ce87b8dc04: Consultants checking their own design. When the consultant who designed the villa also reviews the contractor's claims for design-related changes, they are judging, in part, their own drawings. Most consultants handle this professionally. But a variation caused by a design gap is a difficult thing for the designer to call. In August 2025, Dubai Municipality warned villa consultancies about over-designing structures and inflating build costs (Gulf News). A design that is heavier than it needs to be is expensive, and a second, independent look is the simplest way to test it.
737e9f995a41bc40: Fees tied to construction value. Consultant fees in Dubai are commonly a percentage of construction cost. That is market practice, not wrongdoing, but it means the fee structure itself does not reward making the building cheaper.
9d7a69a4207f2f2f: Contractor-employed project managers. The contractor's project manager is there to deliver the contractor's job profitably. That is their job. It is not the same job as protecting your budget.
fffb61199f1fd3b1: Anyone who has run a building company knows the pattern: projects where the client has no independent adviser are commercially easier for the contractor. Provisional sums go unquestioned, variation rates go untested and monthly valuations are rarely challenged. Nobody is doing anything wrong. There is simply no one asking.
4eee4187fb2c559f: Whatever you call the role, put it in writing. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on the final form.

af5751943b2cfadc: Covered in our guide to villa construction contracts in the UAE. The key point here: the contract should name who represents the owner and what that person may do.
03cac42ba396a845: When do you need an owner's representative, and when don't you?
e9b1306704d55409: To be straightforward about it, not every villa needs one.
75fde4587207784c: You probably do not need one if the villa is relatively simple, the design is complete before pricing, you have built before, you live in Dubai, you have time to attend site and read the monthly reports, and you trust your consultant to act firmly for you with the contractor. In that case, a well-appointed consultant and a sound contract may be enough.
cbbdd2779b734526: You probably do need one if any of the following apply:
deba3c5130e46a1d: You live overseas or travel a lot. See building a villa in Dubai from the UK.
931dda10c1b60fba: The villa is large, bespoke or technically demanding: basements, waterfront plots, structural glazing, heavy automation.
581863ffb8321407: You are using a design-and-build firm. See design and build or a separate architect.
43fde72c9e2fdc3a: You have not built before and do not know what a valuation or variation should look like.
953b2682e90fc8b1: The budget matters to you and you want someone with no stake in the price testing it.
693aec6c7d8459f1: The project has stalled or is in dispute.
73a8b6ac6bf3362a: There is no published benchmark for owner's representative fees in Dubai; our guide to client-side project manager fees in Dubai compares the fee models and lists the questions to ask any firm, including us. The test is simple: would independent control of cost, programme and variations save more than it costs? On a straightforward villa, it may not. On a complex one, in our experience, it usually does.
4fc46f36a9a95659: What should you ask before appointing an owner's representative?
b9fb132528c14d10: If you decide you want one, test the fit before you sign; our guide to choosing a client-side project manager goes into more detail. These are the questions we would ask in your position:
fb3dca9e81f677df: Who else pays you on this project? The only acceptable answer is nobody. Ask whether they receive referral fees, commissions or any other benefit from consultants, contractors or suppliers.
530954d442a9eb54: What have you built, and from which side? Experience on the contractor's side, the consultant's side or the developer's side gives different strengths. Ask for specifics, and be wary of anyone who claims experience they cannot describe in detail.
c6959a4cff9066bb: What exactly will you deliver each month? A sample report tells you more than a brochure.
e0cd224180fb3072: How often will you be on site, and who will come? Agree the frequency and the person, not just the firm.
1ded210355b1f85b: What will you not do? A good owner's representative is clear about the boundary with your registered consultant, and will not claim to design, make authority submissions or take on the consultant's statutory role.
91d9ca49b363df59: How is the fee structured? A fixed or time-based fee against a defined scope keeps incentives cleaner than a percentage of construction value.
0131cad73515fa12: An honest answer to the last question often tells you more than the others.
d977e901e355d860: For how these roles fit into the overall sequence, see how to build a villa in Dubai.
497fb95ed7cbb563: We are an independent, client-side owner's representative. We work alongside your registered consultant and your contractor, not instead of them, and we act for the owner alone. Our owner's representative service and our independence page explain how we work and what we will not do. If you are deciding whether you need us at all, ask us; we will tell you honestly.
dd2397c6c5c8a4e7: Is an owner's representative the same as a project manager?
26a00a46acca4ac4: Not quite. The terms overlap and are often used loosely. A project manager can be employed by anyone on the project, including the contractor. An owner's representative acts only for the owner and has no financial interest in the design or construction.
c1894492f911dee6: Can an owner's representative replace my consultant in Dubai?
5e4ee90bcef1b2b8: No. Only registered consultancies may practise engineering consultancy in Dubai. The consultant's design and statutory role cannot be handed to an owner's representative; the two roles work alongside each other.
7fc3d3804e503246: How much does an owner's representative cost?
9f833a93f5192351: There is no published benchmark for owner's representative fees in Dubai. Firms charge a percentage of construction cost, a monthly fee or a fixed fee per review, so compare what each fee covers: the named people, the site attendance, the reports and the exclusions. Agree the fee against a written scope. Our guide to client-side project manager fees in Dubai sets out the questions to ask any firm.
fbed75f567375cbd: Do I need an owner's representative if I use a design-and-build company?
12272d876893634f: It is worth considering. With design and build, one firm designs, prices and builds, so nobody independent is checking the design against your budget or the price against the market unless you arrange it.

881c57bd3948d367: Renovating a villa on Palm Jumeirah starts with a Nakheel NOC, then a building permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits. Anything that changes the structure, the footprint, the façade or the pool needs both; purely cosmetic interior work usually needs far less. The money is usually lost not in the approvals but in what the contractor finds once the walls, roofs and pool shells are opened up.
f1c8335334a2b110: Who approves a villa renovation on Palm Jumeirah?
db5e29679f1a8c7d: Palm Jumeirah is a Nakheel master community. That means two layers of approval sit above your design.
c2e0dee72ca118a8: The master developer. Renovation and extension approvals in Nakheel communities start with an NOC application through Nakheel's portal. Nakheel is checking that your proposal respects the community's design guidelines, plot limits and frontage rules, and that the works will be carried out in a way that does not disrupt neighbours or damage shared infrastructure. Expect to submit drawings, contractor details and, for larger work, a deposit or undertaking. A Nakheel design approval issued in June 2026 shows the pattern: the design is checked against the plot's development control regulations, the approval is valid for six months, and a Nakheel site access NOC and a security deposit for modification works are required before any construction starts, applied for through Nakheel's online services (Nakheel). The same document notes two Palm-specific points: PVC site hoarding is mandatory on Palm Jumeirah, and the gas NOC there comes from a different provider from other Nakheel communities.
49f459d234990801: The permitting authority. With the NOC in hand, your registered consultant applies for the building permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits. Service-authority NOCs now come through one online window rather than door to door. The Build in Dubai platform now covers alterations as well as new builds. Our step-by-step guide to Dubai villa building permits explains what the consultant submits and what the owner signs.
7b8986fd4f037371: The owner appoints the consultant and the contractor. The consultant prepares and submits the drawings; the contractor carries out the work under the permit. Our role at Eastbridge is to represent you alongside both, not to replace either.
0dadea3a5ed94288: What needs approval, and what usually does not?
e17df3422ccfef79: Requirements change, and Nakheel and the authorities publish their own lists, so treat the following as a guide to the conversation, not a ruling.
4fe3d4704c285197: Extensions, new rooms, enclosing terraces, basements
02f587c096f13fce: Nakheel NOC plus building permit; full drawings and structural design
0caa763f1405efba: Façade changes: new openings, cladding, glazing, colour
2a65433384fb67a6: Nakheel NOC (design guidelines apply); permit where structure or openings change
ccdfbd27aeb4f2a3: Nakheel NOC plus permit; structural and MEP drawings
4eb8dbf63218574e: Structural alterations: removing walls, new beams, new stairs
8a32d7f199af663c: Nakheel NOC plus permit; structural engineer's design
52ad345d3b7b7a92: MEP replacement: new AC system, rewiring, plumbing
f6c7f6405f894c4d: Often requires NOC and service authority approvals, depending on scope
5d6b1cd7bf4bcdf2: Kitchen and bathroom refits with no layout or services change
c4c0ed31e2aeb257: Usually lighter or no approval, but confirm with Nakheel first
97bead0db71c7962: Generally cosmetic; access and contractor registration rules still apply
9b938170d6c84191: The point we make to every owner is simple. If you are not sure whether something needs approval, assume it does until the consultant has confirmed otherwise in writing. Unapproved work on the Palm tends to surface at the worst possible moment: when you sell, when you apply for a later extension, or when a neighbour complains. Nakheel has enforced the point before: in 2018, Gulf News reported that Jumeirah Islands owners who altered villas without approval faced fines, alongside a charge for the added space (Gulf News).
536d761a4e77b1fa: In what order should a Palm Jumeirah renovation run?
f9e087bdbf3fc694: A clean sequence saves months. The one we work to looks like this; our plan for a villa renovation in Dubai sets out the same steps for any community.
34a3b41c303e576a: Brief and budget. Agree what you want, what you will spend, and what you would cut first if the numbers come in high.
2a94f791adcc7fac: Condition survey and opening-up. Before any design is fixed, get the existing villa properly inspected: roofs, basement, wet areas, pool, MEP plant and distribution. Where it matters, open up small areas.
5b3c6eafaea622bc: Concept design and early cost check. Your consultant develops the design; get it priced at concept stage, not after the drawings are finished.
0caeae4e72350e3e: Nakheel NOC. Submit through the Nakheel portal. Our guide to the Nakheel NOC for villa renovations explains what triggers one and how to sequence the contractor around it.
5b63617d18501ffb: Detailed design and building permit. Structural, MEP and architectural drawings, then the permit application through the unified window.
c5ceb5e31fba3ba2: Contractor selection. Compare bids like-for-like on the same drawings and specification. Our guide on how to choose a villa contractor in Dubai covers the questions to ask.
d5b627b18afa305e: Contract. Agree scope, price basis, programme, payment terms and how changes are handled. See villa construction contracts in the UAE.
81e64411d4071910: Works, inspections and completion. Staged authority inspections, then completion and handover.
351db42a3603d623: Snagging and defects period. Walk the villa properly before you accept it.
037edc98a8424a55: The most expensive mistake is skipping step 2. On the contractor's side, an incomplete survey was where the commercial opportunity sat. A builder pricing a refurbishment against thin information knows that whatever is hidden will come back as a variation, at rates you no longer have any leverage to negotiate.
6c0c9b6955954a1d: What hidden problems do older Palm villas have?
80f5e14c4ecfe31b: Many of the original frond villas are now around two decades old. They were built quickly, at scale, in a demanding marine environment. In our experience the same issues come up again and again on coastal houses of that age, wherever they are.
40bfd2d449bb25d5: Roof membranes, wet-room tanking, terraces over habitable rooms and basement waterproofing all have a finite life. Failures often show as staining, blistering paint or musty rooms long after the damage has started. Replacing a roof or basement membrane is not a cosmetic job; it means stripping finishes, possibly lifting screeds, and doing it before any new interior goes in.
94a98f12517b604c: Air-conditioning systems, ductwork, pipework and electrical distribution installed when the villa was built may be near the end of their life or undersized for how you want to live now. Have them surveyed: if they do need replacing and you are replacing finishes anyway, it is usually cheaper to do both at the same time than to open the villa up again in three years.
4dcef86afbeec19b: Wind-borne salt attacks external metalwork, fixings, balustrades, window frames, AC condensers and, in the worst cases, reinforcement in concrete where the cover has been compromised. Cracking and rust staining on external concrete need investigating by a structural engineer, not painting over.
d58953a459423007: Pools on older villas commonly have leaking shells, failed tiling and outdated plant. A pool is a structure, and a rebuild sits firmly in the approvals column. One Dubai engineering consultancy puts a basic fibreglass pool at AED 80,000–120,000 and a standard concrete villa pool at AED 150,000–250,000 (Optimal Engineering), which is a useful reality check if the pool is on your list.
495388774126685c: On the contractor's side, the first thing we priced on any refurbishment of an older coastal house was the risk in the envelope. Interiors are predictable. Roofs, basements and anything facing the sea are not, and an honest contractor will tell you so.
5973060f62391482: What does it cost to renovate a villa on Palm Jumeirah?
e7f9cec93adfb721: Published guides disagree, and none of them is specific to the Palm. The table sets two side by side.
a12e680d159311c6: Luxury villa: structural work and premium materials (Palm given as an example)
6280882d274983a3: The contractor's guide cites no sources for its figures. Property Finder's table ties its bands to villa type and scope; it names communities only as examples, not as a reason for a price difference. A full refurbishment of a Palm villa, with new services, waterproofing, kitchen, bathrooms, joinery and external works, will usually sit well inside the luxury band. Three further allowances are worth carrying from the start:
f516441562eb4348: Contingency. Engel & Völkers says a contingency of 10–15% of total project cost is widely recommended on new builds (Engel & Völkers). For a renovation of an older villa, in our experience you should sit at the top of that range or above until the opening-up survey is done.
58300ae1d0ee7173: Preliminaries. Turner & Townsend's 2025 UAE market intelligence puts preliminaries in Dubai at 12% of construction cost on a 2,500 m² project (Turner & Townsend). On a renovation in an occupied community, site set-up, protection, access restrictions and waste removal are real costs, and they should be visible in the bid.
6481c8c1e26bbc54: Inflation. Currie & Brown forecast UAE cost escalation of around 3% for 2026 (TradeArabia); Turner & Townsend forecast 4% for Dubai. On a long design and approvals period, that matters.
7b42bae9183256a3: For a full renovation budget with a worked example, see villa renovation costs in Dubai. For a fuller breakdown of new-build costs, see how much it costs to build a villa in Dubai.
69efedc8513f8049: What are the budget traps on a Palm renovation?
3fb8ba961731b05e: The traps are rarely dramatic. They are small decisions that compound.
224cf17954dc1dca: Provisional sums for the unknown. If the bid carries a modest provisional sum for "waterproofing repairs" or "MEP remedials", the real cost is still unknown. Push for investigation before signing, or at least a clear rate.
a553424ab8ac9d84: Specification drift. Upgrading a finish here and a fitting there feels small. Across a whole villa it is not. Agree a specification and track every change against it.
6c3b45ee81687de7: Design changes after the NOC. Altering an approved design can mean resubmitting to Nakheel and the authority, with time and fees attached.
29d65ce1cc1a78da: Programme slippage. Every extra month is another month of preliminaries, another month of rent if you have moved out, and another month before you can use the house.
ff4917a540d7e3d5: Exclusions. Landscaping, pool plant, AV, lighting control and loose furniture are frequently outside the main contract. Ask what is not included, not just what is.
b648cb0f3a664796: These traps are not unique to the Palm; we cover the seven we saw most often as the contractor in villa renovation mistakes, from the builder's side.
4acd6f843435ff15: Palm Jumeirah is a lived-in, high-value neighbourhood, and your contractor will be working next to people who did not choose to have a building site beside them. Expect access hours, restrictions on deliveries and parking, noise limits, requirements for hoarding and site tidiness, and rules on where waste and materials can sit. Narrow frond roads and shared access make logistics harder than on an open plot.
bc48105c1ed81053: Two practical points. First, a contractor who has not priced for these constraints will either cut corners or come back for more money. Second, good relations with neighbours are worth protecting; a polite letter before work starts and a contact number for complaints prevent a great deal of friction.
7dede0cc0f7f2738: If you plan to stay in the villa during the works, be realistic. For anything involving services, waterproofing or structure, living in it lengthens the programme and adds cost, because the contractor has to phase work around you and protect occupied areas.
83a5692ca06750ec: Should I renovate or rebuild my Palm villa?
3f8694085f101503: This is the question owners least want to ask, and the one that most often needs asking.
d3bb43c96963696b: Renovation makes sense when the structure is sound, the layout broadly works, and your brief is mainly about finishes, kitchens, bathrooms, services and outdoor space. Rebuild deserves serious consideration when the brief keeps expanding towards new structure, a reworked envelope, full services replacement and significant extensions. At that point you can end up paying for much of a new house while still working within the constraints of the old one, and carrying the risk of whatever the existing structure is hiding.
17e82f7699b2164a: Our rule of thumb: once the renovation scope starts to look like a new building, get both routes priced properly by your consultant before committing. A rebuild means a longer approvals route and a longer programme, but it also gives you a new house with known construction and a full set of warranties.
4fc8ca2b6f440b84: We represent the owner on villa renovations, working alongside your registered consultant and your chosen contractor. 88af27411151c92a: Published 2026 renovation rates run from about AED 120–250 per sq ft for basic work to AED 250–450 for mid-range and AED 450 or more for luxury or structural work; new-build construction runs from about AED 300–500 per sq ft at a standard specification to AED 850–1,200 or more for luxury, before fees.
604a99aa25cb8725: On our worked example, a 6,000 sq ft villa costs roughly AED 1.9m–3.7m to renovate at mid-range (about AED 460 per sq ft likely) and AED 3.8m–7.3m to knock down and rebuild at premium (about AED 910 per sq ft likely), including fees, contingency and rent while the family lives elsewhere.
d01f05075c154dfa: A rebuild takes about 14–23 months from the start of design to keys on published phase estimates, but the family can usually stay in the old villa through design and approvals, so the months out of the house are fewer.
e93cc3de12ded19d: Rebuilding wins when the existing structure, services or waterproofing are failing, when the plot allows meaningfully more floor area, or when the layout cannot be made to work; it rarely wins on cost per square foot alone.
b8df35551d3d94fd: Decide on evidence: a condition survey and some opening-up of the existing villa, then a cost plan for each option, before any design is fixed.
79a7e39da15eef92: What does each option cost per square foot?
075d390887657fa5: A worked example: 6,000 sq ft, mid-range renovation against a premium rebuild
331757d9b352a822: For most Dubai villas with a sound structure, renovating costs less per square foot of finished space than knocking down and rebuilding, and gets the family home sooner. Rebuilding earns its place when the structure, services or waterproofing are failing, when the plot allows a meaningfully larger villa, or when the layout cannot be fixed without major structural change. The decision should rest on a condition survey and a cost plan for each option, not on a headline rate.
bb15ee9fb149eeaf: We spent 21 years as the builder in UK premium residential construction, pricing both kinds of job. The renovations that went wrong were rarely the ones with a large budget. They were the ones where nobody had looked properly at the existing building before the price was agreed. This guide sets out the published figures, how to compare the two options fairly, and the questions that usually decide it. Our renovate or rebuild tool runs the same comparison on your own numbers.
080aea9ebf63b15a: What does each option cost per square foot?
8a679bd4ca287814: The fair comparison is cost per square foot of finished space, with the soft costs included. A renovation rate applies to the villa you already have. A rebuild rate applies to the new built-up area, and comes with demolition on top.
dd36fd7b9d6d4e55: Published rate, AED per sq ft
4ee142300fb7592a: A Dubai renovation contractor's guide
e77ef6634a0ca3e7: The renovation sources disagree. Property Finder's villa range starts higher than the contractor's basic band and runs well past its mid-range band, and neither publisher explains how its figures were built, so treat any one band as a starting point rather than a price. Our villa renovation cost guide sets the published ranges side by side.
c612ae40f544e178: Those are construction rates. On a rebuild, design and engineering fees typically add 6–12% of the construction cost, and Optimal Engineering recommends a contingency of 10–15%; Engel & Völkers calls 10–15% "widely recommended". Approvals, NOCs and connections add a further sum, and demolition of the existing villa is an extra line: our cost calculator uses AED 50,000–200,000, the only published figure we have found. A renovation that touches structure, façade or services carries fees and approvals too; a cosmetic refresh usually does not.
9b835a6406ab7bb2: Two things make the renovation rate less reassuring than it looks. First, the published bands describe typical villas. An older villa that needs new services, new waterproofing and a new roof finish sits at the top of the range or above it. Second, the rate is per square foot of the existing house. If the family needs more space, a renovation can only add it as an extension, which brings structural work, approvals and a much higher rate for the new area.
aeb30d4f8895ab97: The same source also publishes whole-villa bands for a typical villa (basic AED 200,000–300,000, mid-range AED 400,000–800,000, luxury from AED 1 million), and our cost calculator uses those bands for its renovation mode. They do not change with floor area, so for the 6,000 sq ft villa below the calculator shows mid-range works of AED 400,000–800,000, while the per square foot rates give AED 1.5m–2.7m. The two do not reconcile. For a large villa, the rate per square foot is the more realistic basis, and it is the one our renovate-or-rebuild tool and this article use.

92f53bd9bb088e16: Take a 6,000 sq ft villa. One option is a mid-range renovation: kitchens, bathrooms, interiors. The other is to demolish and rebuild at the same size to a premium specification. In both cases the family rents a four-bedroom villa while the house is unusable, at the Dubai average of AED 343,461 a year from Engel & Völkers' May 2026 rental data, about AED 28,600 a month.
a92350b042ca5c4e: Rent while out of the house
c572699cbeae9f03: Likely cost per sq ft of finished space
e682933044c1d8af: Start of works or design to completion
41c0dcaeb513d7d3: The figures come from our renovate or rebuild tool, which uses the same rates as the cost calculator, rounded line by line. They exclude the plot, pool, landscaping, furniture, finance and VAT. The UAE's general VAT rate is 5%, so check whether your quotes include it.
373ecabacbedb044: On these numbers, the rebuild costs about twice as much. That is the usual picture. The question is what the extra money buys, and whether the renovation figure is real.
9db8a3554c05896e: Change one assumption and the picture moves. If the existing villa needs a luxury or structural renovation, the published rate starts at AED 450 per sq ft, and the same 6,000 sq ft villa starts at about AED 3.3m with fees, contingency and six months of rent. That is close to the bottom of the rebuild range, for a building that keeps its old structure, its old slab levels and its old ceiling heights.
16ce0a361640e4eb: If the plot's rules allow a larger villa, say 8,000 sq ft instead of 6,000, the rebuild's likely cost rises to about AED 7.1m but the cost per square foot of finished space falls slightly, to about AED 890, because demolition, approvals and part of the fees do not grow with the floor area. The renovation cannot add that space without an extension.
48f3e755016cdf27: How long does each option take?
53c80d3bb3ddbcaa: Renovation is quicker by a wide margin. The renovation contractor's guide puts interior upgrades at around two to three months, kitchens and bathrooms at four to six months, and structural changes, extensions or a complete redesign at six months or longer. Approvals for a renovation, where they are needed, typically take a few weeks. Our villa renovation timeline shows where those months go, phase by phase.
a2ec3846c6aaa039: A rebuild runs through the full sequence. The phase estimates we use, the only phase-by-phase breakdown we have found (published by a property information website), are design 3–4 months, approvals 2–3, construction 8–14 and snagging 1–2: about 14–23 months end to end, less where phases overlap, and 24–36 months for a custom luxury villa. Engel & Völkers puts most villas at 12–24 months from approval to completion, and Optimal Engineering typically allows 12–18 months for construction.
5e76ee69159343ee: What matters to most families, though, is the time out of the house. On a rebuild, the old villa usually stays habitable while the new one is designed and approved. The move comes at demolition, so the months away are construction plus snagging, roughly 9–16 months on the same estimates. That is still two to three times longer than a mid-range renovation, and every month has a cost. Our delay cost estimator shows how quickly rent and finance add up when a programme slips.
9b95190f3b4c3c7d: What approvals does each option need?
52103b03f65154b6: The approvals burden is often the deciding factor for owners who live abroad.
3af1c061188a8ab0: A renovation that leaves structure, façade and services alone often needs no authority permit, although the master developer may still require an NOC; in Nakheel communities, for example, renovation and extension approvals start with an NOC application through Nakheel's portal. Structural changes, extensions, façade changes, a new pool and most services replacement need the master developer's NOC and a permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits. Our guide to the Nakheel NOC covers that sequence.
4c00b4b94cc074c5: A rebuild needs approval to demolish, then the whole permit sequence for a new villa. Dubai Municipality's published procedure for residential buildings runs from drawings and fees submitted online by your registered consultant, through authority NOCs, to the permit and stamped drawings, staged inspections, a joint completion inspection, the completion certificate and service connection (Dubai Municipality). The new design must comply with the current Dubai Building Code. Our Dubai Municipality permit guide explains where those months go.
15788f2f112711e6: There is a quieter point here. An older villa may have been built to earlier rules. A renovation generally works with what was approved; a rebuild must meet today's code and today's community guidelines, which can change setbacks, heights or what is permitted on the roof. Ask your consultant to check both before you assume the new villa can match the old one, let alone exceed it.
46ea82dd20feaed7: From the builder's side, the jobs where we told a client to stop and think again shared a pattern. The structure was tired, the services were at the end of their life and the layout fought the way the family wanted to live. Each of those can be fixed in a renovation. All three together usually cannot be fixed economically.
cef0ca2bc6841a8d: Rebuilding tends to make sense when:
3465569a442aeb44: The structure or waterproofing is failing. Cracking, corroded reinforcement, persistent leaks through roofs, terraces or basements. Repairs are possible but expensive, and they leave you with an old building.
9e8b89766c7adc44: The services are finished. Replacing cooling, electrics, plumbing and drainage throughout means opening every wall and ceiling. At that point most of the renovation cost is demolition and making good. See rewiring and replumbing an older Dubai villa for how to find out before you decide.
8cb313469fea10c9: The plot allows a much larger or better villa. If the permitted built-up area, height or layout allows meaningfully more house, the rebuild buys space a renovation cannot.
1f79bfa5bc7a3117: The layout cannot work. Moving stairs, changing floor-to-ceiling heights or opening up structural walls on every floor is a rebuild by another name.
eaf66b106580191d: Renovation tends to make sense when the structure is sound, the services can be upgraded in sections, the family likes the house and its position on the plot, and time out of the house matters.
2f3f20de67495942: Most owners face this decision with two numbers: a contractor's price for a renovation and a rough idea of what a new villa costs. Neither is enough. The renovation price was given for what the contractor could see, and the new-build figure leaves out demolition, fees, approvals, contingency and the cost of living elsewhere for a year or more.
c1804c4d540d2e69: Commission a condition survey and opening-up. Expose the structure, the roof build-up, the waterproofing and the services in representative places before any design is fixed. It is the cheapest money on the whole project.
00f53753cd4789c0: Check what the plot allows. Ask your consultant to confirm the permitted built-up area, height and setbacks, and the master developer's guidelines, so the rebuild option is real.
3573cbb24bf70112: Price both options on the same basis. Construction, demolition, fees, approvals, contingency, rent and time, line by line. Our cost calculator and the renovate or rebuild tool give a first view; a cost plan from your consultant should follow.
13189b062df242b8: Watch the design. In August 2025 Dubai Municipality warned villa engineering consultancies about over-designing structures and inflating build costs (Gulf News). A design review before tender is usually cheaper than a variation after it.
210f13d7ddd8806b: Plan the cash. A rebuild is paid over a longer period, with an advance, monthly valuations and retention. Our stage payment planner shows what leaves your account each month.
eff0344a391206e5: Our guide to villa renovation costs covers the hidden costs that catch out older villas, and what it costs to build a villa in Dubai covers the new-build side in more detail.
98ddf7ad517675e0: We represent the owner, not the contractor or the consultant. On a renovate-or-rebuild decision we work alongside your DM-registered consultant to get the condition evidence and the plot constraints in front of you, then put both options on the same footing: cost, time, approvals and risk. You decide, with numbers you can test. See our villa renovation project management service, or contact us for a free 30-minute call.
5338c14701921cb6: Is it cheaper to renovate or rebuild a villa in Dubai?
bee33d74f7abc847: Usually cheaper to renovate if the structure is sound. One Dubai renovation contractor's 2026 figures put renovation at about AED 120–450 or more per sq ft depending on scope, and Property Finder gives a wider villa range of AED 150–600, while new-build construction starts at about AED 300–500 per sq ft at a standard specification and rises to AED 850–1,200 or more for luxury, before demolition, design fees, approvals and contingency. A deep renovation of an older villa can close much of that gap.
ffd2db4cff9cd671: How long does it take to knock down and rebuild a villa in Dubai?
a93c608d146229c7: Published phase estimates are design 3–4 months, approvals 2–3, construction 8–14 and snagging 1–2, about 14–23 months end to end, and 24–36 months for a custom luxury villa. Engel & Völkers puts most villas at 12–24 months from approval to completion.
73cd8b5823308731: Do I need a permit to demolish and rebuild a villa?
417b34822b6b78f4: Yes. Demolition needs approval, and a new villa needs a full building permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits, usually after a master developer NOC. Your DM-registered consultant makes the submissions; the new design must meet the current Dubai Building Code.
d1327a3b03349256: When does rebuilding make more sense than renovating?
5e9070b69caaf369: When the existing structure, services or waterproofing are failing, when the plot's rules allow a much larger villa, or when the layout cannot be made to work without major structural change. In those cases the renovation cost rises towards a rebuild and the rebuild buys a new building.
723d1648e0f2df7b: Can I live in the villa during a renovation?
c5399c9df77c467d: During a light refresh, sometimes. During a full renovation with new services, structural work or waterproofing, rarely: the house is usually without power, water or cooling for long stretches. Budget for living elsewhere for the length of the works.

d5f69d05337d26e1: What should you check when imported materials arrive?
caf5ee26e17b6e74: Sourcing stone, joinery, lighting and fittings abroad is one of the best ways to make a one-off Dubai villa feel like nobody else's, and one of the easiest ways to lose months. It works when every choice is fixed in a signed sample or mock-up, each order is placed early enough to survive production, shipping, customs and any conformity checks, and someone checks what arrives against what was chosen. It goes wrong when beautiful things are bought on enthusiasm and the programme is left to catch up.
adcf996fa9f56f64: This article explains how to plan it, what UAE customs and conformity rules mean for the timing, and what to check when the crates arrive.
333017d3767b97a2: Why source materials abroad for a Dubai villa?
01118d547f846362: Dubai has a deep local supply market, and for many items a local supplier is the sensible choice: shorter lead times, local stock for replacements, and someone in the same city to call when something is wrong. Owners go abroad for the things that define the house. A particular quarry's marble, a joinery workshop whose detailing they have seen in person, a lighting maker, or ironmongery and sanitaryware that simply are not stocked locally.
bf2ffc2669f4bd60: That choice is worth making deliberately, item by item. A useful test is whether you would notice the difference standing in the finished room. If you would, it may be worth the extra lead time and risk. If you would not, buy locally and spend the time elsewhere.
f618c33a4a9baf08: Morvoren, Feock, Cornwall. Built by P Chapman Construction.
255615a98fb25cd5: What did we learn from sourcing trips with UK clients?
9a077ed24f2d6d65: This is P Chapman Construction's UK experience. On the high-end houses our founder, Philip Chapman, built over 21 years, he regularly travelled with clients to choose stone, joinery and fittings, in the UK and abroad. Three lessons from those trips carry straight over to a Dubai villa.
6a869b39becfea01: Choose the actual material, not a catalogue name. Natural stone varies from block to block and from slab to slab. The same named marble can look quite different from one batch to the next. On the builder's side, we learned to ask for the slabs to be laid out together before they were cut, photographed, numbered and reserved, so the client was choosing the stone that would actually be fitted.
7bc5f4ca8c8aac73: Sign the sample and keep it. Every agreed sample, whether a stone offcut, a timber and finish board, a door handle or a light fitting, was labelled, signed and dated by the client and kept as the reference. When a delivery arrived months later, it was checked against that sample, not against anyone's memory of a showroom.
2cae3ae25d3e9317: Talk to the people who will make it. The most useful hour of many trips was spent in the workshop, not the showroom: how they pack for long journeys, what they need from site to make templates, and what they consider an acceptable variation. Those answers belong in the order, in writing.
6cacb69f227cbc30: How do samples and mock-ups protect the owner?
a3d3be40aa748c1c: Samples fix the material. Mock-ups fix how it goes together. For anything that will be repeated across the house, such as a stone floor, a run of joinery, a bathroom wall or a lighting scheme, ask for a mock-up before full production.
eb80e75801c4ff92: What to agree in a sample or mock-up
c81c6a5c349a37a0: Slab selection, vein direction and matching, finish (polished, honed, brushed), edge details, sealant
4d4da481f50f580f: Timber species and finish, door and drawer construction, hinges and runners, how it fixes to walls in a humid climate
eea27cb9d283ebff: Colour temperature, beam angle, dimming behaviour with the chosen control system, finish
33aa23a3b7bbc7a6: Finish and how it ages, operation, compatibility with the doors and sanitaryware it will fit
89f88f605145cd3e: Mock-ups are also where a contractor's and a supplier's assumptions meet. If the stone fixer, the joiner and the electrician all see the same mock-up, fewer things are argued about later. Agree in the contract who builds it, where, and who pays if it has to be rebuilt.
31dde02b958c9fb2: How should lead times be planned?
29316be156f5c167: Plan backwards from the date each item must be on site, not forwards from the date you fall in love with it. For each imported package, the programme needs room for:
971217d76d180a98: Final design and sample sign-off, including any shop drawings the supplier prepares.
92f0f823ebba6cb9: Production, which for bespoke joinery or stone can be the longest stage.
e013bd6a60838acd: Packing and delivery to the port or airport.
3732ef1fb110dac8: Customs clearance in the UAE, and any conformity documents that must be in place.
192e28ede2164fef: Delivery to site, storage, and acclimatisation where the material needs it.
57c2a51d520317c6: Installation by the contractor or the supplier's fitters.
0e4c8c1a971602a9: Ask each supplier for their lead time in writing, ask what it assumes, and add your own allowance for the stages they do not control. In our experience, the dates that slip are rarely production dates. They are the decisions that come before production, and the paperwork that comes after it.
42764d0caceed902: Tie these dates to the contractor's programme. If a stone floor arrives after the date the contractor needs it, the contractor may have a claim for delay. We cover the overall timeline in how long it takes to build a villa in Dubai.
6fafb87871a15749: Who should buy the materials: you or the contractor?
49a57fb61f4d41a4: This is the decision that matters most commercially, and it should be made before the building contract is signed.
46995e446e36bed1: Contractor-supplied. The item sits inside the contract, often as a prime cost sum that is adjusted once the item is chosen. The contractor orders it, carries the delivery and quality risk, and adds the agreed mark-up. You keep the choice; the contractor keeps the risk.
08b9f80d9c179c51: Owner-supplied. You buy direct, often at a better price, and the contractor fixes it. From the builder's side, we always priced owner-supplied items carefully: unloading, storage, protection, fixing, and the time lost if the item arrived late, damaged or wrong. Any of those can become a variation or a delay claim. The contractor will also usually give no warranty on a product they did not supply.
c0bae6f0e1e44939: Neither route is wrong. What causes disputes is leaving it unclear. For each imported package, the contract should say who buys it, who receives and checks it, who stores it, who carries the risk of damage, and what happens to the programme if it is late.
387dd72bea130211: How do shipping terms affect who pays and who is responsible?
05a3a855ba388dee: International sales normally use the ICC Incoterms rules, which set where the seller's responsibility ends and the buyer's begins. Under EXW (Ex Works), the buyer collects from the seller's premises and must complete any import formalities; the ICC suggests considering FCA instead where possible. Under DDP (Delivered Duty Paid), the seller must handle import formalities, and the ICC notes that some countries restrict foreign entities from doing so and recommends DAP instead of DDP where possible (ICC Academy).
8f7b3249dd951eeb: For an owner, the practical points are simple. Know which term applies, know who arranges insurance for the journey, and appoint a licensed freight forwarder and clearing agent in Dubai before the goods leave the factory, not after they reach the port.
6f1391337b36323a: What UAE customs duty and VAT apply to imported materials?
871b53ffcb4b7808: The UAE is part of the GCC customs union, which applies a common duty of 5% on goods imported from outside the union, with listed exemptions and higher rates for some goods (Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security). Duty is generally charged on the cost, insurance and freight (CIF) value of the import (PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries).
900f1bff7d961781: The standard UAE VAT rate is 5% (PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries). The Federal Tax Authority's import guide says import VAT is calculated on the value of the goods including any customs duty and excise tax due, and that importers not registered for VAT must pay the applicable taxes before the goods are cleared (Federal Tax Authority).
cd78b3853de13745: Classification matters. Dubai applies the 2022 edition of the GCC Unified Customs Tariff, based on the World Customs Organization's Harmonized System (Dubai Customs). Ask your clearing agent to confirm the tariff code and duty for each item before you place the order, and build both duty and VAT into the budget.
a541e875e7f808b8: Paperwork is the other half. Dubai Customs requires customs declarations and their required documents to be submitted within 30 days of completing the declaration, with a late fee of AED 5 a day up to AED 300, and records kept for five years (Dubai Customs). In practice, delays at clearance usually come from documents that do not match: an invoice, packing list and transport document that describe the same crate differently. Ask the supplier to send drafts for checking before shipment.
38cd2c8dc704b2f9: Do imported products need UAE conformity approval?
eae91e62a4d8e945: Some do, and this is where an imported item can sit in a warehouse while the programme moves on without it.
2602ec6cd69ca5ed: Regulated products. The Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology issues UAE Certificates of Conformity for products subject to technical regulations, supported by a test report from an accredited laboratory (MoIAT). Electrical items, including lighting, should be checked against the regulated products list before you buy.
88227945696a0ba8: Fire and life safety products. Products such as fire detection and suppression equipment and emergency lighting need a UAE Civil Defence Certificate of Conformity issued through an approved body (BSI).
0a9fd69ac76341f1: Construction materials testing. Dubai Central Laboratory, part of Dubai Municipality, tests cement and other construction materials for consultants and contractors in Dubai (Dubai Media Office). 517e46a92aa3e8db: None of this is a reason not to import. It is a reason to ask every supplier, before you order, for the test reports and certificates they already hold, and to have your registered consultant confirm what applies. The same questions apply whether your villa is in Dubai or Abu Dhabi.
71eda97aa58113e7: What should you check when imported materials arrive?
4d77ef46c5923208: Arrival is the last chance to reject something cheaply. Once stone is cut and fixed, or joinery is installed, every problem becomes a negotiation. Check each delivery before the delivery note is signed:
280466d46b60ab22: Against the order: quantities, sizes, finishes and product codes match the order and the packing list.
262991b17699daf7: Against the signed sample: colour, veining, finish and texture match the reference you kept.
b99385a82472183e: Condition: crates opened and inspected for breakage, chips, water damage and warping, with photographs taken before anything is moved.
0a04fb0ad88f52fa: Documents: certificates of conformity, test reports, warranties, care instructions and spare parts are handed over with the goods.
b82692f241154649: Storage: the material is stored where the supplier says it should be, protected from sun, heat, humidity and other trades.
d350b899bea0934c: Record any shortfall or damage in writing on the day, with photographs, and notify the supplier and the insurer straight away. We cover the final checks in our villa snagging checklist.
86c28376be2d0fa9: Where do sourcing budgets usually leak?
887b9af1dfec3446: In our experience from the builder's side, the leaks are predictable: allowances in the contract set below the quality the owner actually chooses; duty, VAT, freight and clearing left out of the comparison with a local supplier; spares and extra stone for future repairs never ordered; and the contractor's handling and fixing of owner-supplied items priced late, as a variation. A sourcing schedule that lists every imported item, its landed cost and its required-on-site date closes most of these gaps. It sits naturally alongside the cost report described in villa construction cost in Dubai.
f5f4a24bb6499baa: Sourcing is part of our full service for one-off villas. We travel with you to choose stone, joinery, lighting and fittings, record every sample and decision, build the sourcing schedule into the programme and the cost report, and check what arrives against what you chose. We take no commission, referral fee or discount from any supplier; you pay suppliers direct, and travel is charged at cost. We cover every community in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. See materials and specialist sourcing, owner's representation, our fees, or contact us to talk it through.
0c58291407d8bb5e: How much customs duty will I pay on materials imported into Dubai?
71fd10d69caafc91: Goods from outside the GCC generally pay customs duty of 5% on their cost, insurance and freight value under the GCC common tariff, with some goods charged at different rates. Import VAT is then calculated on the value including any duty. Your clearing agent should confirm the tariff code and rate for each item before you buy.
ca6ce716a9866612: Should I buy materials myself or let the contractor buy them?
e2ba8b361f74d77e: Either can work. If the contractor buys, the item sits inside the contract and the contractor carries delivery and quality risk. If you buy, you control the choice and the price, but you also take on lead time, damage, customs and warranty risk, and the contractor will price handling and fixing separately. 35afda856c2b4c23: Do imported light fittings need approval in the UAE?
d52fa5597e988992: Some may. Products covered by a UAE technical regulation need a Certificate of Conformity from the Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology, and emergency lighting falls under the Civil Defence certification scheme. Ask the supplier for test reports early and have your registered consultant confirm what applies to each fitting.

fe0e347a61022d18: No. We take no commission, referral fee or discount from any supplier. Every price we negotiate is the owner's price, and the owner pays the supplier direct.
5dbca48980d0018d: Can you come with me on a sourcing trip?
ee5160e8525a5387: Yes. Travelling with the owner to choose stone, joinery and fittings is part of our full service. Travel is charged at cost, and we agree the trips in the written scope of works.

Only then choose between getting the current contractor back on track, renegotiating, or a managed change of contractor, which Dubai Municipality allows under a published procedure.
412d024291076395: A stalled site is stressful because everyone has a different story. The contractor says it has not been paid. The consultant says the contractor is late. The owner has often paid well over half the contract sum for a building that looks less than half finished. We spent 21 years as the builder in UK premium residential construction. From the builder's side, we know how a stalled job looks from the contractor's chair, and what an incoming builder needs before it will price the rest. This is what we would want any owner to do, in order.
5b0bfb4a58b7517a: A stall is a symptom. Before deciding what to do, work out which of a small number of causes you are looking at, because each calls for a different response.
be582da7cc67af10: The contractor's cash flow is under strain, on your job or across its business
273a9351de0348b3: Have all valued payments been made, and is the contractor paying its own supply chain?
67f0f214b8438518: Work stopped in one area, waiting
095c9ecc190182db: Missing or late design information, or an unmade owner decision
5aec517345180512: Is there an outstanding request for information or selection, and whose is it?
ccd0201cd3944bbf: A formal letter about suspension or delay
a4d5b2216abd0d08: A dispute about payment, variations or time
b8d127b472cd8136: What does the contract say about notices, suspension and extensions?
9b09c8416fa53df7: Contractor over-committed elsewhere, or deliberately slowing to force a negotiation
48e484044286e165: What does the programme say, and when was it last updated?
a7085ffdb2a4f008: A dispute between owner and consultant, or a consultant stretched too thin
a6bfa826888352c7: Is the consultant's appointment and fee position in order?
51eead247393a0d9: Abandonment, insolvency or a serious dispute
44899cfabb7dec25: Has the contractor responded in writing, and is it still trading?
2cee00b3db0226bb: On the builder's side, a slowing site was almost always a cash signal before it was a programme signal. Labour goes first, then the subcontractors stop returning calls, then the letters start. An owner who notices the first stage and asks the right questions early has far more options than one who waits for the letter.
39323ef0eebe91b7: What should I do in the first ten days?
5f8ec5b08df349e7: The checklist below is the order we recommend. It is deliberately conservative: nothing in it closes off an option, and everything in it improves your position whichever route you choose.
ec7d83d3831f64d1: Visit, photograph and video the whole site, dated
19641d5b27745ba7: Fixes the state of the works before anything is moved, removed or disputed
3cb48bae3ac9f9b0: Check site security, hoarding, safety and weather protection
229f2172c6184adf: An open, unprotected site deteriorates and creates liability
49c8601af73a38fd: Write to the contractor asking for the reason and a return date
f341147af35e7dbc: Puts the position on record and invites a reply you can rely on
f2608cb9ec2a1d55: Gather the contract, drawings, programme, valuations, payments and correspondence
da54af283d034c2c: You cannot assess anything you cannot find
a561b9d1edd63725: Pause further payments until the position is checked
d03b4f605cbf7d1a: Money paid ahead of work is leverage lost
c0dd1627c2807857: Read the termination, suspension, notice and dispute clauses with a lawyer
ac34c624dd4c150e: A wrongful termination can turn a strong position into a weak one
74f7f8199e3740a7: Confirm the permit, insurance and bond position
146ad009b3f248c7: Expiring cover or guarantees cannot be recovered later
3624c886dba2a637: Ask your consultant for a technical assessment of progress and quality
aa06af32773f7942: It is the basis of any restart, renegotiation or changeover
6b581eebc7e98955: Reconcile what has been paid against what has been built
3f911f80422646c3: Tells you whether you are ahead of or behind the work
b5533b0d3de349b4: Estimate the cost and time to complete, and set out the options
9bbcdbe5f026d3c8: Turns a crisis into a decision
6dced5fbb587d8f0: Days 1–2: secure the site and the record
170d795cb6cb196e: Go to site, or send someone you trust. Photograph and video every room, elevation and service run, with dates. Note what materials are on site and what plant has been removed. Check the hoarding, access control, temporary power and water, and anything open to the weather, such as unprotected roof membranes, exposed reinforcement or stored finishes. Under many contracts these risks sit with the contractor while it is in possession of the site, but a deteriorating building is your problem whoever pays for it.
efad380ae81e448a: Days 2–3: pause the money, not the conversation
a10381103b847bec: Keep talking to the contractor, politely and in writing. Ask why work has stopped and when it will resume. But pause any payment not yet properly valued until you know where you stand. Pay only what has been properly valued and approved under the contract for work actually done, and take legal advice before withholding anything the contract says is due, because an unjustified non-payment can hand the contractor a right to suspend.
325cdef45488fa44: On the contractor's side, the request we dreaded most from a client was not an angry phone call. It was a calm letter asking for an updated programme, a list of outstanding information and a reconciliation of the account. Those three documents show quickly who is really behind.
fe353d367ad52862: Days 3–5: read the contract before acting on it
afb7a0cc598de19a: Find the clauses on suspension, termination, notices, extensions of time, liquidated damages, retention, bonds and disputes. Notice periods matter: many contracts require a notice of default and a period to remedy it before termination is possible. This is general information, not legal advice; your contract and UAE law decide what you can do, so take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer at this point, not after you have sent a termination letter. Our guide to villa construction contracts in the UAE explains the main mechanisms, and if the dispute is about variations or time, see how we help with variations, delays and claims.
f1fee7d73935dd2e: Check three time-sensitive items at the same time: whether the building permit and its conditions remain in order (ask your consultant), whether the contractor's all-risks and liability insurance is still in force, and when any performance bond or advance payment guarantee expires. A bond that lapses during a dispute protects no one.
19b2b360d1498997: Days 5–8: establish what has actually been built
3057809c673900ed: Ask your registered consultant for a technical assessment of the stage of the works and whether they conform to the permit and the approved drawings. Alongside it, reconcile the money: total valued, total paid, retention held, variations agreed and variations claimed. Compare that with what is physically in place. If the payments have run ahead of the work, you need to know by how much.
627fbc974e03cf6b: Days 7–10: cost to complete, and the options
6a958ef6db4c7bf8: With the record and the reconciliation in hand, estimate what it will cost and how long it will take to finish. Then set out the options side by side: bring the current contractor back with a recovery programme, renegotiate scope or terms, or replace the contractor. A changeover carries real costs in time, re-pricing and risk.
a669dcbfda948830: Not in the first ten days, and not without legal advice. Termination is sometimes right, but it is a legal step with consequences, and a contractor that has been terminated wrongly may have a claim against you.
de9a7cb2670d54f1: For context, a Gulf News legal column published in 2024 describes the general position under Article 877 of the UAE Civil Transactions Law: where a contractor performs defectively or contrary to the agreement, the owner may require it to put matters right within a reasonable time and, if it fails, may ask the court to cancel the contract or to authorise completion by another contractor at the first contractor's expense. How that applies to your contract is a question for a UAE-qualified lawyer.
9ac2da9118a8486b: How do I change contractor on a Dubai villa?
d7052453f1c187c7: Dubai Municipality's Administrative Resolution No. 10 of 2019 sets out the procedures for replacing an engineering consultant or a contractor on applications made to the municipality. In summary, as the English translation on the Dubai Legislation Portal describes it (the Arabic text prevails):
aebfbd1ba95647af: With the outgoing contractor's agreement: your engineering consultant submits the application, signed by the consultant and the outgoing contractor, with a declaration from the owner approving the change and, where a permit has been issued, the consultant's technical report on the stage of the works and their conformity with the permit and approved plans.
728b90a3cb475a66: Without its agreement: the consultant submits the application with the owner's declaration, the reasons for the change and the technical report. The municipality notifies the outgoing contractor, which has five working days to give its reasons and its own technical report. If it does not respond, the municipality proceeds. Where the dispute is financial or contractual, the municipality proceeds with the replacement; where it is technical, the municipality verifies the issues first.
985f5db13cb9ec05: In both cases: the replacement contractor must be licensed, with a classification not lower than the building requires, and may not start work until a new building permit is issued in its name, on payment of the prescribed fees and security.
e2a0e39c5b66bb08: Dubai Municipality publishes a request form for changing a consultant or contractor, with and without agreement, and its online building permit system includes the change of consultant or contractor among its services. Your consultant makes the application, through the Build in Dubai platform or the authority's own system. If your permit was issued by Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority rather than Dubai Municipality, the route may differ, so ask your consultant to confirm the procedure for your plot. In communities with a master developer, check whether the developer's own approvals also need updating.
f3cda5ea74d064f5: What about a stalled villa in Abu Dhabi?
07a44505503809d0: The principles are the same: secure the site, preserve the record, pause unvalued payments, take legal advice and establish what has been built. The procedure is not. In Abu Dhabi the Department of Municipalities and Transport regulates private villas and permits are handled by the municipalities through TAMM. Ask your consultant to confirm the current requirements for changing a contractor on your permit before you commit to a changeover.
dfc1aee4be052f15: What does an incoming contractor need to price the rest fairly?
fbdc7a5aea7f5c70: An incoming contractor prices the unknown first: work it cannot see, quality it cannot verify, materials it cannot account for and paperwork it does not have. Every unknown goes into the price as risk.
933bf16fa6b956a9: An incoming contractor prices more keenly when it receives:
9cd70a7db72078ec: A dated photographic and written record of the works in place, including concealed work recorded before it was covered, where it exists.
c4738cbe2f3eb406: The consultant's technical report on progress and conformity.
114659ab2473b263: A defects list, so the new contractor is not later blamed for, or paid twice for, the previous contractor's work.
f88498749440a2a7: An inventory of materials and equipment on site, with ownership confirmed.
7c88c2f97120e56d: The current drawings, specification and outstanding design information, with nothing left open that can be closed.
4351af7afb7d47ee: A clear scope to complete, separating remedial work from new work.
e4231a3c7511f32c: Without that pack, a recovery price carries every doubt as contingency. With it, the job can usually restart at a fair price.
180f6a9b95c7b040: What mistakes make a stalled villa worse?
00e1877ddd52cf10: Paying an advance or a "goodwill" sum to get labour back, with no change to the programme or the terms.
c351781589888894: Terminating by email in frustration, before checking notice provisions and taking legal advice.
0df305cceb96d018: Letting another builder start work before the change is approved and a new permit is in place.
8e830292c2ad67be: Allowing the outgoing contractor to remove materials or equipment without an agreed inventory.
cdf34a5551cb3699: Letting the bond, the insurance or the defects record lapse while attention is on the argument.
f7592eacd637069f: Agreeing a new price for "finishing" without separating remedial work from incomplete work.
6a608cad4871584a: Most of these come from the same instinct: wanting the site busy again quickly. A week spent establishing the facts usually saves months later.

d07b6cf7ec069d6b: What should I do if my villa contractor stops work in Dubai?
1be3ddf45ac520ff: Photograph and record the site, write to the contractor asking for the reason and a date to return, pause any payment not yet properly valued until the position is checked, and ask your registered consultant for an assessment of progress and quality. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer before withholding sums the contract says are due or terminating the contract.
40027e5532403b59: Can I change contractor halfway through a villa build in Dubai?
91b77941d3630cad: Yes. Where Dubai Municipality issued the permit, its Administrative Resolution No. 10 of 2019 sets out procedures for replacing a contractor both with and without the outgoing contractor's consent. The engineering consultant submits the application with an owner's declaration and, where a permit has been issued, a technical report on the stage and conformity of the works. If your permit came from Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, ask your consultant to confirm the procedure.
341bf5a75e888953: What if the outgoing contractor refuses to agree to the change?
0a4ec8fa03d95e82: Under the resolution, Dubai Municipality notifies the outgoing contractor, who has five working days to respond with its reasons and a technical report. If it does not respond, the municipality proceeds. If the dispute is financial or contractual, the municipality proceeds with the replacement; if it is technical, it verifies the issues first.
847ea269ae848aaf: How long does it take to restart a stalled villa?
fbbef1f2a5143de2: It depends on the cause, the state of the works and whether the current contractor can be brought back. Restarting with the existing contractor can take weeks; a changeover needs a condition record, a new price, a new contract and a new permit in the replacement contractor's name, so in our experience it is usually measured in months rather than weeks.
6f194a245df295de: Should I keep paying the contractor while the site is stopped?
8e30353dd4cf68af: Pay only what has been properly valued and approved under the contract for work actually done. Do not make advance or goodwill payments to restart work until the position is understood, and take legal advice before withholding sums the contract says are due.

162ec8e49c20219f: Dubai Municipality publishes two guidance contract forms for private villas: one for engineering consultancy services and one for construction contracting. DM's stated aim is to strengthen contractual relationships between owners, consultants and contractors and reduce the disputes that delay projects.
83b96e8bb70b0cb7: The forms are currently available in Arabic only.
45912407c03d9ba4: They are for guidance and not mandatory.
eac775dae8f0b1cd: The parties may amend them by agreement.

f683e93de64baf28: Your consultant's appointment matters too. Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, engineering consultancy across Dubai, including free zones, is regulated, and only registered consultancies may practise as engineering consultants.
