396fe268e3435410: Lump sum or remeasure: which contract do I have?
12ccc77414c7bddd: This is the first thing to establish, because it decides who carries the risk of quantities. RICS practice information on contract selection lists the main ways of setting the contract sum as a fixed-price lump sum, remeasurement and target cost, alongside prime cost plus a fee, and treats the choice as one of the main decisions in choosing a contract.
e853f242fa5bf12d: Fixed price for a defined scope
df171607c41942fe: Agreed rates applied to measured quantities
ce7423001c09f5ff: Higher, if the scope is complete
5a87e78bb7c8c4d6: Lower until the work is measured
ffd3c02d12b0c744: Work that cannot be fully defined at the start
4bd094ef8df9e8b8: A lump sum is only as fixed as the scope behind it. If the drawings are incomplete, the "fixed" price will move through variations. Many villa contracts are a blend: a lump sum for most of the work, with remeasurable elements such as excavation or piling, plus provisional sums. Know which items sit where. If the contractor also designs the villa, the risks move again; see design and build or a separate architect.
5a63fb0faa6740b4: How should payments be valued and approved?
50e83327c9d47830: Payments should follow work done, not the calendar. A sound process looks like this:
78ea122999fc0b1d: The contractor submits a monthly application showing work completed and materials on site.
effe345b39891607: The owner's consultant checks it against progress on site and the contract rates.
8626599be659b29a: The approved amount is issued, less retention and any agreed deductions.
b9cece76d309806d: The owner pays within the period the contract sets.
16de57905bb0c875: Owners get into trouble when they pay against a contractor's application without it being checked, or when the payment schedule is front-loaded so that the contractor is paid ahead of the work. Once you have overpaid, your leverage on quality and completion is gone.
f20e27d6e8786ee1: Retention, advance payments and performance bonds
c3f99e67a26d7e09: These are the owner's main forms of financial security.
1008041a3457fae5: Retention is a percentage held back from each payment. Typically part is released at completion and the balance at the end of the defects liability period. It gives the contractor a reason to return and fix defects.
261e0df3ac12ae33: Advance payment guarantee. If you pay a mobilisation advance, it should be secured by a bank guarantee for the same amount, reducing as the advance is recovered from later payments.
c7caaf343c4197cf: Performance bond. A bank guarantee, often a percentage of the contract value, that the owner can call on if the contractor fails to perform. Check its wording, its expiry date and the conditions for calling it. A bond that expires before completion protects no one.
69cec325df720d16: Ask also for evidence of contractors' all-risks and third-party liability insurance for the duration of the works.
f171e72b5bf6c009: Decennial liability sits outside the contract's security. UAE law makes the contractor and the engineer jointly liable for ten years from handover for total or partial collapse and for defects that threaten the building's stability or safety, and any clause that tries to exclude or limit that liability is void. The rule is in Articles 880 to 883 of the 1985 Civil Code and, from 1 June 2026, Articles 821 to 824 of the new code (Kayrouz & Associates). It does not cover finishes or ordinary services faults, which is why retention and the defects period still matter.
2aa5396dec9e3276: How do variations work in a villa contract?
8d67b6ed9b33ca54: A variation is any change to the work described in the contract: an added room, a different finish, a moved wall, an omission. Variations are normal. Unmanaged variations are the single biggest cause of budget overruns we have seen.
747fd32c06f98f04: A good variation procedure has four steps:
efe374166640755d: Instruction in writing. Only the person named in the contract can instruct a change, and only in writing.
1245925677cf86c1: Quotation before work. The contractor prices the change, including any effect on time, before carrying it out.
de975e63d6c5f62a: Agreement. The owner accepts, rejects or negotiates the cost and time.
d1483afa7ae4a702: Record. The agreed variation is logged and carried into the next payment and the running final account.
c6a0d5a20ef9b36e: On the contractor's side, we learned early that verbal instructions were where margin was made or lost. A client who asked for "just a small change" on a site walk, without paper, would see it reappear later at a price and with a time claim attached. Insisting on written instructions protects both sides.
03c08184b2f727d7: Keep a variation register: number, description, date instructed, quoted cost, agreed cost, time effect, status. Review it monthly against the budget.
8bed08089ab2a6f9: The law sets a floor under all this. Commentary on the new Civil Transactions Law notes that Article 829(2) deals with payment where the scope of work changes or increases through the employer's fault, and that Article 829(3) lets a court restore the balance between the parties if exceptional general circumstances arise, including by extending the completion period or adjusting the price (K&L Gates). A written variation procedure keeps you out of that territory.
fe0c060abfbcce9f: Extension of time and liquidated damages, in plain English
bce4c2b0289f517c: These two clauses work as a pair.
e786597f814a58e6: Liquidated damages (LDs) are a sum the contractor pays for each day or week the villa is late beyond the completion date. They are agreed in advance so the owner does not have to prove the actual loss of a late handover. How they are treated is a matter of UAE law. Under Article 390 of the 1985 Civil Code, a court may, at either party's request, vary agreed compensation to equal the actual loss, and an agreement to the contrary is void (Fenwick Elliott). For contracts made from 1 June 2026, the new Civil Transactions Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 25 of 2025) replaces it with Article 340: the court may reduce the pre-agreed amount, and the owner can claim more only by proving fraud or gross negligence (K&L Gates). Which law applies depends on when your contract was made, so take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on your specific clause.
f5fb5658cd61adf2: Extension of time (EOT) moves the completion date when the delay is caused by something the contract says is not the contractor's risk: owner changes, late information from the owner's side, authority delays outside the contractor's control, or other listed events. If an EOT is granted, the contractor is not liable for LDs for that period.
fa6ae3415bf0d49f: A well-drafted contract also sets out:
51f9f6e040e8f9bc: Notice periods. The contractor must notify a delay event within a set time. Under the FIDIC 2017 Red Book, for example, a party that does not give notice of a claim within 28 days of becoming aware of the event loses its entitlement, and a fully detailed claim follows within 84 days (ICC). The new UAE Civil Transactions Law also requires the contractor to notify the employer immediately of events that may impede the work (Article 816(3)) (K&L Gates).
fd57343254eee43b: Substantiation. The notice should be followed by details of cause, effect and evidence.
c83233ea96b6d24e: Assessment. The person named in the contract assesses the claim within a set period.
b86d1073752bea32: Loss and expense. Whether the contractor can recover additional cost, such as extended preliminaries, as well as time.
aaa25b3a0776f7db: From two decades of preparing and answering EOT claims under JCT contracts and through adjudication, our view is that the outcome is decided by the programme and the records, not the rhetoric. A claim supported by an updated programme, dated correspondence and site records is hard to resist. A rejection with no evidence behind it is equally hard to defend.
86cb0096d12ded34: What does good contract administration look like?
2cb20869e256e8ed: This is where we draw most directly on two decades on the builder's side. The projects that ended well shared the same habits:
a4dddada3d6c8610: A baseline programme agreed at the start, updated monthly, with the critical path shown.
b36f52d195ad64a4: Weekly site records: labour and plant on site, work done, weather, instructions received, problems encountered, with photographs.
5331d8bcda310f73: Minuted progress meetings with actions and owners, issued within days.
89599ba6f153eff9: One instruction route. All changes in writing through the named person.
82206002de648044: A live variation register and cost report, reviewed against budget every month.
27569a3ef562d312: Notices dealt with on time, by both sides, every time.
f8ae754ea4e1629b: Correspondence filed so it can be found a year later.
80ef28fabf54084c: None of this is glamorous. All of it decides who wins an argument about time and money.
e8d9ae7bf7171f53: How are villa construction disputes resolved?
4fb5fab895e22930: In general terms, most contracts provide for a sequence: negotiation between the parties, sometimes escalation to senior representatives or mediation, then a binding route such as arbitration or the courts, depending on what the contract says. The UK statutory adjudication regime that many British owners know does not apply in the same way in the UAE. The right route, the time limits and the costs depend on your contract and on UAE law, so take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer early. The cheapest dispute is the one prevented by good records. If work has already stopped, our guide to what to do when a villa build stalls sets out the first ten days.

d697fe6a215b9b74: Is the price basis clear: lump sum, remeasure or a blend?

48a3fef6245edbba: Is there a written variation procedure with pricing before work?
1685171df62b9d6a: Are notice periods for delays and claims stated?
74f26c04dc88a639: Are LDs, retention, the advance payment guarantee and performance bond defined, with dates?
aecad3c7aaa1277a: Does the payment process tie to checked work on site?
be402f5fe28c2f66: Has a UAE-qualified lawyer reviewed it?

a0ff7472339c5a88: What is the difference between a lump sum and a remeasure contract?
1a3ef8bd35a35884: Under a lump sum contract the contractor agrees a fixed price for a defined scope, so the risk of quantities is largely the contractor's. Under a remeasure contract the work is measured as built and paid at agreed rates, so the final cost moves with the quantities.
f971bbe2a6770984: A pre-agreed amount, usually per day or week, that the contractor pays the owner if the villa is completed late without a valid extension of time. How enforceable they are, and whether they can be adjusted, is a matter of UAE law, so take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer.
1e9709beefac68aa: What should I do if my contractor submits a delay claim?
eb75bce71d616cef: Do not ignore it and do not simply reject it. Ask for the notice, the cause, the evidence and the effect on the programme, and have it assessed against the contract. Keep your own records, and take legal advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer if the sums are significant.
7c17b2df21da7ee8: Percentages vary by contract and are negotiated. What matters more is that retention is clearly defined: how much is held, when part is released at completion, and when the balance is released at the end of the defects period.

9e962b76ef8857ad: How much does it cost per square foot to build a villa in Dubai?
6430cc48769b4a14: Published sources broadly agree on the shape of the market, if not the exact edges. All of the figures below are construction only.
7f7968c7a93b4258: Turner & Townsend's UAE-wide figures for individual detached villas sit in the same bands: about AED 460–560 per sq ft for medium standard and AED 1,000–1,230 for prestige (AED 4,950–6,050 and 10,800–13,200 per m², Q1 2024). Our cost calculator uses AED 300–500 for standard, 500–850 for premium, 850–1,200 for luxury and 1,200–1,400 or more for ultra-luxury. Currie & Brown, reported by TradeArabia in February 2026, forecast UAE construction cost inflation of around 3% for 2026, which matters on a build that will be priced now and paid for over the next year or two.
0832f9a29608bbbc: Two cautions. First, these are averages across very different projects. A rectangular two-storey villa on a flat plot and a cantilevered, glass-heavy house with a basement are not the same building at the same rate. Second, the tier you are in is decided by the design, not by the brochure. Basements, large spans, structural glazing, stone cladding and imported joinery move a villa up a tier faster than any finishes schedule.
44367adcfc9c1e3e: What is included in the build cost, and what is not?
42bfed1ee975584c: The contractor's rate normally covers the building itself: substructure, frame, envelope, internal fit-out to the specified standard, and the mechanical, electrical and plumbing installations. It also includes the contractor's preliminaries, the cost of running the site. Turner & Townsend's 2025 UAE market intelligence puts contractor preliminaries in Dubai at 12% on a 2,500 m² project and 14% on a 50,000 m² one, so a meaningful slice of every square foot is site management, welfare, temporary works, insurance and plant rather than the building you will live in.
13bd7687bd2977c0: What is usually outside the rate:
7434b5ef73769d09: Design and engineering fees for the architect and engineers
88a3ddfc5e3c4c4d: Swimming pool and external works, unless specifically included
d49c9cfb163ff669: Furniture, fixtures and equipment (FF&E), and often specialist items such as home automation, lighting control, audio-visual and wine rooms
b688606290a1259c: The owner's own advisers, including any owner's representative
4e02c87c214f9645: Always read the contractor's list of exclusions before comparing totals. Two bids with the same headline can cover very different buildings.
72204ebe5da22f2f: Optimal Engineering puts full design and engineering at 6–12% of the construction contract value, with fixed-fee packages of AED 35k–150k for simpler projects. At the other end, Engel & Völkers quotes AED 50k–150k for design, engineering and permits, which reflects a much simpler scope, typically a standard villa on a standard plot. A bespoke luxury villa sits firmly at the percentage end.
bec9a5bacc616523: Your consultant must be registered with Dubai Municipality. Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, only registered consultancies may practise as engineering consultants, and the consultant's fee normally covers the statutory site role during construction as well as design. Check exactly which stages are in the fee before you sign.
5692b1077175f291: A property information website puts permits, NOCs and DEWA connection at AED 25k–75k for a straightforward villa. Optimal Engineering itemises more: a Dubai Municipality building permit at AED 15k–60k for a standard villa, a permanent DEWA connection at AED 10k–40k, and AED 80k–250k for authority approvals in total. The range is wide because it depends on the plot, the master developer's own charges, and the size of the electrical load. Your route runs through Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits, and usually through the master developer first.
1534200059cfbfb1: Engel & Völkers and Optimal Engineering both put it at 10–15%. We would add one qualification from experience: contingency is not a fixed percentage, it is a measure of how much of the building is still undecided when you sign. A fully resolved design with a complete finishes schedule can carry less. A design with half the specification still described as "to be confirmed" needs more.
859eb3ced526f5b1: Optimal Engineering prices a pool at AED 80k–120k for a basic fibreglass pool and AED 150k–250k for a standard concrete one, and AED 400k or more for a luxury pool. For landscaping and furniture we have found no industry source; a property information website gives landscaping at AED 100–500 per sq ft of garden and FF&E at 30–40% of build cost at the top end of the market. FF&E is the line owners most often forget, and on a luxury villa it can be one of the largest. If stone, joinery or fittings are coming from abroad, add shipping, duty and lead time to the budget early; see sourcing materials abroad for a Dubai villa.
e26db4c17c5f4413: What does a 10,000 sq ft luxury villa cost to build in Dubai?
fb16cafece9c3a2b: Here is a worked example using the published ranges above. It is illustrative, not a quotation. We assume 10,000 sq ft of built-up area, luxury specification at AED 850–1,200 per sq ft (Optimal Engineering, the same band as our calculator), and 4,000 sq ft of landscaped garden. For authority charges we use the top of the fixed range as a floor and 2% of build as a prudent ceiling; that is our own rule of thumb for a villa this size.
71f325c17cec66af: The arithmetic is simple; the point is the spread. Construction is roughly 68–82% of the total before FF&E, and less again once furniture is added. If you only budget the per-square-foot rate, you are budgeting perhaps two thirds of the project.
0631d434e3aa2b39: The range is also wide because the low column pairs the cheapest assumptions together and the high column the most expensive. A real project sits somewhere inside it, and the brief decides where. Inflation of around 3% for 2026 should be layered on top if contracts will be signed late in the year.
adb6e264cc8c38cb: Our founder spent 21 years running a premium building company whose houses won RIBA and LABC recognition. From that seat, budgets almost never failed on the rate. They failed on the gaps around it.
0865c294a9d29b34: Provisional sums. When a design is incomplete, the contractor carries an allowance for the unknown item: a kitchen, a staircase, a lighting system. The allowance is often set low so the overall bid looks competitive. When the real item is chosen, the difference becomes an addition. On the contractor's side, a bid with a lot of provisional sums was always a bid with a lot of room in it, for us.
cf7b8e0b455e013a: Late decisions. A change on paper costs a drawing revision. The same change after the slab is poured costs demolition, re-work, a programme delay and the contractor's time-related site costs for every extra week. Finishes, sanitaryware, glazing systems and automation chosen late are the most common culprits.
c9561ca180496839: Variations priced without competition. Once a contractor is appointed, every change is priced by one firm, with no competing bid to keep it honest. Variation rates are often higher than the rates in the original price.
80e33c25a9c4c2bc: Over-design. In August 2025, Dubai Municipality warned villa consultancies about over-designing structures and inflating build costs (Gulf News). An over-specified frame or foundation is cost you pay for without seeing it.
a69fc2f1a7a56236: Delay. Every extra month on site means another month of the contractor's preliminaries. With preliminaries at 12–14% of the contract (Turner & Townsend), a long overrun is expensive before a single extra brick is laid. Our guide to how long it takes to build a villa in Dubai explains where programmes usually slip. We cover this in more detail in what a builder knows that most villa owners don't.
19132997775ca42a: How do you protect a villa construction budget?
050442253380a1cf: Finish the design before you price it. The more of the building that is drawn and specified at bid stage, the fewer provisional sums and the more real competition you get.
638e7f83ad3cb784: Set the budget from the brief, not the rate. Use the full list above, including fees, external works and FF&E.
6bf7ef95d1bb1a94: Compare bids like-for-like. Normalise exclusions, provisional sums and preliminaries before you look at totals. Our guide to choosing a villa contractor in Dubai explains how.
71294d54264f263b: Hold the contingency yourself. It should sit in the owner's budget, released by decision, not buried in the contractor's price.
f3326c45d577055c: Price every change before it is instructed. Agree cost and time effect in writing first.
a7c76eef7aeabdaa: Track cost monthly against the programme. Payments should follow work actually done, not dates on a calendar.
b66df05c22995b07: Read the contract before signing it. Our guide to villa construction contracts in the UAE covers the clauses that matter, and you should take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer.
d055006b4af361a8: To run your own numbers, try our villa build and renovation cost calculator, which uses the same construction rates per square foot, applies its own stated assumptions to the other lines, and shows its sources. b2889127517f5b41: The published ranges are a useful starting point. What they cannot tell you is how much of your villa's real cost is still hidden behind its walls. That is where renovation budgets are won or lost, and it is what most of this guide is about.

d6cb438fee468ec5: AED 400,000–700,000; basic improvements to a three-bedroom villa about AED 600,000

429fd6acbc27f032: The gaps are less errors than different definitions. A low kitchen figure is replacing units; a high one is rebuilding the room, with new drainage, waterproofing, electrics and ventilation behind it. A whole-villa band describes an average house and an average scope, and none of the sources says which. Treat any single figure as the start of a conversation, not a budget.

b8ce16c45682304c: No published source we have found supports a location premium for renovation: Property Finder names communities only as examples of villa types, and Bayut ties its costs to the property type and the extent of the work. dad7f886b89a4d64: Two cautions. These are averages across very different houses, and a renovation's tier is decided less by the finishes you choose than by what the existing building needs. A villa with sound roofs and healthy services can be refreshed at the bottom of a band. The same villa with failed waterproofing and end-of-life air conditioning is a different project, whatever the finishes schedule says.
fecbd3960de1830e: What is not included in a renovation quote?
1fcd004c705bb13b: Most published figures, and most contractor quotes, cover the building work itself. Outside that, owners usually need to budget for:
12aae103a0c9697f: Design and engineering. Any renovation that touches structure, layout, services or the façade needs drawings from a DM-registered consultant. A master developer NOC where your community has one (see our guide to the Nakheel NOC for villa renovations), then a permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits. 704fddad0c7ce102: Contingency. Engel & Völkers and Optimal Engineering both put it at 10–15% on new builds. A renovation carries more unknowns, not fewer.
8999fe198e6a792a: External works. The renovation contractor's guide puts outdoor, pool and landscaping work at AED 50,000–200,000 combined; a pool rebuild alone can use much of that, since Optimal Engineering puts a standard concrete villa pool at AED 150,000–250,000.
09e234f95557ba57: Furniture, AV, lighting control and automation, which are often outside the main contract.
77b2abc02a2fb8e3: Living elsewhere. Rent, storage and removals if you move out for the works.
9eefdb96b51dde11: Inflation. Currie & Brown forecast UAE cost escalation of around 3% for 2026 (reported by TradeArabia); Turner & Townsend forecast 4% for Dubai.

aa4ba66dc0e431bb: What are the three hidden costs in older villas?
d9d26f81b0d3504f: Our founder, Philip Chapman, ran P Chapman Construction, a premium residential builder in the UK, for 21 years. From the builder's side, the renovation budgets that failed almost never failed on the rates. They failed on three things the original price did not capture.
c4bc9602b588e811: A new build is priced from drawings. A renovation is priced from what can be seen, and in an older villa the expensive parts usually cannot be.
c30704b90c750954: Waterproofing. Roof membranes, terraces over rooms, wet-room tanking and basements all have a finite life. Failure shows late, as staining, blistering paint or a musty room, long after the damage started. Replacing a membrane means stripping finishes and often lifting screeds, before any new interior goes in.
d6a1f344e5ec14cd: Services. Air conditioning, ductwork, pipework and electrical distribution installed when the villa was built may be near the end of its life, or undersized for how you want to live now. In Dubai the cooling system is the heart of the house, and replacing it is a building project, not a fitting.
f1b58238f1aac8f2: Concrete and salt. In coastal communities, wind-borne salt attacks metalwork, fixings, frames and, where concrete cover is poor, reinforcement. Cracking and rust staining need a structural engineer's view, not paint.
339dffd4fd137188: On the contractor's side, the first thing we priced on any refurbishment was the risk in the envelope and the services. Interiors are predictable; roofs, basements and plant are not. When the information was thin, we priced what we could see and knew the rest would come back as variations, priced by one firm with no competition. That is the single biggest reason renovation budgets move.
7bc1860035b33266: Renovations spread. Move a bathroom and you need new drainage falls, new waterproofing and new screeds. Open up a wall and the electrics behind it no longer suit the new layout. Replace the air-conditioning units and the ducts, controls, condensate routes and electrical supply may all need to follow. Lay new flooring on one level and the thresholds, doors and stairs no longer line up.
0fd406eb0944ba80: There is also the regulatory knock-on. The Dubai Building Code applies to building designs permitted after it came into force (Decree No. 45 of 2021), and the code itself describes its application to the renovation, modification and addition of existing buildings. In practice, new work in an older villa is designed to today's rules, not the rules the house was built under. Your consultant will tell you what that means for your scope; it is better to know at concept stage than at permit stage.
5dcbf5c91f2eb9bd: In our experience, a brief that starts as "kitchen, bathrooms and finishes" and ends as "most of the services and half the screeds" is the norm in older villas, not the exception. Price the knock-ons at design stage and they are decisions. Discover them on site and they are variations.
b3ff89fdaf8eb1ac: Every extra month on a renovation costs you three ways. The contractor's preliminaries, the cost of running the site, continue: Turner & Townsend's 2025 UAE market intelligence puts preliminaries in Dubai at 12% of construction cost on a 2,500 m² project. Your rent and storage continue if you have moved out. And the house is unusable for another month.
037760e19139dae6: Time is lost in predictable places: discoveries that need redesign, late decisions on finishes, design changes after the NOC that need resubmitting, and long-lead items such as glazing, joinery and imported stone ordered too late. Published guides put larger projects with structural work at six months or more on site, before approvals. Our villa renovation timeline breaks the months down phase by phase.
0ea08aa75598de41: Living in the villa during the works rarely saves money once services, waterproofing or structure are involved. The contractor has to phase the job around you, protect occupied rooms and work slower, and you pay for all of it in preliminaries.
81b0156981169965: How do you keep a villa renovation on budget?
135eed97880e6387: Survey before you design. Commission a proper condition survey of roofs, wet areas, basement, pool and MEP, and open up small areas where it matters. It is the cheapest money on the project. Our guide to rewiring and replumbing an older villa sets out what to test and open up.
e7cb9f2b7e7955e1: Price the design at concept stage. Get an early cost check before the drawings are finished, so the brief and budget can be adjusted while it is cheap to do so.
195abea8518964de: Turn provisional sums into scope. If the bid carries an allowance for "waterproofing repairs" or "MEP remedials", the real cost is still unknown. Investigate before signing, or at least agree rates.
836035799af4ac4b: Compare bids like-for-like. Normalise exclusions, allowances and preliminaries before looking at totals. Our guide to choosing a villa contractor in Dubai explains how.
ee024417230bd26a: Hold the contingency yourself. Release it by decision, not by default.
2fe722063cf5346b: Price every change before it is instructed. Cost and time, in writing, first.
8f02cb4afc1e3bfe: Decide early, order early. Finishes and long-lead items fixed before work starts protect the programme.
4ae0324a2e2dc86d: Read the contract. See villa construction contracts in the UAE, and take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer.

6240d0ce38c67bcf: The villa renovations that go wrong in Dubai rarely go wrong on site. They go wrong in the months before: a scope that is still moving when the contractor starts, an existing villa that nobody opened up before it was priced, finishes chosen after the strip-out, and approvals that run behind the programme. Each of these is avoidable, and each one is cheaper to fix on paper than in the building.
539c990175b0c96e: We spent 21 years on the contractor's side of premium residential work in the UK. The mistakes below are the ones we saw owners make again and again, described the way the builder sees them. None of them is about choosing a bad contractor. A good contractor working to a moving brief will still deliver a late, over-budget job, and will be entitled to be paid for it.
f145f8a2ee2e084c: Why do villa renovations run over budget?
28ee2819c4cabbf7: Renovation budgets leak through the gaps between what was priced and what is built. On a new build the drawings describe almost everything. On a renovation the existing villa hides things, and every surprise becomes a price agreed after the contract is signed, when the owner has the least bargaining power. Our step-by-step plan for a villa renovation in Dubai shows the order that avoids most of the mistakes below.

Property Finder and a Dubai renovation contractor's 2026 guide give different bands for the same kinds of work, which is one reason we never let an owner budget from a single headline rate. f5b796b36d38015f: Mistake 1: starting on site before the scope is frozen
e7e79f7b9e6d2caf: This is the most expensive habit we saw, and the most common. The owner is keen to start, the contractor is happy to mobilise, and the design is "nearly there". The kitchen layout will be settled next week. The bathroom tiles are being chosen. The pergola might become a covered terrace.
3ebf7a40c65cf1af: From the builder's side, every one of those open questions is an opportunity. Once the contract is signed and the site is running, a change is a variation, priced at the contractor's rates, with an adjustment to the programme that the contractor writes first. Nobody tenders against a variation. On a renovation with a moving brief, the variation account can grow steadily without anyone noticing the total until the final account.
5f7983cc71e34c5c: The fix is simple to state and hard to hold to: freeze the layout, the specification and the main finishes before the job is tendered, and treat any change after that as a decision with a price and a date attached. Our article on what a builder knows that most owners don't explains how contractors price this risk.
8204a53e423349f1: Mistake 2: not opening up the existing villa before it is priced
44223fd50bb53058: Older villas in established communities such as Jumeirah Islands, Arabian Ranches and the Palm Jumeirah were built to the standards and services of their day. What sits behind the plaster, under the screed and above the ceilings is often original: wiring, plumbing, drainage, waterproofing and air-conditioning ductwork.
175835ff5080a9d3: If nobody has looked, the contractor cannot price it. So the unknowns go into the quote as provisional sums or exclusions. On the contractor's side, a provisional sum was a placeholder we expected to grow, and it usually did once the walls were opened and the real condition of the services was clear.
ee6e0ffd86c421f6: A condition survey, with some opening-up of walls, ceilings and wet areas, costs a small fraction of the works and turns guesses into a scope. It is also the evidence you need if the honest answer turns out to be a rebuild rather than a renovation: see renovate or rebuild.
ccdb91a0f70f30ab: Owners often leave the enjoyable decisions until the end: stone, tiles, joinery, sanitaryware, lighting. The trouble is that many of these items have long lead times, and the programme cannot finish until they arrive.
aa8e92066504de35: In our experience the finish date of a renovation is usually set by the slowest item to arrive, not by the site work. Bespoke kitchens and wardrobes, imported stone, large-format glazing and replacement air-conditioning plant are typical examples. If they are chosen after the strip-out, the site waits, and a contractor who is waiting is usually entitled to more time and sometimes more money.
cfe350351847d75a: Choose the long-lead items during design, confirm them with signed samples, and order them against a programme date. If you are buying items yourself, read our guide to sourcing materials abroad first: owner-supplied items move risk onto you.
155384d0684718ff: Mistake 4: letting the programme run ahead of the approvals
fd89dc08072ff7fa: Most villa renovations in master-planned communities need the master developer's approval before the authority permit. In Nakheel communities the process starts with a Nakheel NOC application through its portal, and Nakheel's own customer FAQs cover NOCs, access permits and contractor requirements. Owners in at least one Nakheel community have been stopped from modifying villas without approval.
9c027b26946890c6: The building permit then comes from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits, through the single window and the Build in Dubai platform. Your DM-registered consultant makes the submissions, and the design must meet the current Dubai Building Code.
067469e797151878: The mistake is to book the contractor's start date first and hope the approvals catch up. A contractor mobilised with nothing they are allowed to do still costs money, in site set-up and in preliminaries, which Turner & Townsend puts at around 12% of cost on a small Dubai project in its 2025 market intelligence. Plan the start around the approvals, not the other way round.
9dea83599f116dc3: Mistake 5: comparing quotes on the bottom line
424cc22c5e1ca52f: Three quotes for the same renovation can differ widely, and the cheapest is rarely the cheapest outcome. The differences usually sit in what each contractor has left out: different allowances for kitchens and finishes, provisional sums set at different levels, preliminaries priced differently, and exclusions buried at the back.
27ae140114b6eae1: Before comparing totals, put every quote onto the same basis: the same scope, the same allowances, the same treatment of provisional sums and the same exclusions. Our guide on how to choose a villa contractor covers the checks, and a contractor quote review does it for you before you sign.
bf961ef07b6c963c: Mistake 6: paying ahead of the work
b9eeb8bae8f4747b: Large advances and payment schedules that run ahead of progress are common, and they hand the leverage to the contractor. If the job slows, or a dispute starts, the owner has already paid for work that has not been done.
e7972532e502613b: Pay against measured work and agreed milestones, and hold retention until the defects are closed out. Dubai Municipality publishes guidance contract forms for private villas that are a sensible starting point; take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on the contract you sign.
5dc544f81eff2b0b: Mistake 7: agreeing changes on site, by word of mouth
5c967baf20cf006c: Some changes are unavoidable: something is found behind a wall, or a decision looks different once the room exists. The mistake is agreeing them in a conversation on site and finding out the price at the final account.
e88d36ff57be6eb7: Every change should go through a written change request with a price and a time effect, approved in writing before the work is done, and recorded in a decision log. It is dull, and it is the single best protection an owner has against a final account that nobody recognises.
9f07332a409a1b55: Should you live in the villa while it is renovated?
234ca1cd4f048d66: For a light refresh, sometimes. For a full renovation with new services, waterproofing or structural work, it usually costs more than it saves. The contractor has to phase the work around the family, keep power, water and cooling running, and protect occupied rooms, all of which takes time and money. In summer, the midday break from 15 June to 15 September also shortens productive outdoor hours.
a1eaff88775fb9f6: How much contingency should you hold?
deab8bef3788b0d3: Engel & Völkers says a contingency of 10–15% of total project cost is widely recommended. On an older villa with original services, we would plan at the upper end. The important part is who controls it: the contingency is the owner's money, released only against approved changes, not an extra line in the contractor's price.

53e0165befa3f1ba: Where do the months go before anyone starts on site?
1e5fc3ec61019ea0: Survey and opening-up. Older villas hide their problems behind finishes: tired air-conditioning, original wiring, failing waterproofing in wet areas and on roofs, drainage that has settled. Two to four weeks spent finding out is the cheapest time on the whole programme. Skip it and the same questions are answered after the strip-out, at the contractor's rates and with the crew waiting. Our guide to villa renovation mistakes explains why this one matters most.
695658890168d7f2: Design to NOC level. The master developer needs to see what will change: layout, structure, façade, pool, external plant. The design should be priced at the same time, so you do not seek approval for something you cannot afford.
0109240f5c3114f5: The master-developer NOC. In Nakheel communities, Nakheel says an NOC from its Urban Planning team is needed before any alteration, requested through its online services (Nakheel). It has said that villa modification applications are assessed case by case (Gulf News), and it does not publish a single turnaround. Nakheel approvals carry an expiry date, so check yours and keep the contractor's start within it. Emaar communities follow a similar pattern: in Arabian Ranches, any alteration needs Emaar's approval through a home modification NOC (Emaar Community Management). Our Nakheel NOC guide covers the process in detail.
b3dcd085968dd3b5: The authority permit. Where the scope needs one, your DM-registered consultant applies to Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits, with service-authority NOCs gathered through Dubai's unified window (Dubai Municipality; Build in Dubai). 96ce9122505ec56f: A clause excluding or limiting that liability
801d9675f5e8d02c: Structural parts of a unit bought from a developer (jointly owned property, Dubai)

Commentary on the new law says it largely keeps the ten-year regime, now in Articles 821 to 824 (Charles Russell Speechlys).

5186726f9f6302f1: Retention is money held back from payments and released in stages, often part at handover and the rest at the end of the defects period. 20a37e0a13ddd57a: How snag lists get closed out, and how they stall
e2cef83c5a60f80c: We spent two decades on the contractor's side of handovers. Here is what we know about how they go.
fe87a0079a3caa26: A clean, numbered list. A contractor's site manager can allocate a numbered list to trades in an hour. A vague list becomes an argument.
6da456bfbdd16e23: One list, one owner. When the owner, the family, the interior designer and the consultant all send separate lists, items get duplicated, contradicted and lost.
bc4ac1278945ac17: Money still on the table. On the contractor's side, the jobs we closed out fastest were the ones where a meaningful sum was still to be paid on completion.
9417eec2be92a028: Joint walkrounds. Walking the list together, item by item, and signing off what is closed stops the same items being reopened.
face78755c488ad1: Early release of money. Once the final payment and retention have gone, the snag list competes with every other job for the contractor's attention. It usually loses.
1ff2def5aa55e839: Trades demobilised. Subcontractors leave site once their package is paid. Getting a tiler back for three tiles is hard for the main contractor too.
226b6a7c659e08b1: Snags mixed with changes. If the list includes things you have changed your mind about, the contractor will treat the whole list as a variation request. Separate defects from new requests.
f19fc567df69af53: Moving in too early. Once furniture and family are in, it becomes difficult to prove who caused a scratch or a chip. Inspect and record before occupation.
27740973c294f1bf: No deadline. Agree a date for closing items, in writing, as part of handover.

75d125cae4d73f67: A builder knows that the price you sign is a starting point, that the margin on a job is often planned in the gaps rather than the headline, and that most owners never read the documents where those gaps sit. Provisional sums, preliminaries, variation rates, programme float and the monthly valuation are where a villa's real cost is decided. We spent 21 years on the contractor's side of premium residential building in the UK, and this is what we would want any owner to know before signing.
ea20ace8a35b4d6f: Nothing here is a criticism of contractors. Building is a hard, risky business with thin margins, and a good contractor is worth paying properly. But the commercial logic of the contractor's side is not the owner's logic, and the owner who understands it gets a better building for less trouble.
1accb36cbead3cb9: How does a contractor actually price a villa bid?
b604cbc7b4b3f359: Owners imagine a contractor adds up materials and labour, puts a margin on top, and sends the number. That is the estimate. The bid is something else.
b09a76d7373cd7f0: On the contractor's side, the first thing any builder prices is not the building. It is the risk in the documents. How complete was the design? Which items were vague? What was missing from the drawings that would obviously have to be built? Where would the client inevitably change their mind? Those answers decide how a contractor bids.
371decc595d9eb32: When the design is complete and the competition strong, contractors price tight, because there is little to recover later. When the design is loose, the market can afford to bid lower, because everyone knows the job will grow. That is the uncomfortable truth: an incomplete design does not just add risk, it invites a lower bid, which looks like good news to the owner and is often the opposite.
a02e137d787cf174: Contractors also price the client. A first-time owner who lives overseas, with no independent adviser, is a different commercial proposition from an experienced developer with a quantity surveyor checking every valuation. Nobody writes that on the bid, but it is in the number.
e834f43a7300ce53: Then there is the subcontract market. Much of a villa is built by specialist subcontractors: MEP, glazing, joinery, stone, pools. The main contractor's bid depends on quotes from them, and those quotes can be sharpened after the main contract is signed. Savings found after signature are the contractor's to keep unless the contract says otherwise.
cfc12f4d15906d27: What are provisional sums, and why do they matter so much?
c1cfc04cd3034bf3: A provisional sum is an allowance for something not yet designed or chosen. "Kitchen: AED X." "Lighting control: AED Y." When the actual item is selected, the contract sum moves to the real cost.
9d0299fb06eb7b5a: From the builder's side, provisional sums do three useful things for the contractor:
56f6c0b4b0204f50: They make the bid look lower. If the owner's documents leave the allowance to the contractor, a low allowance makes the total more competitive, and the real cost arrives later.
a620eedcd76ec7de: They move risk to the owner. Whatever the item eventually costs, the owner pays it.
aad16285582c7e15: They often carry their own mark-up and attendance. Read how the contract adjusts provisional sums: is the contractor's overhead and profit added to the difference, and is there extra time?
6a5c6cbf0cbd6c98: In Dubai, this is particularly relevant on luxury villas, where kitchens, wardrobes, lighting, automation, AV and loose specialist items are often left as allowances because the owner has not chosen yet. In our experience, a bid where these make up a large share of the total is not really a fixed price at all.
1d572ec7f78f23d7: What to do: resolve as many items as you can before pricing. Where you cannot, set the provisional sums yourself, at realistic levels, so every bidder carries the same figure. Then compare bids on what is left. RICS guidance on tendering makes the same point about information: an answer given to one bidder's query should go to every bidder, so that no one prices on a different basis.
e1193dc8e56e25a4: Why are preliminaries the line to watch?
0414ad3a08b9c2c7: Preliminaries are the cost of running the site: the site manager, welfare, security, temporary power and water, scaffolding, hoarding, plant, insurances, waste and so on. Turner & Townsend's 2025 UAE market intelligence puts preliminaries in Dubai at 12% of construction cost on a 2,500 m² project and 14% on a 50,000 m² project.
6b1fcaff67d0e8b1: The important point is that many preliminaries are time-related. They are priced per week or per month. That means:
4c022a6f1173b0a0: A contractor who prices a short programme can show a low preliminaries figure. If the programme then slips, the time-related costs reappear in an extension-of-time claim.
955d5a8249272ef9: Every week of delay that the contract attributes to the owner, through late decisions, late information or changes, carries a weekly cost.
3138e47bf0bbce3a: When we compared our own bids against competitors, an unusually low preliminaries figure usually meant one of two things: an unrealistic programme, or preliminary costs hidden elsewhere in the rates. Ask every bidder for a weekly breakdown of time-related preliminaries. It tells you what delay will cost before it happens.
adf3cd245d5b4c94: A variation is a change to the work. Some are genuine owner changes. Many are not; they arise because the drawings were unclear, two consultants' drawings disagreed, or something necessary was simply missing.
37c6e900787db739: On the contractor's side, the commercial team reads the contract documents looking for exactly these gaps, from the day the job is won. Every ambiguity is a potential variation. Every late answer to a request for information is a potential delay. This is ordinary practice, and a contractor who did not do it would not stay in business for long.
80e5cd6ecb57f28e: How a variation claim is typically assembled:
a8e2287beba62c10: The direct cost of the extra or changed work, priced at contract rates where they apply and at new rates where they do not. New rates are where the margin tends to be.
ff343252218ebe5a: Knock-on costs: work removed or redone, materials wasted, re-sequencing.
84301f53e336863e: Time: if the change affects the critical path, an extension of time, and with it time-related preliminaries.
27f577c61568ba7d: Disruption: loss of productivity from working out of sequence.
c3f8a32d899d9dcd: The defence is the same in every case: price the variation and agree its time effect before it is instructed, in writing. A variation agreed after the work is done is priced by one party, the one that did it.
7233fcc0cc646d63: Notice matters as much as price. Commentary on the UAE's new Civil Transactions Law, in force for contracts made from 1 June 2026, notes that it deals with payment for changes or increases in scope caused by the employer (Article 829(2)) and requires the contractor to notify the employer immediately of events that may impede the work (Article 816(3)) (K&L Gates). International standard forms are stricter still: under the FIDIC 2017 Red Book, a party that does not give notice of a claim within 28 days of becoming aware of the event loses its entitlement (ICC). A contractor's commercial team diarises those dates from day one. The owner's side should too. We cover the contractual side in villa construction contracts in the UAE; take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on your specific contract.
5ec4074138842ccf: Float is the slack in a programme: the amount an activity can slip without delaying completion. Owners rarely think about it. Contractors think about it a great deal.
8c41b51aae280f74: If the contract is silent, the practical answer is usually that float is used by whoever needs it first. A contractor who has planned well keeps float in its own activities and presents a programme where the owner's decisions sit on the critical path, with no slack. Then any late owner decision, a tile not chosen, a sample not approved, causes immediate, claimable delay.
116c1d3fea041ec3: When reviewing a contractor's programme, look for:
9521fa44ffb67880: Owner decisions shown with no float, while the contractor's own activities have plenty.
086c7eadd94f5eb9: Durations for long-lead items that assume orders the owner has not yet been asked to approve.
ed424bfff8fa72d4: A programme without a clear list of information required from the owner, and when.
ac2d7990d4acb771: A decision schedule, agreed at the start, listing every owner choice and the latest date it can be made without delay, is one of the cheapest protections an owner can have.
470ff7ca4ae9436e: Why is the cheapest bid rarely the cheapest outcome?
790e78d56befab5c: Put the pieces together. The lowest bid often has some combination of low provisional sums, tight exclusions, a short programme with low preliminaries, and keen rates on the measured work but generous scope to recover through new rates. It may also have been priced by a contractor who needs the turnover.
1ca6f7a5f853d893: RICS practice information on contract selection treats the basis of the contract sum, whether a fixed-price lump sum, remeasurement or a target cost, as one of the main choices an employer makes. A lump sum is only as fixed as the scope behind it.
5cbcf23dd2ec455a: None of that is visible in the total. It is visible in the breakdown, which is why bids should be compared line by line, with provisional sums normalised, exclusions priced back in, and preliminaries tested against a realistic programme. Our guide to choosing a villa contractor in Dubai shows how.
fb5ca5cc57a67aa7: There is one more factor: design. In August 2025, Dubai Municipality warned villa consultancies about over-designing structures and inflating build costs (Gulf News). A competitive bid on an over-designed villa is still a bid for more building than you need.
2455858710e80216: How should you read a monthly valuation?
e4c0226a49ba3603: Each month the contractor submits a valuation: the value of work done to date, less previous payments and retention. On the contractor's side, the valuation was also a cash-flow tool, and it was normal to value optimistically. Front-loading, valuing early activities generously so cash arrives ahead of cost, is common practice across the industry.
6a3e83b6ec6d1869: Read a valuation line by line:
f23e508a7497ab97: Is the work actually installed? Not delivered, not "in progress", installed. Materials on site are a separate question, and paying for materials off site needs proof of ownership and insurance.
429e2d911acdc262: Do percentages match what you see? If the electrical installation is valued at 60%, is 60% of it actually done?
c99e6fb345c89b3a: Are variations valued only once agreed? Unagreed variations should be shown separately, not slipped into the total.
35a7af671ea60f1a: Does the cumulative value track the programme? A valuation running ahead of physical progress is a warning sign, especially if the contractor's position is weakening. If the site then slows or stops, see what to do when your villa build stalls.
5c906f6204dc5fa7: Our cost and programme control service reviews valuations for owners independently.
7266580bec24c4fd: Practical completion and handover is the moment the balance of power shifts. Before it, the contractor wants the final payments, the release of part of the retention, and to stop paying for the site. After it, they have moved their team to the next job.
f2c53d773fbdd645: From the builder's side, we always knew which defects would be fixed promptly: the ones listed before handover, while money was still held. Defects raised months later, with retention already released, joined a queue.
5bd71b959d77e401: Snag thoroughly before accepting handover, with an independent inspection, not just a walk-round. Our villa snagging checklist is a starting point.
806701ec4b086382: Do not release payments or retention until agreed defects are rectified, within what your contract allows.
96ebd9e14f844c59: Insist on as-built drawings, operating manuals, warranties and test certificates before handover, not after.
d93ff7acdaf7f3ce: Know your defects liability period and diarise inspections well before it ends.
30616e14adbeaecb: Structural safety sits outside this bargaining. UAE law makes the contractor and the engineer jointly liable for ten years from handover for collapse or defects that threaten the building's stability or safety, and that liability cannot be excluded by contract (Kayrouz & Associates). Everything else, from a leaking shower to an undersized air-conditioning unit, depends on your contract and on the leverage you kept.
2004d1baf7ad48d8: We spent two decades as the builder. Now we sit on the client's side of the table, working alongside your registered consultant and your contractor. We help you compare bids like-for-like, test programmes, review valuations and variations, and protect your position at handover. See our variations, delays and claims service, or contact us to talk through your project.
bfb6fa5925bad20f: Why is the cheapest villa construction bid rarely the cheapest outcome?
20ad3bb1d662343d: Because the lowest bid often carries low provisional sums, tight exclusions or optimistic preliminaries. The difference is recovered later through additions and variations priced without competition.
8c5428a6d6846c8a: What is a provisional sum in a villa building contract?
1dbb6a49823c8627: An allowance in the contract for work that has not been fully designed or chosen yet, such as a kitchen or lighting system. When the real item is selected, the contract sum is adjusted up or down to the actual cost.
217ccf05bd2e2410: What are preliminaries on a construction bid?
5bfe7059a33b2053: The contractor's cost of running the site: management, welfare, temporary works, plant, insurance and similar. Turner & Townsend put them at 12% of construction cost in Dubai on a 2,500 m² project and 14% on a 50,000 m² project. Many are time-related, so they grow with delay.
4613eb1026e11961: When do I have the most leverage over my contractor?
16cbeecd5f074a53: Before handover, while payments and retention are still held. Once you have taken possession and released money, the contractor's incentive to return for defects drops.

c6357392ff939e09: In almost every villa community the master developer's approval comes before the authority permit, and that step often sets the programme more than the permit does.

0c5cd4d7c31cceb0: Three authorities issue villa building permits in Dubai: Dubai Municipality, Trakhees and the Dubai Development Authority (DDA). Which one covers your villa is decided by the plot, not by the community name, so the only safe answer is the one your registered consultant confirms from your plot documents. In Abu Dhabi the route is easier to name: the municipality issues the permit through TAMM, under rules set by the Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT).
bb82b196ae28986f: That sounds like a technicality. It is not. The authority decides which regulations the design is drawn to, which portal the application goes through, who inspects the work and who issues the completion certificate. Get it wrong at the start and the design is reworked later, which is where months go.
dc31d85a99bada8e: Why can't I tell the authority from the community name?
cf4b879077837d8e: Because Dubai law draws the boundaries plot by plot, and they move.
c53b08a3dbfba34a: The DDA. Law No. 8 of 2023 defines the DDA's free zone as the Creative Clusters plus specific land plots whose boundaries are marked on plans attached to the law, and any other zone or plot the Ruler later places under the DDA (Dubai Legislation Portal). The plans list individual plots by number and district. The DDA describes its own role as permitting construction activities, carrying out inspections and issuing completion certificates for projects within its jurisdiction (DDA).
774c0ad88943ce2c: Trakhees. Decree No. 22 of 2009 created special development zones covering land owned by the Ports, Customs and Free Zone Corporation (PCFC) and Dubai World and their affiliated companies, naming Nakheel among them, and gave PCFC exclusive responsibility for licensing there (Dubai Legislation Portal). Trakhees is the PCFC body that regulates those zones. In March 2024 Nakheel and Meydan were folded into Dubai Holding (Dubai Media Office), a reminder that ownership, and the arrangements that follow it, change.
00244f7d9c2257a3: Dubai Municipality. Under the 2023 urban planning law, the authority responsible for a special development zone or free zone issues planning permits for the land it oversees, while Dubai Municipality holds the wider planning powers across the emirate (Dubai Legislation Portal).
728eed97f228c9bf: So a single community can, in principle, contain plots that sit differently, and a community's position can change by legislation. That is why our rule is simple: confirm with your consultant; never assume by community.
625b1f3f5a493eda: Does it matter which authority it is if everything goes through one window?
4280d5de9c4b43dc: Less than it used to, but yes. Since 2022, building permits for Dubai Municipality, the DDA, Trakhees and the Dubai Integrated Economic Zones Authority have run through a single unified e-window, with Civil Defence, RTA, DEWA and the telecoms providers linked in (Dubai Municipality). The Build in Dubai platform now covers a project from land and design to completion and later alterations.
fccc82e5c6a8db7f: One front door does not mean one rulebook. Each authority still applies its own regulations, fees, inspection regime and completion process. For an owner, the practical questions are:
ff69384b1c120ddf: Which regulations is the design being drawn to?
ebcdaa40ac3724b9: Is the consultant experienced with this authority, and is the contractor registered to work under it?
df248986839b123c: Which inspections will the authority carry out, and when do they fall in the programme?
1f9ec42d13486f4d: Who issues the completion certificate, and what does it need to see?
22d2d9a1532c0dd3: Our guide to the Dubai villa building permit walks through the permit stages themselves.
66d6c5abea4d5daa: Location, authority and what it changes for your programme
840facaf06218681: The table covers the communities we write about most. It is a planning aid, not a ruling. The master developer column reflects the developer whose approval normally comes first; the authority column says "confirm with your consultant" wherever a primary source does not settle it, which in Dubai is every row. We cover every community in Dubai and Abu Dhabi; these are examples, not limits.

c9cd99c270e012ab: Why the Dubai rows all say "confirm"
9d628c6e6d15322d: We could have filled the column with what agents, forums and listings say. Some of it is probably right. But we could not verify a current, community-by-community list from a primary source, and the legislation above shows why one would date quickly. An owner who designs to the wrong authority's regulations pays for it in redesign. A five-minute question to the consultant at the start costs nothing.
1c863340e870d199: Why the master developer usually matters more than the authority
c91ac83fa1d99ea8: In practice, the approval that most often sets a villa programme is not the permit. It is the master developer's review.
8216bbd937210526: In Nakheel communities, Nakheel's guidance is that you need an NOC from its Urban Planning team before making alterations, and that site access involves its own requirements, including a security deposit, a site access permit and a site fence (Nakheel). Owners who skip that step find out later: Gulf News reported Jumeirah Islands owners being stopped from modifying villas without Nakheel's approval (Gulf News). Our Nakheel NOC guide sets out the sequence.
b1737940cb2e4e61: Abu Dhabi master communities work the same way. The development control regulations for Al Raha Gardens, an Aldar community, published in the Abu Dhabi Municipality's e-library, require an Abu Dhabi Municipality building permit, Abu Dhabi Distribution Company approval and Civil Defence approval for structural work, extensions and new structures, and require some finishes to be colour-matched to the existing for Aldar's approval (Abu Dhabi Municipality). Each community has its own regulations; get the ones for your plot.
901a4b3abe2baea2: Abu Dhabi is easier to name and has moved faster on simplification. Building permits are requested through TAMM (TAMM), under regulations set by DMT. In September 2025 DMT amended the private villa regulations, including a 1.5-metre front setback and allowing a lightweight rooftop majlis (DMT). In August 2025 it introduced a streamlined route for minor works such as small extensions, pools, canopies and fences, which licensed contractors can apply for directly (DMT).
f9792c611c5d585e: On plot communities the master developer still comes first. Modon's Wadeem on Hudayriyat has more than 1,700 plots for owners to design their own villas (Modon), and each owner works to Modon's plot requirements before the municipality permit. Our Abu Dhabi permit guide covers the TAMM route in detail.
b8b2421b77373994: What does the authority change for your programme?
e45434c21bac1128: The authority affects the programme in four practical ways.
e7813d060356e02d: The design brief. Setbacks, heights, basements and roof structures are drawn to the authority's regulations and the developer's guidelines together. Confirm both before the consultant starts concept design.
a6aca29b29ec1125: The team. Ask whether the consultant regularly submits to this authority and whether the contractor is registered to work under it. A contractor who has to register partway through is a contractor who is not on site.
7b9847a00f355d1a: The inspection calendar. Staged inspections fall at different points and are booked differently. Build them into the programme as hold points, not as surprises.
a15a04f49085b7cb: The finish line. The completion certificate and service connections come from the authority's process. Handover dates in the contract should follow it, not a hopeful date.
bc59050761e0879a: From the builder's side, this is familiar. On every UK job we ran, the first practical question was who the building control body was, the local authority or a private approved inspector, because it decided who we booked inspections with, what they wanted to see before work was covered up, and how long sign-off took at the end. The jobs that ran late were rarely the complicated ones; they were the ones where nobody asked that question until the first inspection was due.
3964b5e6b737b727: A short checklist before design starts
32e2421a58c1199f: Get the plot documents in hand: title deed, affection plan and any plot sale agreement or design guidelines from the developer.
cda3415feeb64cfb: Ask your consultant, in writing, which authority covers the plot and on what basis.
3efb71908838c795: Get the master developer's current guidelines and NOC process for your community.
d0a664f9b79c051d: Confirm the consultant's experience with that authority and the contractor's registration under it.
b85eed9c85472615: Put developer review, the permit and staged inspections into the programme as separate lines, with an allowance for at least one round of comments.
09ab7e29a66a3bf9: If you are buying, do this before you commit. Our plot checks guide covers the rest.
54e8962819f23339: We are a client-side project manager, not a consultant or contractor: your registered consultant prepares and submits the applications and confirms which authority covers your plot. Our role is to make sure that question is asked and answered at the start, that the developer review, permit and inspections are realistic in the programme, and that the contracts follow the approvals rather than run ahead of them. A plot review or our design and approvals support is the usual starting point. Tell us about your plot or villa.
f8f3e203bb692f2a: How do I find out which authority covers my villa plot in Dubai?
39e399b16c029155: Ask your registered engineering consultant to confirm it from the plot documents (title deed, affection plan or plot sale agreement) before design starts. Your master developer can also tell you which authority its community submits to. Do not rely on a community name, a listing or a neighbour's experience.
32733c06ad0fa2e5: Is Palm Jumeirah under Trakhees or Dubai Municipality?
18657db9259f47b7: Owners and consultants commonly describe Palm Jumeirah as a Trakhees area, and Decree No. 22 of 2009 placed Nakheel land within the special development zones regulated by the Ports, Customs and Free Zone Corporation. Nakheel has since become part of Dubai Holding, and jurisdiction is decided plot by plot, so have your consultant confirm it for your villa. Whichever authority applies, a Nakheel NOC comes first.
9d37080763837572: Does the permit authority change the cost of my villa?
a4014577306ec7f2: Each authority sets its own fees, inspections and submission requirements, so the figures differ. The bigger cost is usually time: a design prepared against the wrong regulations has to be reworked. Confirm the authority before the consultant starts detailed design.
b16abe42f066711c: Who applies for the building permit?
3fc17f06eb71986a: Your registered engineering consultant prepares and submits the application, or for some smaller works in Abu Dhabi a licensed contractor can apply directly. The owner appoints the team, provides the plot documents and agrees the brief and design.
ebcd382a3f698a97: Do I still need master developer approval if I have a building permit?
d0d5598de8fba7c8: Yes, in almost every master-planned community the developer's NOC or design approval is needed before the authority will consider the application. The two are separate approvals with separate conditions.

795f341a4a9b27a9: What should I check before accepting a new villa?
595aced332c089f0: Waterproofing, drainage and roof areas, air conditioning performance, plumbing and hot water, electrical and lighting controls, glazing and doors, finishes, pool and external works. Our snagging guide goes room by room, and the printable checklist adds a severity column and a snag log.
fefb36bb1cb88974: Can I appoint you just for snagging?
bfad36f8dacb2e20: No. Snagging and handover are one stage of our full service on a villa we represent, so there is no snagging-only fee. If all you need is a single inspection of a finished villa, a snagging inspection firm offers that, and our free snagging checklist will help you do a first pass yourself.
8c8fca304fa53fe6: What documents should I receive at handover?
6ef8cf7eb9fbe01e: At least the completion certificate, as-built drawings, warranties and guarantees, operation and maintenance manuals, test certificates and keys and codes schedules.
bb69056eeb83c55c: Can I inspect before final payment?
3fdfe7a13d95de28: Usually, yes, and you should. Building contracts commonly tie the payment due at completion, and the first release of retention, to an inspection and an agreed snag list, but the order is set by your contract, so read it before the handover appointment. For a villa bought from a developer, the sale and purchase agreement sets the order of payment, inspection and handover. A UAE-qualified lawyer can confirm your rights. On our appointments, the pre-handover inspection is planned into the programme so that it happens before the payment, not after it.
f8b99eadd4c04b0f: What if the villa fails inspection?
6e0bc76145b8417c: A handover inspection rarely ends in a simple pass or fail. It produces a list. Minor items are normally recorded on a snag list for the contractor to close within an agreed period. Serious defects, such as water coming in, unsafe electrics or systems that do not work, are a reason to delay accepting the villa until they are put right and inspected again. The authority's completion inspection is separate; your registered consultant will confirm where it stands. What you can do next depends on your contract: we set out the options and recommend one, and a UAE-qualified lawyer advises on your rights.
5f02691840cc1965: Should I sign handover documents before snags are closed?
a588fa34bd3f3e40: Read exactly what you are being asked to sign first. A handover or completion certificate can start the defects liability period, trigger the release of part of the retention and affect delay damages, so signing one is a significant step. Accepting handover with a list of minor snags attached is common, provided the list forms part of the document and the contractor's obligation to close each item, and by when, is clear. Do not sign anything stating the villa was accepted free of defects while items are still open. If in doubt, take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer before you sign.
dd931334fc5c4fe6: Do I need to be present?
744c65073f54a970: Not at every inspection. On our appointments we carry out the pre-handover inspections and report each item with photographs, so you can follow it from abroad. If you can, attend the final walk-through and the demonstration of the systems: it is your home, and that is when you are shown how to run it. If you cannot travel, we can take you through it on a video call. Whatever is signed at handover is your decision.

5c7d43bcfe38ab36: From the builder's side, the cost of delay was always easier to see from the contractor's chair than from the owner's: site cabins, supervision and plant hire run by the week whether work moves or not. The owner's costs are quieter but often larger, because rent and finance never stop. When a build has stalled, our guide to what to do when a villa build stalls covers the first ten days, and a stalled project review puts a number on the way back.
1b99590ca8da1fdb: How much does a month's delay cost on a villa build in Dubai?
8e6e7a9fc185d198: It depends on your circumstances, but the main costs are rent or a hotel while you wait, interest on money borrowed, the rise in price of the work still to build, and, if the delay is on your side, the contractor's time-related site costs. On the default example, renting a four-bedroom villa at the Dubai average and with half the build still to go, one month's delay is likely to cost about AED 44,300.
c285793f74b37ab6: Who pays for delay on a construction project?
d9cbae5a651fcfe6: That depends on the cause and the contract. A contractor-caused delay may entitle the owner to delay damages; an owner-caused delay may entitle the contractor to more time and costs. The records made at the time decide most disputes. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on your contract.
b9f8be5d276c4aa8: How much does construction inflation add each month?
87c5a133179584c5: For 2026 Turner & Townsend forecast construction inflation of 4% in Dubai and 5% in Abu Dhabi, and Currie & Brown about 3% for the UAE. A year's inflation divided by twelve, applied to the work still to build, gives a rough monthly figure. On a firm fixed price the contractor carries much of that risk, until the scope or the programme changes.
e22b61bf766da3a8: What should I do if my villa project is delayed?
930b65cb8ff6ff4a: Establish the cause in writing, keep dated records of the site and the correspondence, check what the contract says about notices and extensions of time, and pay only what has been properly valued. If the site has stopped, read our guide to the first ten days of a stalled villa build.
3a11317b41d61cdd: Does this include delay damages from the contractor?
c6f66537b3a0a5ca: No. Whether delay damages are payable, and how much, depends on the contract, the cause of the delay and UAE law, so the estimator shows your costs only.

7b80547eaeb291bc: How long does a rebuild take compared with a renovation?
e82a66df40ea9aa7: Renovation works typically take two to six months, longer for structural changes. A rebuild goes through design, approvals, construction and snagging, about 14–23 months end to end on published phase estimates and 24–36 months for a custom luxury villa. You can usually stay in the old villa while the new one is designed and approved, so the months out of the house are fewer than the total.
d2af0b5c16024006: Do I need a permit to demolish and rebuild my villa?
6d3401d0c778e9d2: Yes. Demolition needs approval, and the new villa needs a full building permit through Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits, usually after your master developer's NOC. Your DM-registered consultant handles the submissions. A purely cosmetic renovation often needs no permit, though the master developer may still require an NOC.
3aed7c98d3f3f063: Can I build a bigger villa if I knock down the old one?
d770449d5411b225: Sometimes. The plot's permitted built-up area, setbacks and height, and the master developer's own rules, set the limit. Check them with your consultant and the master developer before you assume extra floor area, because it is often the deciding factor in favour of rebuilding.
7b407a09918a4ae1: It is indicative, built from published market ranges, and it cannot see the condition of your villa. Use it to frame the decision, then test it with a condition survey, opening-up and a proper cost plan for each option before committing.

75a18ac37119d7a1: Advance. Al Tamimi & Company describes an advance payment of between 10% and 20%, depending on the nature of the project, as industry practice.[1] Under FIDIC contracts it is given in return for an advance payment guarantee. The planner recovers it from each monthly valuation in proportion to the work done, a simple and common approach; your contract may set a different recovery schedule.
deb6cb59b31723c7: Monthly valuations. The contract sum spread over the build period on the pattern you choose. Each month's value is rounded to the nearest AED 1,000 and the last month takes the difference, so the months add up to the contract sum exactly.
d4571568c737af61: Retention. DLA Piper describes common UAE practice as 10% retention, with 5% released at handover and 5% after the defects liability period.[2] Under the FIDIC Red Book, the taking-over certificate releases the first half.[1] Retention is not required by UAE law; the percentage, any cap and the release dates are whatever your contract says.
efad96033e4a6c86: Build period. The example uses 12 months. Published estimates put villa construction at typically 12–18 months[3] or 8–14 months for the construction phase alone.[4]
a4508c92f3f0fcd3: The column "Advance not yet recovered" is your exposure: money paid ahead of the work. It falls as the advance is recovered, which is why the advance payment guarantee should reduce on the same schedule and stay valid until the last of it is recovered. Retention is the opposite: the contractor's money in your hands, which is why it gives you leverage at handover.
50c9a3dbe96a99d9: From the builder's side, the first month's valuation was always the one we watched most closely, because front-loading the early payments is the easiest way for a contractor to finance a job with the owner's money. A schedule like this one, agreed before signing, gives you something to check each payment application against. Our guide to villa construction contracts in the UAE covers retention, advance payment guarantees and bonds in more detail.
c5eb73293d930118: How much advance payment is normal on a UAE villa build?
d8c4465710af681f: An advance of 10–20% of the contract sum is described as industry practice, depending on the project (Al Tamimi & Company). It should be secured by an advance payment guarantee that reduces as the advance is recovered from later payments. The figure is negotiable and set by your contract.
e73fb9e0b3a410b5: How much retention is held on a construction contract in the UAE?
9c7b16869b49112d: Commonly 10% of each payment, with 5% released at handover and 5% after the defects liability period (DLA Piper). Retention is not mandated by UAE law, so the percentage, any cap and the release dates are whatever your contract says.
c1a7da040f9128d7: Typically half at handover (the taking-over certificate under FIDIC) and the balance at the end of the defects period, often a year. Keep a dated list of defects and report them in writing well before the period ends.
7f4d3dd701597eae: Why does the busiest month matter?
694565dc9fcf260f: Because it is the month your cash has to be ready. On an S-curve the middle months carry the most work, so the peak payment is well above the average. Plan finance drawdowns and currency transfers around it.
12f3d3d26f4de08f: No. It illustrates a typical schedule. Payment terms, retention, guarantees and their release are contract-specific; take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on your contract.

19f30f4cc739f0a0: The consultant of record carries statutory supervision duties: that the building is built to the approved design and the code. c005de590851801f: In our experience the opposite. Good contractors prefer an informed client: decisions are made on time, information arrives when it should and payments are made promptly for work done. The contractors who dislike scrutiny are the ones you most need it with.
